AUCoFF: Session Summary

AgenticAI Unified Compliance Framework for Fintechs. Specification-driven development and Build Session 1, 18-19 October 2026.

1. Outcome at a glance

Repository: praveendhac/aucoff, branch main. Hand-rolled SDD, no Spec Kit. v1 (MVP) is local-only: built and tested on a laptop with kind; nothing is deployed to AWS. AUCoFF is released under the MIT License (relicensed from AGPL-3.0 on 2026-10-19).

2. What exists in the repository

  • Specifications (10 files, below) with a consistent ID scheme; a cross-reference check (all IDs and links) passes.
  • Backend scaffold: FastAPI with layered packages, /api/v1/health/live and /ready, OpenAPI exported to backend/openapi.yaml (drift check and Spectral lint clean), Python licence gate, 7 tests, ruff and mypy.
  • Frontend scaffold: Next.js (App Router, strict TypeScript, Tailwind), Vitest test, ESLint, Prettier, npm licence gate, production build; LGPL sharp replaced by a stub.
  • Deploy: kind cluster config and a Helm chart skeleton (restricted pod security, ingress, default-deny network policies); helm lint passes.
  • CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) with no deploy job; written but not yet run on GitHub.
  • Repo conventions: README, CLAUDE.md, CODEOWNERS, PR template, Makefile (make check), LICENCES.md register, MIT LICENSE.

4. Key decisions

  • Scope: v1 local-only on kind (minikube not used); AWS, Terraform and EKS are post-v1. Multi-tenant SaaS with operator-provisioned tenants, audited break-glass operator access and time-boxed scoped external auditors.
  • Frameworks (all in v1): PCI DSS v4.0.1, PCI 3DS, SOC 2, ISO 27001:2022, ISO 27701:2025, ISO 20022-1:2026 (Ed. 3), GDPR, DPDP, RBI DPSC and PPI, FFIEC BSA/AML 2026 and IT Handbook, FTC Safeguards, GLBA, NYDFS 500, PSD2, DORA. Versions are owner-supplied and still to be verified (T-005).
  • Stack: Next.js + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + TanStack Query; Python 3.13 FastAPI gateway and agent services over RabbitMQ; LangGraph; PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector 0.8.6 with row-level security; Auth.js + Keycloak; OpenAPI at backend/openapi.yaml with Swagger for every endpoint.
  • AI controls: deterministic checks first (wrapped open-source scanners), advisory-only agents, human approval for consequential actions and anything leaving the tenant, citation validation, redaction before LLM calls, evaluation gates, budgets.
  • History: 12 months visible (stored 13), immutable snapshots, any-to-any scan comparison.
  • Licensing: permissive-only dependencies (LIC-1 to LIC-8); AUCoFF itself is MIT (LIC-9). First-pass audit in LICENCES.md found MinIO (AGPL-3.0, repo archived April 2026), Grafana/Loki/Tempo (AGPLv3), Steampipe (AGPL-3.0), ScoutSuite (GPL-2.0), Semgrep/Opengrep engines (LGPL-2.1), the Semgrep rules licence and current Redis (RSALv2/SSPLv1/AGPLv3) unapproved. Sources are web-search results, to be confirmed from each project's LICENSE file.

GitHub can't do that. A repo path is always `owner/repo`, so `praveendhac/aucoff/specs` can't exist as a repository. These are the closest options:

1. **Separate private repo, with a different name.** For example, `praveendhac/aucoff-specs`, added here as a submodule at `./specs`. The folder is still `specs`, but the repo name differs.
2. **Plain `specs/` folder inside aucoff.** The path would then read `praveendhac/aucoff/specs` on GitHub. It isn't a submodule and isn't a private repo of its own. It would have the same visibility as aucoff.

Which do you want? If it's option 1, tell me the repo name. I'd create it with `gh repo create --private` and then add the submodule.

# Plan: SDD spec templates for AUCoFF

## Context
AUCoFF (AgenticAI Unified Compliance Framework for Fintechs) will be built as a full-stack web app using hand-rolled specification-driven development (no Spec Kit). The repo has only a `specs/.gitkeep`. This step creates nine spec templates in `specs/` that the user fills in and later drives implementation from.

## Decisions (from user)
- Stack: Next.js (React, TypeScript) frontend + FastAPI (Python) backend.
- Infra: local Kubernetes via Helm chart on laptop now; AWS later (templates include an "AWS migration notes" section to update later).
- Detail: structured skeletons with AUCoFF-specific guiding prompts and placeholders (not filled-in content).

## Files to create (all in `specs/`)
1. `constitution.md` - non-negotiable principles: compliance-first, auditability, human-in-the-loop for agents, security/privacy (PII, PCI), testing bar, change/versioning rules.
2. `spec.md` - product spec: vision, problem, personas (compliance officer, auditor, fintech engineer), in-scope frameworks (e.g. PCI DSS, SOC 2, GDPR, RBI/PSD2 placeholders), user stories, functional/non-functional requirements, success metrics, out of scope, open questions.
3. `agent.md` - agentic AI spec: agent roles, tools, orchestration pattern, prompts/guardrails, memory/RAG sources, human approval gates, evaluation, audit logging, failure handling.
4. `design.md` - architecture: system context, components, data model, data flow, security architecture, tech decisions (ADR table), trade-offs.
5. `frontend-spec.md` - Next.js: pages/routes, components, state, auth flow, accessibility, error/loading states, testing.
6. `backend-spec.md` - FastAPI: modules/services, domain models, auth/RBAC, persistence, background jobs, agent integration, logging/observability, testing.
7. `api-contract.md` - conventions (versioning, errors, pagination), endpoint table template, request/response schema stubs, auth scopes, events/webhooks.
8. `infrastructure-spec.md` - local Helm/k8s now (chart layout, values, services, ingress, secrets, local dev workflow), AWS-later section (EKS, RDS, Secrets Manager, etc. as TODO), CI/CD, observability.
9. `tasks.md` - task breakdown: phased checklist with ID, description, owner, spec reference, acceptance criteria, status.

Each file: title, status/version/owner header, purpose line, then sections with `<!-- guiding prompt -->` comments and `TODO` placeholders. Cross-link specs (e.g. tasks reference spec IDs).

## Verification
- `ls specs/` shows all nine files plus `.gitkeep`.
- Each file renders as valid Markdown and has the header block and cross-links.
- Then commit on `main` (user to confirm; do not push).

# Plan: SDD spec templates for AUCoFF

## Context
AUCoFF (AgenticAI Unified Compliance Framework for Fintechs) will be built as a full-stack web app using hand-rolled specification-driven development (no Spec Kit). The repo has only a `specs/.gitkeep`. This step creates nine spec templates in `specs/` that the user fills in and later drives implementation from.

## Decisions (from user)
- Stack: Next.js (React, TypeScript) frontend + FastAPI (Python) backend.
- Infra: local Kubernetes via Helm chart on laptop now; AWS later (templates include an "AWS migration notes" section to update later).
- Detail: structured skeletons with AUCoFF-specific guiding prompts and placeholders (not filled-in content).

## Files to create (all in `specs/`)
1. `constitution.md` - non-negotiable principles: compliance-first, auditability, human-in-the-loop for agents, security/privacy (PII, PCI), testing bar, change/versioning rules.
2. `spec.md` - product spec: vision, problem, personas (compliance officer, auditor, fintech engineer), in-scope frameworks (e.g. PCI DSS, SOC 2, GDPR, RBI/PSD2 placeholders), user stories, functional/non-functional requirements, success metrics, out of scope, open questions.
3. `agent.md` - agentic AI spec: agent roles, tools, orchestration pattern, prompts/guardrails, memory/RAG sources, human approval gates, evaluation, audit logging, failure handling.
4. `design.md` - architecture: system context, components, data model, data flow, security architecture, tech decisions (ADR table), trade-offs.
5. `frontend-spec.md` - Next.js: pages/routes, components, state, auth flow, accessibility, error/loading states, testing.
6. `backend-spec.md` - FastAPI: modules/services, domain models, auth/RBAC, persistence, background jobs, agent integration, logging/observability, testing.
7. `api-contract.md` - conventions (versioning, errors, pagination), endpoint table template, request/response schema stubs, auth scopes, events/webhooks.
8. `infrastructure-spec.md` - local Helm/k8s now (chart layout, values, services, ingress, secrets, local dev workflow), AWS-later section (EKS, RDS, Secrets Manager, etc. as TODO), CI/CD, observability.
9. `tasks.md` - task breakdown: phased checklist with ID, description, owner, spec reference, acceptance criteria, status.

Each file: title, status/version/owner header, purpose line, then sections with `<!-- guiding prompt -->` comments and `TODO` placeholders. Cross-link specs (e.g. tasks reference spec IDs).

# AUCoFF Constitution

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Status | Draft |
| Version | 0.2.0 |
| Owner | Praveen Darshanam |
| Last updated | 2026-10-18 |

> Purpose: the non-negotiable rules every spec, design decision and code change must obey. If another spec conflicts with this file, this file wins. Rules use RFC 2119 keywords: **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD**, **MAY**. Each rule has an ID so specs, tasks and reviews can cite it.

Related: [spec.md](spec.md) · [design.md](design.md) · [agent.md](agent.md) · [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) · [frontend-spec.md](frontend-spec.md) · [infrastructure-spec.md](infrastructure-spec.md) · [tasks.md](tasks.md)

## 1. Mission and Principles

**Mission:** AUCoFF gives fintechs one agentic AI-assisted framework to map, assess and evidence compliance across multiple regulatory frameworks, with every conclusion traceable and every consequential action approved by a human.

| ID | Principle | Meaning |
|----|-----------|---------|
| P1 | Compliance first | A feature that weakens compliance posture or evidence quality is rejected, however useful. |
| P2 | Traceability | Every finding, mapping and agent output traces to source (control ID, evidence, prompt version, model). |
| P3 | Human accountability | Agents advise; humans decide anything consequential. |
| P4 | Secure and private by default | Least privilege, minimal data, encryption everywhere; opt in to exposure, not out. |
| P5 | Simplicity | Prefer the simplest design that meets the spec; complexity needs a recorded reason. |
| P6 | Spec is truth | Behaviour is defined in `specs/`; code follows specs, never the reverse. |

## 2. Architectural Rules

- **ARC-1** The system MUST be a Next.js (TypeScript) frontend and a FastAPI (Python) backend communicating only through the contract in [api-contract.md](api-contract.md).
- **ARC-2** The frontend MUST NOT access databases, the agent runtime, or LLM providers directly.
- **ARC-3** The backend MUST be layered: `api` (routing/validation) -> `domain` (business rules) -> `db`/`agents` (adapters). Lower layers MUST NOT import upper layers.
- **ARC-4** Business and compliance logic MUST live in `domain`, not in routers, UI components, prompts or SQL.
- **ARC-5** All external dependencies (LLM provider, vector store, identity provider, object store) MUST sit behind an interface so they can be swapped (e.g. local to AWS) without domain changes.
- **ARC-6** Multi-tenancy: every persisted record MUST carry a tenant identifier and every query MUST be tenant-scoped.
- **ARC-7** Services MUST be stateless; state lives in the database, queue or object store, so they run unchanged on local Kubernetes and AWS.
- **ARC-8** Configuration MUST come from environment/Helm values (12-factor); no environment-specific values in code.
- **ARC-9** Long-running agent work MUST run asynchronously (queue/worker) with status polling or streaming, never block a request.
- **ARC-10** Significant architectural decisions MUST be recorded as an ADR in [design.md](design.md) before implementation.
- **ARC-11** Infrastructure MUST be declared as code (Helm now, IaC for AWS later); no manual cluster changes.

## 3. Design Philosophy

- **DES-1** Design for audit: model data as append-only where history matters (assessments, approvals, agent runs); corrections are new records, not edits.
- **DES-2** Explicit over implicit: typed schemas, explicit errors, no hidden global state or magic defaults.
- **DES-3** Fail closed: on uncertainty, missing authorisation or invalid agent output, deny or escalate to a human.
- **DES-4** Idempotent operations: retried requests, jobs and agent runs MUST NOT duplicate side effects.
- **DES-5** Small, composable modules with a single responsibility; prefer composition over inheritance.
- **DES-6** Do not build for hypothetical requirements; build what the current spec requires (YAGNI), but keep boundaries (ARC-5) clean.
- **DES-7** Contract first: change [api-contract.md](api-contract.md) before changing endpoints; the OpenAPI output MUST match it.

## 4. Coding Standards

| ID | Rule |
|----|------|
| COD-1 | Python: version pinned in repo; formatted and linted with Ruff; fully type-annotated and checked with mypy (strict for `domain`). |
| COD-2 | TypeScript: `strict` mode on; ESLint + Prettier; no `any` without a justification comment. |
| COD-3 | Names reveal intent; functions do one thing; avoid functions over ~50 lines or deep nesting. |
| COD-4 | Comments explain *why*, not *what*; no commented-out code or untracked TODOs (TODOs MUST reference a task ID from [tasks.md](tasks.md)). |
| COD-5 | Validate all external input at the boundary (Pydantic on the backend, schema validation on the frontend). |
| COD-6 | Errors MUST use the error format in [api-contract.md](api-contract.md); never swallow exceptions silently. |
| COD-7 | Dependencies MUST be pinned via lockfiles, justified, license-checked and kept minimal. |
| COD-8 | Logging MUST be structured (JSON) with a request/correlation ID; MUST NOT log secrets, credentials or PII. |
| COD-9 | Database changes MUST be versioned migrations, reversible where feasible, never edited after merge. |
| COD-10 | Git: small focused commits, imperative messages, branches reviewed via pull request; `main` stays releasable. |

## 5. Quality and Testing Baselines

| ID | Rule |
|----|------|
| QA-1 | Every task has acceptance criteria and is not done until they are verified by a test or a documented manual check. |
| QA-2 | Test pyramid: many unit tests, fewer integration/contract tests, few end-to-end tests. |
| QA-3 | Coverage floor: >= 80% line coverage overall and >= 90% for `domain`; coverage MUST NOT decrease in a PR. (Targets reviewable; see section 10.) |
| QA-4 | Bug fixes MUST include a regression test that fails before the fix. |
| QA-5 | API contract tests MUST confirm backend responses match [api-contract.md](api-contract.md). |
| QA-6 | Agent behaviour MUST be covered by an evaluation suite (see section 7) run in CI; regressions block merge. |
| QA-7 | CI MUST run lint, type checks, tests, dependency and secret scans on every PR; a failing check blocks merge. |
| QA-8 | Tests MUST be deterministic and independent; LLM calls in unit/integration tests are mocked or replayed. |
| QA-9 | Performance and availability targets come from NFRs in [spec.md](spec.md) and are checked before release. |
| QA-10 | Accessibility target: WCAG 2.2 AA for all UI. |
| QA-11 | Definition of done: code reviewed, tests green, spec/docs updated, migrations included, no new scan findings, observability added. |

## 6. Security and Compliance

| ID | Rule |
|----|------|
| SEC-1 | Authentication is required on every endpoint except health checks; authorisation is role-based and enforced server-side (never only in the UI). |
| SEC-2 | Least privilege for users, services, database roles and Kubernetes service accounts. |
| SEC-3 | Secrets MUST NOT be in source control, images, logs or prompts; they come from Kubernetes Secrets locally and a managed secret store on AWS. A pre-commit secret scan (Gitleaks) MUST remain enabled. |
| SEC-4 | Encrypt in transit (TLS) and at rest for all sensitive data. |
| SEC-5 | Data classification: PII, financial and regulated data are classified; the highest class sets handling rules. Collect and retain the minimum needed, with defined retention and deletion. |
| SEC-6 | Cardholder data (PAN, CVV) MUST NOT be stored or processed by AUCoFF; keep the system out of PCI DSS cardholder-data scope. |
| SEC-7 | Follow OWASP ASVS/Top 10: input validation, output encoding, CSRF/XSS/SSRF/injection defences, secure headers, rate limiting. |
| SEC-8 | Containers run as non-root with minimal base images, scanned for vulnerabilities; critical/high findings block release. |
| SEC-9 | Every security-relevant event (login, permission change, approval, data export, agent action) MUST write an immutable audit log entry with actor, time, action, target and outcome. |
| SEC-10 | Audit logs are append-only, tamper-evident and retained per policy (period TODO in [spec.md](spec.md)). |
| SEC-11 | Tenant data MUST NOT cross tenants, including in logs, caches, embeddings and prompts. |
| SEC-12 | A threat model is maintained in [design.md](design.md) and reviewed on significant change. |
| SEC-13 | Regulatory mapping (PCI DSS, SOC 2, GDPR and others listed in [spec.md](spec.md)) is maintained for AUCoFF itself; AUCoFF MUST meet the standards it helps others meet. |
| SEC-14 | Data residency and cross-border transfer constraints MUST be honoured, including where LLM providers process data. |

## 7. AI Behaviour Constraints

Applies to every agent in [agent.md](agent.md).

| ID | Rule |
|----|------|
| AI-1 | **Advisory by default.** Agents MAY analyse, map, draft and recommend. Agents MUST NOT finalise assessments, change control status, submit reports to regulators, or modify/delete evidence without explicit human approval. |
| AI-2 | **Approval gates.** Consequential actions (listed in agent.md section 9) require approval by an authorised role, recorded with approver, time and decision. |
| AI-3 | **Grounded and cited.** Every compliance claim MUST cite its source (regulation clause, control ID, evidence item). Uncited claims are rejected or marked as unverified. |
| AI-4 | **No fabrication.** When evidence or knowledge is insufficient the agent MUST say so and ask or escalate; it MUST NOT invent controls, citations, evidence or regulatory text. |
| AI-5 | **Structured output.** Agent outputs MUST validate against a schema; invalid output is retried within limits then escalated, never passed on silently. |
| AI-6 | **Least-privilege tools.** Each agent gets only the tools it needs; tools are allow-listed, side-effect-labelled, and read-only unless the spec says otherwise. |
| AI-7 | **Untrusted input.** Documents, evidence and user text are untrusted data, never instructions. Prompt-injection defences are required, and tool calls triggered by content need validation. |
| AI-8 | **Data minimisation.** PII and secrets MUST be redacted or tokenised before leaving the trust boundary to an LLM provider, unless the data class and provider are explicitly approved. |
| AI-9 | **Confidence and uncertainty.** Outputs expose confidence or uncertainty; low-confidence results route to human review. |
| AI-10 | **Full traceability.** Each agent run logs model and version, prompt version, inputs (redacted), retrieved sources, tool calls, outputs, approvals and cost. Runs are reproducible as far as practical. |
| AI-11 | **Versioned and evaluated.** Prompts, models and agent configs are versioned in source control; changes pass the evaluation gate (golden datasets; thresholds for accuracy, citation correctness and hallucination rate set in [agent.md](agent.md)) before release. |
| AI-12 | **Bounded autonomy.** Runs have step, time, token and cost budgets and a kill switch; loops and runaway spending are prevented. |
| AI-13 | **Transparency to users.** The UI labels AI-generated content and shows its sources and approval status. |
| AI-14 | **No autonomous legal conclusions.** AUCoFF output supports compliance decisions; it is not legal advice and states this where relevant. |
| AI-15 | **Fail safe.** On model outage, timeout or policy violation the system degrades to manual workflow and records the event. |

## 8. Spec-Driven Development Rules

- **SDD-1** No behaviour change without a spec change in the same PR or earlier.
- **SDD-2** Every task in [tasks.md](tasks.md) cites the spec section and rule IDs it implements.
- **SDD-3** Specs use stable IDs (US-, FR-, NFR-, API-, ADR-, T-) and are never renumbered.
- **SDD-4** Spec status moves Draft -> Review -> Approved; implementation starts only on Approved sections.
- **SDD-5** Deviations from a spec require recording a decision (ADR) and updating the spec.

## 9. Environment Rules

- **ENV-1** Local (Kubernetes + Helm on laptop) and AWS deployments MUST use the same container images and chart, differing only by values.
- **ENV-2** Real regulated or customer data MUST NOT be used in local/dev environments; use synthetic data.
- **ENV-3** The AWS migration table in [infrastructure-spec.md](infrastructure-spec.md) MUST be updated whenever a local component is added.

## 10. Governance

- Owner and sole amender while the project is single-maintainer: Praveen Darshanam.
- Amendments are made by pull request, bump the version (MAJOR: rule removed/relaxed; MINOR: rule added; PATCH: clarification) and add a changelog row.
- Exceptions to a rule require a recorded ADR with rationale, scope and expiry date.
- Thresholds marked reviewable (e.g. QA-3) are revisited at each phase boundary in [tasks.md](tasks.md).

## 11. Open Items
- [ ] Confirm coverage thresholds (QA-3).
- [ ] Define audit log retention period (SEC-10).
- [ ] Choose approved LLM providers and data classes allowed per provider (AI-8, SEC-14).
- [ ] Confirm frameworks in scope for SEC-13.

## 12. Changelog
| Version | Date | Change |
|---------|------|--------|
| 0.1.0 | 2026-10-18 | Initial template |
| 0.2.0 | 2026-10-18 | Added architectural, design, coding, quality, security and AI rules |

Every rule has an ID (e.g. `ARC-4`, `AI-3`) so specs and tasks can cite it. The sections are:

- **Mission and principles (P1–P6):** compliance first, traceability, human accountability, secure by default, simplicity, and "spec is truth".
- **Architectural rules (ARC-1 to 11):**
  - Next.js and FastAPI talk only through the API contract.
  - The backend is layered, with business logic in `domain`.
  - External dependencies sit behind interfaces so you can move from local to AWS.

- **Design philosophy (DES-1 to 7):** append-only audit data, fail closed, idempotency, and contract-first APIs.
- **Coding standards (COD-1 to 10):** Ruff and mypy, strict TypeScript, structured logging with no PII, versioned migrations, and TODOs tied to task IDs.
- **Quality and testing (QA-1 to 11):**
  - Test pyramid and a coverage floor of 80% overall and 90% for `domain`.
  - CI scans that block merges.
  - Agent evaluation suites.
  - WCAG 2.2 AA.
  - A definition of done.
- **Security and compliance (SEC-1 to 14):**
  - Server-side RBAC and secrets handling, keeping the Gitleaks hook.
  - Cardholder data kept out of scope.
  - Immutable audit logs, tenant isolation, and data residency.
- **AI behaviour constraints (AI-1 to 15):**
  - Agents are advisory only and need human approval for consequential actions.
  - Claims must carry citations, with no fabrication.
  - Output is schema-validated and inputs are treated as untrusted, to defend against prompt injection.
  - PII is redacted before it goes to an LLM.
  - Each run is traceable, with budgets and a kill switch.
  - The system falls back to manual workflow when the model fails.
- **SDD rules, environment rules, governance and a changelog.**

# Plan: add database-spec.md and align other specs

## Context
Nine spec files exist in `specs/` (committed and pushed; constitution.md is at v0.2.0). The user wants a new `specs/database-spec.md` (database name, versions, tables, schema, secure configuration, etc.), then all other specs updated to reference it consistently, then commit and push. The user asked to stay in plan mode until they say otherwise.

## Proposed decisions (to confirm)
- Database: PostgreSQL 16 (relational + `pgvector` extension for RAG embeddings, avoiding a separate vector store). Name `aucoff`. Local: in-cluster Postgres via Helm (Bitnami or CloudNativePG, TBD); AWS later: RDS/Aurora PostgreSQL.
- ORM/migrations: SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic (matches backend-spec.md and constitution COD-9).
- Multi-tenancy: `tenant_id` on every table plus Postgres Row-Level Security (constitution ARC-6, SEC-11).
- Audit log: append-only table, no UPDATE/DELETE grants, hash-chained rows (DES-1, SEC-9, SEC-10).

## New file: specs/database-spec.md
Header block (status/version/owner), purpose, related links, then:
1. Engine, name, versions (Postgres 16, pgvector, Alembic, drivers), environments (local vs AWS)
2. Conventions (snake_case, UUID v7 PKs, `tenant_id`, `created_at/updated_at`, soft-delete policy, timestamps in UTC)
3. Schemas and tables: tenants, users, roles, user_roles, frameworks, controls, control_mappings, evidence, assessments, findings, agent_runs, agent_steps, approvals, embeddings (pgvector), audit_log. Per table: columns, types, constraints, indexes, FKs, RLS
4. ER diagram (Mermaid)
5. Migrations (Alembic workflow, naming, rollback, never edit merged)
6. Secure configuration: TLS required, scram-sha-256, least-privilege roles (migrator/app/readonly/audit-writer), RLS, encryption at rest, column-level encryption for sensitive fields, secrets via k8s Secrets then Secrets Manager, network policy, pg_audit logging, no PAN/CVV (SEC-6)
7. Data classification, retention and deletion (SEC-5, SEC-10)
8. Backup/restore and DR (RPO/RTO TODO)
9. Performance (indexes, pooling via PgBouncer, partitioning of audit_log/agent_runs)
10. Local Helm deployment notes and AWS migration notes
11. Testing (migration tests, RLS tests, seed with synthetic data only, ENV-2)
12. Open questions

## Updates to other specs (consistency edits)
- `design.md`: replace generic DB/vector-store rows with PostgreSQL + pgvector; link data model to database-spec.md; add ADR for Postgres+pgvector.
- `backend-spec.md`: fill DB choice, ORM/migrations; link database-spec.md in Related and section 4.
- `infrastructure-spec.md`: Postgres in Helm chart (stateful set/operator, PVC, secrets), AWS row RDS/Aurora; link.
- `agent.md`: vector store = pgvector; link for embeddings and agent_runs tables.
- `api-contract.md`: note IDs are UUIDs and tenant scoping; link.
- `spec.md`: reference data retention NFR to database-spec.md.
- `constitution.md`: add database rules (DB-1..n: RLS, migrations only, least-privilege roles, append-only audit) and bump to 0.3.0 with changelog; add Related link.
- `tasks.md`: add DB tasks (schema, migrations, RLS, seed, backup) in Phase 1/4.
- `frontend-spec.md`: minimal; add link only if needed (UUID id handling).

## Execution (after approval)
1. Write database-spec.md; apply edits above.
2. `git add specs`, commit with Co-Authored-By trailer, `git pull --rebase origin main`, `git push origin main`.

## Verification
- `ls specs/` shows ten spec files.
- Grep: every spec mentions `database-spec.md` where relevant; no stale "vector store TODO" contradictions.
- Mermaid and tables render; IDs unique; `git status` clean and `git log origin/main` shows the push.

# Plan: add database-spec.md and align other specs

## Context
Nine spec files exist in `specs/` (committed and pushed; constitution.md is at v0.2.0). The user wants a new `specs/database-spec.md` (database name, versions, tables, schema, secure configuration, etc.), then all other specs updated to reference it consistently, then commit and push. The user asked to stay in plan mode until they say otherwise.

## Proposed decisions (to confirm)
- Database: PostgreSQL 18.6 (confirmed by user; relational + `pgvector` extension for RAG embeddings, avoiding a separate vector store). Pin the exact pgvector version and verify it supports PG 18 when writing the spec. AWS RDS/Aurora support for 18.x TBD in AWS migration notes. Name `aucoff`. Local: in-cluster Postgres via Helm (Bitnami or CloudNativePG, TBD); AWS later: RDS/Aurora PostgreSQL.
- ORM/migrations: SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic (matches backend-spec.md and constitution COD-9).
- Multi-tenancy: `tenant_id` on every table plus Postgres Row-Level Security (constitution ARC-6, SEC-11).
- Audit log: append-only table, no UPDATE/DELETE grants, hash-chained rows (DES-1, SEC-9, SEC-10).

## New file: specs/database-spec.md
Header block (status/version/owner), purpose, related links, then:
1. Engine, name, versions (Postgres 18.6, pgvector, Alembic, drivers), environments (local vs AWS)
2. Conventions (snake_case, UUID v7 PKs, `tenant_id`, `created_at/updated_at`, soft-delete policy, timestamps in UTC)
3. Schemas and tables: tenants, users, roles, user_roles, frameworks, controls, control_mappings, evidence, assessments, findings, agent_runs, agent_steps, approvals, embeddings (pgvector), audit_log. Per table: columns, types, constraints, indexes, FKs, RLS
4. ER diagram (Mermaid)
5. Migrations (Alembic workflow, naming, rollback, never edit merged)
6. Secure configuration: TLS required, scram-sha-256, least-privilege roles (migrator/app/readonly/audit-writer), RLS, encryption at rest, column-level encryption for sensitive fields, secrets via k8s Secrets then Secrets Manager, network policy, pg_audit logging, no PAN/CVV (SEC-6)
7. Data classification, retention and deletion (SEC-5, SEC-10)
8. Backup/restore and DR (RPO/RTO TODO)
9. Performance (indexes, pooling via PgBouncer, partitioning of audit_log/agent_runs)
10. Local Helm deployment notes and AWS migration notes
11. Testing (migration tests, RLS tests, seed with synthetic data only, ENV-2)
12. Open questions

## Updates to other specs (consistency edits)
- `design.md`: replace generic DB/vector-store rows with PostgreSQL + pgvector; link data model to database-spec.md; add ADR for Postgres+pgvector.
- `backend-spec.md`: fill DB choice, ORM/migrations; link database-spec.md in Related and section 4.
- `infrastructure-spec.md`: Postgres in Helm chart (stateful set/operator, PVC, secrets), AWS row RDS/Aurora; link.
- `agent.md`: vector store = pgvector; link for embeddings and agent_runs tables.
- `api-contract.md`: note IDs are UUIDs and tenant scoping; link.
- `spec.md`: reference data retention NFR to database-spec.md.
- `constitution.md`: add database rules (DB-1..n: RLS, migrations only, least-privilege roles, append-only audit) and bump to 0.3.0 with changelog; add Related link.
- `tasks.md`: add DB tasks (schema, migrations, RLS, seed, backup) in Phase 1/4.
- `frontend-spec.md`: minimal; add link only if needed (UUID id handling).

## Execution (after approval)
1. Write database-spec.md; apply edits above.
2. `git add specs`, commit with Co-Authored-By trailer, `git pull --rebase origin main`, `git push origin main`.

- LLM: provider-agnostic cloud API, Anthropic Claude default.
- Autonomy: read-only scanning; remediation advisory only.
- NFRs: availability (99.9% proposed), scan latency/scale, data retention and residency, LLM cost per assessment, no OWASP Top 10 web/API vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10 + API Security Top 10 as acceptance gate).
- Success metrics: time to audit readiness, control coverage %, agent accuracy/citation correctness, finding remediation cycle time.
- Release plan: all listed frameworks in v1 (large scope; record as top risk, suggest internal milestones in tasks.md).
- spec.md edits: replace TODO placeholders with the above; add sections for integrations, evidence sources, tenancy, autonomy boundaries, microservice list (scanner services), risks; keep numbered IDs (PER-, US-, FR-, NFR-); leave numeric targets not given by the user as marked proposals/open questions. Align with constitution (AI-1, SEC-6, SEC-14).
- Constitution touch-up: SEC-13 framework list and open item "Confirm frameworks in scope" resolved.

- `ls specs/` shows ten spec files.
- Grep: every spec mentions `database-spec.md` where relevant; no stale "vector store TODO" contradictions.
- Mermaid and tables render; IDs unique; `git status` clean and `git log origin/main` shows the push.

# AUCoFF Database Spec

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Status | Draft |
| Version | 0.1.0 |
| Owner | Praveen Darshanam |
| Last updated | 2026-10-18 |

> Purpose: the database engine, schema, migrations and secure configuration for AUCoFF. Implements constitution rules ARC-6, DES-1, COD-9, SEC-2 to SEC-5, SEC-9 to SEC-11 and DB-1 to DB-8.

Related: [constitution.md](constitution.md) · [design.md](design.md) · [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) · [agent.md](agent.md) · [infrastructure-spec.md](infrastructure-spec.md) · [api-contract.md](api-contract.md)

## 1. Engine, Name and Versions
| Item | Value | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|
| Engine | PostgreSQL 18.6 | Confirmed by owner |
| Database name | `aucoff` | One database; tenant isolation by `tenant_id` + RLS |
| Vector extension | `pgvector` (version TODO) | Verify the pinned release supports PostgreSQL 18 before adoption |
| Other extensions | `pgcrypto`, `pg_audit` (TODO confirm availability locally and on AWS), `pg_stat_statements` | |
| ORM | SQLAlchemy 2.x (async) | See [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) |
| Migrations | Alembic | Versioned, forward-only in prod (COD-9) |
| Driver | `asyncpg` (TODO confirm) | |
| Pooling | PgBouncer (TODO decide local vs AWS RDS Proxy) | |

### Environments
| Env | Deployment | Notes |
|-----|-----------|-------|
| local | PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector in the Helm chart (StatefulSet or operator such as CloudNativePG - TODO decide), PVC storage | Synthetic data only (ENV-2) |
| aws (future) | RDS or Aurora PostgreSQL | Confirm 18.x and `pgvector` support at migration time; see section 12 |

## 2. Conventions
- Names: `snake_case`; tables plural; one schema `app` for domain tables, `audit` for the audit log, `ref` for reference data (frameworks, controls).
- Primary keys: UUID v7 (time-ordered), column `id`. (PostgreSQL 18 provides `uuidv7()` natively - verify.)
- Every tenant-owned table has `tenant_id uuid NOT NULL` (ARC-6).
- Timestamps: `timestamptz` in UTC; `created_at`, `updated_at` on mutable tables.
- Append-only tables (DES-1): no `updated_at`; changes are new rows.
- Deletion: soft delete (`deleted_at`) for user-facing entities; hard delete only via the retention job (section 9).
- Enums: PostgreSQL `CHECK` constraints on text columns or lookup tables (avoid native enum types so migrations stay simple).
- JSON: `jsonb` only for flexible payloads (evidence metadata, agent step I/O); core fields are columns.
- Money/scores: `numeric`, never float, where precision matters.

## 3. Tables

### 3.1 Tenancy and identity (`app`)
| Table | Purpose | Key columns |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `tenants` | Customer organisation | `id`, `name`, `slug` (unique), `region` (data residency), `status`, `created_at` |
| `users` | People | `id`, `tenant_id`, `email` (unique per tenant), `display_name`, `idp_subject`, `status`, `last_login_at` |
| `roles` | Role definitions | `id`, `name` (compliance_officer, auditor, engineer, executive, ciso, admin), `permissions jsonb` |
| `user_roles` | Role assignment | `tenant_id`, `user_id`, `role_id` (PK on the three) |
| `integrations` | SSO, ticketing, notification, SaaS connectors | `id`, `tenant_id`, `type`, `config_ref` (secret reference, never the secret), `status` |

### 3.2 Reference and unified controls (`ref`, shared across tenants, read-only to the app role)
| Table | Purpose | Key columns |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `frameworks` | Regulation/standard | `id`, `code` (e.g. `pci_dss_4_0_1`), `name`, `version`, `jurisdiction`, `type` (framework, regulation, messaging-standard) |
| `framework_requirements` | Clause-level requirement | `id`, `framework_id`, `ref` (clause number), `title`, `text`, unique(`framework_id`, `ref`) |
| `unified_controls` | Normalised AUCoFF control | `id`, `code`, `title`, `description`, `domain` |
| `control_mappings` | Requirement to unified control | `requirement_id`, `unified_control_id`, `strength`, `rationale`, `source` (human/agent), `approved_by`, `approved_at` |

### 3.3 Assessments (`app`)
| Table | Purpose | Key columns |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `scopes` | What is assessed (systems, frameworks) | `id`, `tenant_id`, `name`, `framework_ids uuid[]`, `target_refs jsonb` |
| `evidence` | Collected artefact metadata | `id`, `tenant_id`, `scope_id`, `source_type` (cloud, k8s, repo, document, saas), `source_ref`, `object_key` (object store), `sha256`, `collected_at`, `classification` |
| `assessments` | One assessment run set | `id`, `tenant_id`, `scope_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `created_by` |
| `control_results` | Result per unified control | `id`, `tenant_id`, `assessment_id`, `unified_control_id`, `status` (pass, fail, partial, not_applicable, unknown), `confidence`, `summary`, `agent_run_id`, `reviewed_by`, `reviewed_at` |
| `result_evidence` | Links results to evidence with citations | `control_result_id`, `evidence_id`, `citation` |
| `findings` | Gaps | `id`, `tenant_id`, `control_result_id`, `severity`, `title`, `description`, `recommendation`, `status`, `ticket_ref`, `opened_at`, `closed_at` |
| `reports` | Generated audit reports | `id`, `tenant_id`, `assessment_id`, `format`, `object_key`, `sha256`, `generated_by`, `generated_at` |

### 3.4 Agents and approvals (`app`)
| Table | Purpose | Key columns |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `agent_runs` | One agent execution | `id`, `tenant_id`, `agent_id`, `assessment_id`, `model`, `model_version`, `prompt_version`, `status`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cost_usd numeric`, `started_at`, `finished_at` |
| `agent_steps` | Tool calls and outputs (append-only) | `id`, `tenant_id`, `agent_run_id`, `seq`, `kind`, `input_redacted jsonb`, `output jsonb`, `created_at` |
| `approvals` | Human decisions on agent actions | `id`, `tenant_id`, `agent_run_id`, `action`, `requested_at`, `decided_by`, `decision`, `decided_at`, `comment` |
| `embeddings` | RAG vectors | `id`, `tenant_id` (NULL for shared reference text), `source_type`, `source_id`, `chunk_index`, `content`, `embedding vector(N)` (N depends on embedding model - TODO), `model` |

### 3.5 Audit (`audit`)
| Table | Purpose | Key columns |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `audit_log` | Immutable security/compliance events (SEC-9) | `id`, `tenant_id`, `occurred_at`, `actor_type`, `actor_id`, `action`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `outcome`, `request_id`, `details jsonb`, `prev_hash`, `row_hash` |

`row_hash = sha256(prev_hash || canonical row)` per tenant, giving tamper evidence (SEC-10).

## 4. Relationships (ER overview)
```mermaid
erDiagram
  tenants ||--o{ users : has
  users ||--o{ user_roles : assigned
  roles ||--o{ user_roles : grants
  frameworks ||--o{ framework_requirements : contains
  framework_requirements ||--o{ control_mappings : maps
  unified_controls ||--o{ control_mappings : maps
  tenants ||--o{ scopes : owns
  scopes ||--o{ evidence : collects
  scopes ||--o{ assessments : assessed_in
  assessments ||--o{ control_results : produces
  unified_controls ||--o{ control_results : evaluated
  control_results ||--o{ result_evidence : cites
  evidence ||--o{ result_evidence : cited_by
  control_results ||--o{ findings : raises
  assessments ||--o{ reports : yields
  assessments ||--o{ agent_runs : triggers
  agent_runs ||--o{ agent_steps : records
  agent_runs ||--o{ approvals : requests
  tenants ||--o{ audit_log : logs
```

## 5. Indexes and Constraints
- B-tree on (`tenant_id`, `id`) for every tenant table; foreign keys always include `tenant_id` where the parent is tenant-owned (composite FK) so cross-tenant links are impossible.
- `control_results`: unique (`assessment_id`, `unified_control_id`); index on (`tenant_id`, `status`).
- `findings`: index on (`tenant_id`, `status`, `severity`).
- `embeddings`: HNSW index on `embedding` (cosine), plus (`tenant_id`, `source_type`, `source_id`). Tenant filter MUST be applied in every similarity query.
- `audit_log`: index on (`tenant_id`, `occurred_at`) and (`tenant_id`, `target_type`, `target_id`); partition by month on `occurred_at`.
- `agent_runs` / `agent_steps`: partition by month once volume warrants (threshold TODO).
- CHECK constraints for status/severity vocabularies; NOT NULL by default.

## 6. Secure Configuration

### 6.1 Roles and privileges (SEC-2)
| DB role | Used by | Privileges |
|---------|---------|------------|
| `aucoff_owner` | Nobody at runtime | Owns objects; no login in prod |
| `aucoff_migrator` | Alembic job | DDL on `app`, `ref`, `audit`; used only during deploy |
| `aucoff_app` | API and workers | DML on `app`; `SELECT` on `ref`; `INSERT`-only on `audit.audit_log`; no DDL; subject to RLS |
| `aucoff_readonly` | Reporting/support | `SELECT` on `app` (subject to RLS); no PII columns where avoidable |
| `aucoff_audit_reader` | Auditor export | `SELECT` on `audit.audit_log` |

No role is superuser; `aucoff_app` has `NOBYPASSRLS`.

### 6.2 Row-Level Security (SEC-11, ARC-6)
- RLS enabled and FORCED on every tenant table.
- Policy: `tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid`; the API sets `SET LOCAL app.tenant_id` per transaction from the authenticated token. Missing setting = no rows (fail closed, DES-3).
- Shared reference tables carry no tenant data and are read-only.
- RLS tests are mandatory (section 10).

### 6.3 Authentication and transport
- `scram-sha-256` password auth only; no `trust` or `md5`.
- TLS required (`hostssl` only), TLS 1.2+ ; certificates managed by the platform (cert-manager locally, ACM/RDS CA on AWS).
- Credentials come from Kubernetes Secrets locally and AWS Secrets Manager later; never in images, values files in git, logs or prompts (SEC-3). Rotation procedure TODO.

### 6.4 Encryption
- At rest: encrypted volumes locally where available; KMS-encrypted storage on AWS.
- Column-level: sensitive fields (e.g. integration tokens if stored, evidence classified restricted) encrypted with an application-managed key (`pgcrypto` or app-side envelope encryption, TODO decide). Prefer storing only secret references (`config_ref`).
- Backups encrypted.

### 6.5 Network and hardening
- Database reachable only from backend/worker pods (Kubernetes NetworkPolicy); not exposed via Ingress or NodePort.
- Run as non-root; read-only root filesystem where supported; resource limits set.
- `log_connections`, `log_disconnections`, `log_statement = ddl`; `pg_audit` for role/DDL events (TODO); logs exclude bind values to avoid leaking PII.
- `statement_timeout`, `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` and `lock_timeout` set for `aucoff_app`.
- Public schema privileges revoked; `search_path` fixed per role.
- Cardholder data (PAN, CVV) MUST NOT be stored (SEC-6); an automated check scans schema and sampled data for PAN patterns.

## 7. Migrations (COD-9)
- Alembic revisions in `backend/app/db/migrations/`; one logical change per revision; names `YYYYMMDD_HHMM_short_description`.
- Never edit a merged revision; fix forward.
- Destructive changes use expand/contract in separate releases.
- Migrations run as `aucoff_migrator` in a Helm pre-upgrade hook Job locally; CI job on AWS.
- Every migration is tested on an empty DB and on the previous release's schema in CI.
- Row-Level Security, grants and extensions are managed in migrations, not by hand.

## 8. Data Classification
| Class | Examples | Handling |
|-------|----------|----------|
| Restricted | Evidence content, credentials references, audit details | Encrypted, access logged, tenant-scoped, minimal retention |
| Confidential | User identity, findings, reports | Encrypted, RBAC |
| Internal | Agent runs metadata, costs | RBAC |
| Public/reference | Framework text (if licensed for use), unified controls | Read-only; check licensing of standard texts (TODO) |

## 9. Retention, Deletion and Residency (SEC-5, SEC-10, SEC-14)
| Data | Retention | Deletion |
|------|-----------|----------|
| Audit log | TODO (proposal: 7 years) | Never edited; partitions dropped only after retention |
| Evidence and reports | TODO per tenant policy | Object + metadata deletion job, logged |
| Agent steps | TODO (proposal: 13 months) | Partition drop |
| User data | Account life + TODO | Erasure on request (GDPR/DPDP) with audit-log pseudonymisation |
- Each tenant has a `region`; tenant data MUST reside only in that region's database/storage (deployment-per-region model TODO in [design.md](design.md)).

## 10. Testing
- Migration tests: up from empty, up from previous version, downgrade where supported.
- RLS tests: for every tenant table, a session with tenant A cannot read or write tenant B and sees nothing when `app.tenant_id` is unset.
- Privilege tests: `aucoff_app` cannot `UPDATE`/`DELETE` `audit_log`, cannot DDL.
- Audit hash chain verification test.
- Embedding queries always include tenant filter (test with two tenants).
- Seed data: synthetic only (ENV-2).

## 11. Backup, Restore and DR
- Local: scheduled `pg_dump`/volume snapshot for developer convenience (TODO).
- AWS: automated backups plus PITR; RPO/RTO targets TODO (proposal: RPO 15 min, RTO 4 h).
- Restore drills documented and rehearsed per phase.

## 12. AWS Migration Notes (future)
| Local | AWS | Notes |
|-------|-----|-------|
| In-cluster PostgreSQL 18.6 | RDS/Aurora PostgreSQL | Confirm 18.x availability; `pgvector` and `pg_audit` support per engine version |
| PgBouncer | RDS Proxy or PgBouncer | TODO |
| K8s Secret credentials | Secrets Manager with rotation | IAM auth optional |
| cert-manager TLS | RDS CA bundle | |
| PVC storage | gp3/io2 with KMS | |

## 13. Open Questions
- [ ] Exact pgvector version and embedding dimension (depends on embedding model).
- [ ] Local deployment: plain StatefulSet vs CloudNativePG operator.
- [ ] Column-level encryption approach and key management.
- [ ] Retention periods and RPO/RTO targets.
- [ ] Tenant region model: one database per region vs per tenant.
- [ ] Licensing for storing framework text (PCI DSS, ISO standards are copyrighted).

# AUCoFF Product Spec

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Status | Draft |
| Version | 0.2.0 |
| Owner | Praveen Darshanam |
| Last updated | 2026-10-18 |

> Purpose: what AUCoFF (AgenticAI Unified Compliance Framework for Fintechs) must do and why. Describes behaviour, not implementation. Items marked *(proposal)* are suggested values awaiting owner confirmation.

Related: [constitution.md](constitution.md) · [agent.md](agent.md) · [design.md](design.md) · [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) · [api-contract.md](api-contract.md) · [tasks.md](tasks.md)

## 1. Vision
A multi-tenant SaaS in which agentic AI microservices read-only scan a fintech's cloud, Kubernetes, code, SaaS tools and documents, assess them against one unified control set mapped to many regulations and standards, and produce cited findings, remediation guidance and audit-ready reports, with humans approving every consequential outcome.

## 2. Problem Statement
Fintechs must satisfy many overlapping frameworks and regional regulations at once (payments, data protection, financial crime, operational resilience). Teams repeat the same evidence collection per framework, controls are tracked in spreadsheets, audits are slow and costly, and posture drifts between audits. AUCoFF unifies controls, automates evidence collection and analysis, and keeps compliance continuously assessable.

## 3. Personas
| ID | Persona | Goals | Pain points |
|----|---------|-------|-------------|
| PER-1 | Compliance officer | Maintain control mappings, run assessments, approve agent conclusions, prepare for audits | Duplicate work across frameworks, manual evidence chasing |
| PER-2 | Internal / external auditor | Review evidence, findings and the audit trail with confidence | Unverifiable evidence, no traceability |
| PER-3 | Fintech engineer / security team | Understand gaps in their systems and fix them | Vague findings, no technical remediation steps |
| PER-4 | Executive / risk owner | See posture, risk trends and readiness at a glance | No consolidated view |
| PER-5 | CISO | Own security and compliance posture; approve risk acceptance; report to board and regulators | Fragmented tooling, audit surprises |
| PER-6 | Platform admin (tenant admin) | Manage users, roles, SSO, integrations | Manual onboarding |

## 4. Frameworks and Regulations in Scope (all in v1)
| Framework | Version | Jurisdiction | Type | Notes |
|-----------|---------|--------------|------|-------|
| PCI DSS | v4.0.1 | Global | Standard | AUCoFF itself stays out of cardholder-data scope (SEC-6) |
| PCI 3DS | TODO version | Global | Standard | 3-D Secure core security requirements |
| SOC 2 | Trust Services Criteria (TODO year) | Global | Attestation framework | |
| ISO/IEC 27001 | 2022 | Global | Standard | |
| ISO/IEC 27701 | 2025 | Global | Standard | Privacy management extension |
| ISO 20022 | TODO | Global | Messaging standard | Scoped as data-format / message-handling controls, not a control framework |
| GDPR | EU 2016/679 | EU | Regulation | |
| DPDP | Act 2023, 2025 rules (TODO confirm) | India | Regulation | |
| RBI DPSC | TODO exact instrument | India | Regulation | Digital payment security controls |
| RBI PPI | TODO exact instrument | India | Regulation | Prepaid payment instruments |
| FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual | TODO edition | US | Examination guidance | |
| FTC Safeguards Rule | 16 CFR Part 314 | US | Regulation | |
| GLBA | TODO | US | Regulation | |
| NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500 | TODO | US | Regulation | |
| PSD2 | TODO | EU | Regulation | |
| DORA | EU 2022/2554 | EU | Regulation | |

Licensing note: standard texts (PCI DSS, ISO) are copyrighted; how they are stored and displayed is an open question (see [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) section 13).

## 5. Scope Overview
### 5.1 Core capabilities
1. **Unified control mapping** - one AUCoFF control set mapped to all in-scope framework requirements.
2. **Evidence collection and analysis** - read-only collection from connected sources plus uploaded documents; agent analysis.
3. **Gap analysis and remediation** - control results, findings with severity, advisory remediation guidance, ticket creation.
4. **Audit-ready reporting** - exportable reports and evidence packs with citations and approval records.

### 5.2 Evidence sources
| Category | Sources |
|----------|---------|
| Cloud configuration | AWS, GCP, Azure (read-only APIs) |
| Kubernetes / containers | Cluster manifests, Helm values, RBAC, image scan results |
| Code and CI/CD | GitHub, Bitbucket (branch protection, secrets scanning, pipelines, dependency/SAST results) |
| Identity and SaaS | Microsoft Entra ID, Metabase |
| Documents | Uploaded policies, SOPs, reports (PDF, DOCX) |

### 5.3 Integrations
| Type | Systems |
|------|---------|
| Single sign-on | OIDC, SAML |
| Ticketing | Jira, ServiceNow |
| Notifications | Email, Slack, Microsoft Teams |

### 5.4 Tenancy
Multi-tenant SaaS. Strict tenant isolation (see [database-spec.md](database-spec.md), constitution ARC-6, SEC-11). Per-tenant data region.

### 5.5 Autonomy boundaries
Scanning is **read-only**. Agents never change customer systems. Remediation is advisory: agents recommend, humans apply fixes. Consequential outcomes (finalising a control result, accepting risk, publishing a report) require human approval (constitution AI-1, AI-2).

### 5.6 Agentic microservices (v1)
Python microservices coordinated by the backend (see [agent.md](agent.md)); names are proposals.
| Service | Responsibility |
|---------|----------------|
| `mapping-agent` | Maintain and propose mappings between framework requirements and unified controls |
| `cloud-scanner` | Read AWS/GCP/Azure configuration and verify against controls |
| `k8s-scanner` | Verify Kubernetes and container configuration |
| `repo-scanner` | Verify GitHub/Bitbucket and CI/CD settings |
| `saas-scanner` | Verify Entra ID and Metabase configuration |
| `document-analyzer` | Extract and assess evidence from uploaded documents (RAG) |
| `assessment-orchestrator` | Plan and coordinate runs, aggregate control results |
| `remediation-advisor` | Draft findings and remediation guidance |
| `report-generator` | Build cited reports and evidence packs |

## 6. User Stories
| ID | Story | Acceptance criteria | Priority |
|----|-------|---------------------|----------|
| US-1 | As a compliance officer, I want one unified control set mapped to all in-scope frameworks so that I assess once and satisfy many | Each requirement maps to >= 1 unified control; mappings show rationale and approval status | P0 |
| US-2 | As a compliance officer, I want to define an assessment scope (systems and frameworks) so that scans are targeted | Scope saved and used by every scanner in the run | P0 |
| US-3 | As a fintech engineer, I want to connect cloud, Kubernetes, repo and SaaS sources read-only so that evidence is collected automatically | Connection tests pass; only read permissions requested | P0 |
| US-4 | As a compliance officer, I want to upload policy documents so that process controls are assessed | Documents indexed per tenant; analysis cites document passages | P0 |
| US-5 | As a compliance officer, I want agent-generated control results with citations so that I can review and approve them | Every result has status, confidence and evidence citations; approval recorded | P0 |
| US-6 | As an engineer, I want findings with clear remediation steps so that I can fix gaps | Findings include severity, affected resource, steps; can be pushed to Jira/ServiceNow | P0 |
| US-7 | As an auditor, I want to view evidence, results and the immutable audit trail so that I can verify conclusions | Read-only role; tamper-evidence check available | P0 |
| US-8 | As a CISO / executive, I want a posture dashboard by framework so that I see readiness and trends | Coverage %, open findings, trend over time per framework | P1 |
| US-9 | As a compliance officer, I want audit-ready reports per framework so that audits are quicker | Export (PDF and structured) with citations and approvals | P0 |
| US-10 | As a tenant admin, I want SSO and role assignment so that access is controlled | OIDC/SAML login; roles from [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) | P0 |
| US-11 | As a CISO, I want notifications in Slack/Teams/email for findings and approvals so that nothing is missed | Configurable per event type | P1 |
| US-12 | As a compliance officer, I want continuous/scheduled assessments so that drift is detected | Schedules per scope; changes flagged | P1 |
| US-13 | As a CISO, I want to see regional regulation coverage (RBI, DPDP, GDPR, PSD2, DORA, NYDFS) so that I know jurisdictional gaps | Filter results by jurisdiction | P1 |

## 7. Functional Requirements
| ID | Requirement | Traces to |
|----|-------------|-----------|
| FR-1 | Maintain framework, requirement and unified-control catalogues with versioning | US-1 |
| FR-2 | Propose and record requirement-to-control mappings; mappings require human approval | US-1 |
| FR-3 | Manage scopes and scheduled/on-demand assessments | US-2, US-12 |
| FR-4 | Connector management for cloud, Kubernetes, repo, SaaS sources with read-only credentials | US-3 |
| FR-5 | Document upload, storage, chunking and embedding per tenant | US-4 |
| FR-6 | Scanner microservices collect evidence and store it with hash and provenance | US-3 |
| FR-7 | Agents produce control results with status, confidence and citations; reviewer approves, rejects or edits | US-5 |
| FR-8 | Findings lifecycle (open, accepted risk, in progress, resolved) with severity | US-6 |
| FR-9 | Ticket creation and status sync with Jira and ServiceNow | US-6 |
| FR-10 | Immutable audit log of security-relevant events | US-7 |
| FR-11 | Dashboards by framework, jurisdiction and time | US-8, US-13 |
| FR-12 | Report generation and export with citations and approval history | US-9 |
| FR-13 | OIDC/SAML SSO, RBAC, tenant admin | US-10 |
| FR-14 | Notifications via email, Slack, Microsoft Teams | US-11 |
| FR-15 | Agent run tracing: model, prompt version, tools, cost | constitution AI-10 |

## 8. Non-Functional Requirements
| ID | Category | Requirement |
|----|----------|-------------|
| NFR-1 | Security | No OWASP Top 10 (web) or OWASP API Security Top 10 vulnerabilities; verified by SAST, DAST and API testing before each release; high/critical findings block release |
| NFR-2 | Security | Meet constitution section 6 (SEC-1 to SEC-14) |
| NFR-3 | Availability | 99.9% monthly API availability *(proposal)*; scans degrade gracefully when providers fail |
| NFR-4 | Performance | API p95 < 500 ms for non-agent calls *(proposal)* |
| NFR-5 | Scan latency and scale | Single-scope assessment completes within TODO (proposal: 30 min for 1,000 resources); N concurrent assessments per tenant TODO; evidence volume per tenant TODO |
| NFR-6 | Data retention | Per [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) section 9; configurable per tenant within regulatory minimums |
| NFR-7 | Data residency | Tenant data stays in its configured region, including LLM processing where required (SEC-14) |
| NFR-8 | Cost | LLM budget per assessment and per tenant per month, enforced with alerts and hard stops (AI-12); numbers TODO |
| NFR-9 | Auditability | Every agent action and approval reproducible from logs (AI-10) |
| NFR-10 | Accessibility | WCAG 2.2 AA |
| NFR-11 | Privacy | PII redacted before LLM calls (AI-8); GDPR/DPDP erasure supported |
| NFR-12 | Portability | Same images and Helm chart for local Kubernetes and AWS (ENV-1) |

## 9. LLM Approach
Provider-agnostic cloud LLM API behind an interface (ARC-5), with Anthropic Claude as the default provider. Approved providers and data classes allowed per provider remain to be decided (constitution open items).

## 10. Success Metrics
| Metric | Definition | Target |
|--------|-----------|--------|
| Time to audit readiness | Time from scope definition to an approved audit-ready report | TODO (proposal: -50% vs baseline) |
| Control coverage % | Unified controls with approved result and evidence / in-scope controls | TODO (proposal: >= 90% automated or evidenced) |
| Agent accuracy | Agreement with human reviewers on golden dataset | TODO |
| Citation correctness | % of claims with valid, verifiable citations | TODO (proposal: >= 98%) |
| Finding remediation cycle time | Median time from finding opened to resolved | TODO |

## 11. Out of Scope (v1)
- Automated remediation or any write access to customer systems.
- Storing or processing cardholder data (PAN, CVV).
- Legal advice or regulator filings submitted automatically.
- Frameworks not listed in section 4.

## 12. Assumptions, Risks, Dependencies
| ID | Item | Mitigation |
|----|------|-----------|
| R-1 | **Scope risk:** all listed frameworks in v1 is very large | Phase delivery in [tasks.md](tasks.md) by internal milestones; reuse unified controls to share effort |
| R-2 | Licensing of standard texts | Legal review; store references/summaries rather than full text where required |
| R-3 | LLM hallucination in compliance conclusions | Constitution AI rules, citations, approval gates, evaluation suite |
| R-4 | Customer credentials for scanning are high-value targets | Read-only, scoped, short-lived credentials; secrets management (SEC-3) |
| R-5 | Data residency vs LLM provider region | Region-pinned deployments or approved providers (SEC-14) |
| R-6 | Regulation texts change | Versioned catalogues; mapping review process |
| D-1 | Dependencies | LLM provider, identity providers, Jira/ServiceNow, cloud and SaaS APIs |

## 13. Open Questions
- [ ] Exact versions/instruments for PCI 3DS, SOC 2 TSC, RBI DPSC, RBI PPI, DPDP rules, FFIEC edition, GLBA, NYDFS, PSD2.
- [ ] How ISO 20022 translates into assessable controls.
- [ ] Numeric targets for NFR-3, NFR-4, NFR-5, NFR-8 and section 10 metrics.
- [ ] Order of delivery of frameworks within v1 (internal milestones).
- [ ] Report formats and templates per framework.
- [ ] Pricing/tenant plan limits (if any) affecting quotas.
- [ ] Which cloud providers and SaaS scanners ship first.

## 7a. Database Rules

Detail in [database-spec.md](database-spec.md).

| ID | Rule |
|----|------|
| DB-1 | The database is PostgreSQL 18.6 with `pgvector`; versions are pinned and changed only via spec update. |
| DB-2 | Schema changes MUST be made only through versioned Alembic migrations (COD-9). |
| DB-3 | Every tenant table MUST have `tenant_id` and enforced Row-Level Security; the application role MUST NOT bypass RLS. |
| DB-4 | Application roles are least-privilege: no superuser, no DDL at runtime, `INSERT`-only on the audit log. |
| DB-5 | Connections MUST use TLS and `scram-sha-256`; credentials come from the secret store, never source or logs. |
| DB-6 | Similarity (vector) queries MUST always be tenant-filtered. |
| DB-7 | Audit and agent-step tables are append-only; audit rows are hash-chained for tamper evidence. |
| DB-8 | Cardholder data MUST NOT be stored in any table (SEC-6); non-production databases hold synthetic data only (ENV-2). |

## 8. Spec-Driven Development Rules

# Plan: fill in frontend-spec, backend-spec, api-contract, infrastructure-spec

## Context
Specs committed so far (HEAD 3d65082): constitution v0.3.0, spec v0.2.0, database-spec, design, agent, tasks plus skeletons for the four target files. This step turns the four skeleton templates into well-defined specs using the owner's decisions below, keeping IDs/rules consistent with constitution (ARC-, COD-, QA-, SEC-, AI-, DB-, ENV-) and spec.md (US-, FR-, NFR-). Then align design.md, agent.md, tasks.md, constitution (Related/changelog) and commit + `git pull --rebase` + push. Owner wants to stay in plan mode until they ask to execute.

## Owner decisions
- Frontend: Next.js App Router, TypeScript strict, shadcn/ui + Tailwind (Radix), TanStack Query, OpenAPI-generated TypeScript client.
- Backend: FastAPI gateway + Python agent microservices consuming jobs from RabbitMQ; results written to PostgreSQL; agent orchestration with LangGraph (provider-agnostic LLM interface, Claude default; checkpoints stored in Postgres).
- Auth: external OIDC IdP (Keycloak locally; Entra ID/Cognito later), SAML via IdP brokering; FastAPI validates JWTs; Next.js uses server-side session (httpOnly cookie, BFF pattern).
- Object store: MinIO locally, S3 on AWS.
- Local k8s: kind with umbrella Helm chart `aucoff` (subcharts/templates for frontend, backend, each agent service, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, MinIO, Keycloak, observability).
- API: REST + JSON under `/api/v1`, OpenAPI 3.1 as source of truth with Swagger UI (and ReDoc) for ALL endpoints; SSE for agent-run progress; cursor pagination; `Idempotency-Key` on POSTs.
- Observability: OpenTelemetry + Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo.
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions; Terraform for AWS later.
- Secrets/TLS: Kubernetes Secrets + cert-manager + NetworkPolicies locally; Secrets Manager/ACM later.

## File plans
### specs/frontend-spec.md
Tech choices (versions TODO), route map (dashboard, frameworks/controls/mappings, scopes, connectors, evidence, assessments, control results review, findings, approvals, reports, audit log, admin: users/roles/SSO/integrations), components (design system wrappers, data tables, evidence viewer with citations, approval dialog, agent-run timeline fed by SSE), auth/BFF flow, RBAC UI gating by persona PER-1..6, state/data (TanStack Query, generated client, optimistic updates only for safe actions), AI UX rules (AI badge, sources, confidence, approval status - AI-13), error/loading/empty states, WCAG 2.2 AA, security (CSP, no tokens in localStorage, XSS-safe rendering of agent text, OWASP Top 10 - NFR-1), performance budgets, testing (Vitest, Testing Library, Playwright, axe), mapping of screens to US-/FR-.

### specs/backend-spec.md
Tech choices (Python 3.13 TBD, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy 2 async, Alembic, aio-pika, LangGraph, boto3/google/azure SDKs read-only, structlog, OpenTelemetry), layered layout (ARC-3) plus `services/` for each agent microservice (mapping-agent, cloud-scanner, k8s-scanner, repo-scanner, saas-scanner, document-analyzer, assessment-orchestrator, remediation-advisor, report-generator from spec.md 5.6), service responsibilities table, queue topology (exchanges, queues, DLQs, retry/backoff, message schema with tenant_id, run_id, idempotency key), job lifecycle state machine, connector framework (read-only creds, per-tenant secret refs), RBAC permission matrix, tenant context and RLS handling, LLM provider interface, redaction pipeline (AI-8), budgets/cost limits (AI-12), SSE event publication, integrations (Jira, ServiceNow, Slack, Teams, email), config/secrets, logging/metrics/tracing, error mapping, security checklist (OWASP API Top 10 mapping table), testing plan (unit, integration with testcontainers, contract tests, RLS tests, agent evals).

### specs/api-contract.md
Conventions fixed: `/api/v1`, JSON, OpenAPI 3.1 generated by FastAPI and committed as `openapi.json`/`openapi.yaml`; every endpoint documented with summary, description, request/response schemas, error responses, examples, auth scope; Swagger UI at `/docs` and ReDoc at `/redoc` (protected in prod per TODO); CI check that generated spec matches committed and has no undocumented routes. Auth (Bearer JWT, scopes), error envelope (RFC 9457 problem+json style), cursor pagination, filtering/sorting, `Idempotency-Key`, rate limit headers, SSE stream spec (event types, reconnection with `Last-Event-ID`), webhooks. Resource endpoint tables with IDs API-n mapped to FR-/US-: auth/session, tenants/users/roles, integrations/connectors, frameworks/requirements/unified controls/mappings, scopes, evidence + uploads (presigned URLs), assessments, control results (review/approve), findings (+ticket sync), approvals, agent runs + SSE, reports (generate/download), dashboards, audit log (read/verify), notifications, health. Schemas for key objects. Versioning/deprecation policy and changelog.

### specs/infrastructure-spec.md
Environments (kind local, AWS later), container inventory (frontend, backend, each agent service, PostgreSQL 18.6+pgvector, RabbitMQ, MinIO, Keycloak, otel-collector, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo), image standards (non-root, minimal base, pinned digests, SBOM, scanning), umbrella Helm chart layout and values structure (`values.yaml`, `values-local.yaml`, `values-aws.yaml` placeholder), ingress (NGINX or Traefik TBD) + cert-manager TLS with local CA, namespaces, NetworkPolicies default-deny with allow list (DB reachable only from backend/agents), Pod Security (restricted), resource requests/limits, HPA for scanners, secrets handling, migration hook Job, local workflow (kind create, build/load images, helm install, port-forward, teardown), Makefile targets, GitHub Actions pipeline (lint, test, build, scan with Trivy/Gitleaks, SBOM, helm lint/kubeconform, e2e on kind), observability pipeline, backup/restore, AWS migration table (EKS, RDS/Aurora PG, Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ, S3, Cognito/Entra, Secrets Manager, ACM, ALB, ECR, CloudWatch/AMP/AMG, Terraform modules layout), region/residency note, cost notes, open questions.

### Alignment edits
- design.md: components table (RabbitMQ, MinIO, Keycloak, LangGraph), architecture overview text/diagram, data flows, ADR-3 LangGraph, ADR-4 RabbitMQ, ADR-5 OIDC IdP, ADR-6 OpenAPI-first.
- agent.md: LangGraph orchestration (state, checkpointer in Postgres, human-approval interrupt nodes), service names.
- tasks.md: expand phases with backend/frontend/infra/API tasks and traceability.
- constitution.md: add Related links; add rule API-1..n (OpenAPI documentation required, contract tests) and bump to 0.4.0 with changelog.
- database-spec.md: add LangGraph checkpoint tables note and queue/outbox note if needed.

## Execution (after owner says go)
Write/edit files above, then `git add specs`, commit with Co-Authored-By trailer, `git pull --rebase origin main`, `git push origin main`.

## Verification
- `ls specs/` still shows ten spec files; no TODO-only skeleton sections in the four target files except marked open items.
- Grep for cross-links and consistent IDs (US-/FR-/NFR-/API-/DB-); no references to removed choices.
- Spot-check tables and Mermaid blocks render; `git status` clean and `git log origin/main` shows the push.

# AUCoFF Frontend Spec (Next.js)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Status | Draft |
| Version | 0.2.0 |
| Owner | Praveen Darshanam |
| Last updated | 2026-10-18 |

> Purpose: UI behaviour and structure for the Next.js (React, TypeScript) app. Entity IDs are UUID strings and the tenant comes from the session, never the URL or client input (see [database-spec.md](database-spec.md), [api-contract.md](api-contract.md)).

Related: [spec.md](spec.md) · [api-contract.md](api-contract.md) · [design.md](design.md) · [constitution.md](constitution.md) · [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md)

## 1. Tech Choices
| Area | Choice | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| Framework | Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript `strict` | Version pinned in `package.json` (TODO); COD-2 |
| UI | shadcn/ui (Radix primitives) + Tailwind CSS | Components copied into repo under `components/ui` |
| Server state | TanStack Query | Caching, retries, invalidation |
| API client | TypeScript client generated from the backend OpenAPI spec (e.g. `openapi-typescript` + `openapi-fetch`; tool TODO) | Generated on CI; never hand-edit; keeps contract in sync (DES-7) |
| Forms / validation | React Hook Form + Zod | Zod schemas mirror API schemas |
| Charts | TODO (e.g. Recharts) | Dashboards (US-8) |
| Auth | Server-side session via BFF pattern (Auth.js or equivalent - TODO) | See section 5 |
| Unit/component tests | Vitest + Testing Library | |
| E2E / a11y tests | Playwright + axe-core | |
| Lint/format | ESLint + Prettier | COD-2 |

## 2. Information Architecture
| Route | Page | Persona | Roles | Spec refs |
|-------|------|---------|-------|-----------|
| `/` | Posture dashboard (per framework / jurisdiction, trends) | PER-4, PER-5 | executive, ciso, compliance_officer | US-8, US-13, FR-11 |
| `/frameworks` | Framework and requirement catalogue | PER-1 | all (read) | US-1, FR-1 |
| `/controls` | Unified controls and mappings (review/approve) | PER-1 | compliance_officer | US-1, FR-2 |
| `/scopes` | Assessment scopes and schedules | PER-1 | compliance_officer | US-2, FR-3 |
| `/connectors` | Source connectors (cloud, k8s, repos, SaaS) | PER-3, PER-6 | engineer, admin | US-3, FR-4 |
| `/evidence` | Evidence list, document upload, evidence viewer | PER-1, PER-2 | compliance_officer, engineer, auditor | US-4, FR-5, FR-6 |
| `/assessments` | Assessment runs and live progress | PER-1 | compliance_officer | US-5, FR-3, FR-15 |
| `/assessments/[id]` | Control results with citations; review/approve | PER-1, PER-2 | compliance_officer, auditor (read) | US-5, FR-7 |
| `/findings` | Findings list and detail, ticket links | PER-3, PER-5 | engineer, compliance_officer, ciso | US-6, FR-8, FR-9 |
| `/approvals` | Pending agent-action approvals | PER-1, PER-5 | compliance_officer, ciso | US-5, FR-7 |
| `/reports` | Generate, list, download reports | PER-1, PER-2 | compliance_officer, auditor, ciso | US-9, FR-12 |
| `/audit-log` | Audit trail and integrity check | PER-2 | auditor, ciso | US-7, FR-10 |
| `/settings/users` | Users and roles | PER-6 | admin | US-10, FR-13 |
| `/settings/sso` | OIDC/SAML configuration | PER-6 | admin | US-10 |
| `/settings/integrations` | Jira, ServiceNow, Slack, Teams, email | PER-6 | admin | US-11, FR-9, FR-14 |
| `/login`, `/logout` | Auth entry points | all | - | US-10 |

## 3. Key Screens
### 3.1 Control result review (`/assessments/[id]`)
- Table of unified controls with status, confidence, framework badges, last reviewed.
- Detail panel: agent summary (AI-labelled), cited evidence passages with deep links to the evidence viewer, mapped framework requirements, run metadata (model, prompt version).
- Actions: approve, reject with comment, edit status (reason required). Each action calls the approvals API and shows the recorded approver and time.
### 3.2 Agent run timeline
- Live steps from the SSE stream (see [api-contract.md](api-contract.md)): started, tool call, evidence collected, result produced, awaiting approval, failed.
- Shows token/cost progress against budget (NFR-8).
### 3.3 Posture dashboard
- Coverage % by framework and jurisdiction, open findings by severity, trend, readiness score (definitions from [spec.md](spec.md) section 10).
### 3.4 Findings
- Filter by severity, framework, jurisdiction, status; remediation steps; "Create ticket" with Jira/ServiceNow link and status sync.
### 3.5 Reports
- Pick assessment and framework, generate, show status, download; shows included approvals.

## 4. Components
| Component | Purpose | Notes |
|-----------|---------|-------|
| `AppShell` | Navigation, tenant/user menu, role-aware items | Hides items the role cannot use (server still enforces, SEC-1) |
| `DataTable` | Sorting, cursor pagination, filters | Server-driven; keyboard accessible |
| `AiBadge` | Marks AI-generated content | AI-13 |
| `CitationList` | Source citations with links | AI-3 |
| `ConfidenceIndicator` | Shows confidence/uncertainty | AI-9; never colour-only |
| `ApprovalDialog` | Approve/reject with comment | Confirms consequences |
| `RunTimeline` | SSE-driven run progress | Reconnects with `Last-Event-ID` |
| `EvidenceViewer` | Preview documents/config snippets | Sanitised rendering only |
| `FrameworkBadge`, `SeverityBadge`, `StatusBadge` | Consistent visuals | |
| `EmptyState`, `ErrorState`, `Skeleton` | Standard states | |

## 5. Auth and Session
- Login via the external OIDC identity provider (Keycloak locally; Entra ID/Cognito later). SAML handled by the IdP.
- Next.js server (BFF) performs the code flow with PKCE, holds tokens server-side, and issues an `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` session cookie. Tokens MUST NOT be stored in `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`.
- API calls from the browser go to Next.js route handlers or a same-site proxy that attach the access token; CSRF protection on state-changing requests.
- Role and tenant come from token claims; UI gating is cosmetic only.
- Session expiry and silent refresh handled server-side; idle timeout TODO.

## 6. Agent Interaction UX (AI-13, AI-9)
- AI-generated text carries an `AiBadge`, sources, confidence and approval status.
- Low-confidence or unverified claims are visually distinct and routed to the approvals queue.
- Agent output rendered as plain text/sanitised Markdown only; no raw HTML (XSS).
- Users can see which model/prompt version produced a result.

## 7. State and Data Fetching
- All server data via TanStack Query with the generated client; query keys include resource and filters (tenant is implicit in session).
- Optimistic updates only for safe, reversible UI actions (never approvals).
- SSE handled by a dedicated hook that updates the query cache.
- Uploads use presigned URLs from the API and show progress; client checks size/type but server is authoritative.

## 8. States and Errors
Loading (skeletons), empty (guidance + primary action), error (problem+json message and request ID), permission denied (403 page), offline/reconnecting banner, partial agent failure shown inline. Forms show field-level errors mapped from API validation errors.

## 9. Accessibility and i18n
- WCAG 2.2 AA (NFR-10, QA-10): keyboard navigation, focus management in dialogs, ARIA labels, contrast, no colour-only status, reduced-motion support; axe checks in CI.
- English first; strings externalised for later localisation (TODO library); dates/numbers formatted via `Intl`.

## 10. Security (NFR-1)
- Strict Content-Security-Policy, `X-Content-Type-Options`, frame protections, `Referrer-Policy`, HSTS (via ingress).
- No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with untrusted content; sanitise Markdown; validate and encode all URL params.
- Dependency audit and lockfile checks in CI (COD-7).
- No secrets in client bundles; only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` public config.

## 11. Performance Budgets (proposal)
- LCP < 2.5 s and INP < 200 ms on dashboard on a mid-range laptop; JS budget per route TODO; tables virtualised above 200 rows.

## 12. Project Layout
```
frontend/
  app/                # routes (App Router)
  components/ui/      # shadcn/ui
  components/         # app components
  lib/api/            # generated client + wrappers
  lib/auth/
  hooks/
  tests/              # unit, e2e
```

## 13. Testing Plan
- Unit/component: Vitest + Testing Library for components and hooks.
- E2E: Playwright against the kind deployment for critical flows (login, run assessment, review and approve, create ticket, generate report).
- Accessibility: axe-core in component and E2E tests.
- Contract: generated client compiled against committed OpenAPI; build fails on drift.
- Visual regression: TODO.

## 14. Open Questions
- [ ] BFF auth library choice and session store.
- [ ] Charting library.
- [ ] i18n requirements and target locales (India/EU).
- [ ] Dark mode and branding.
