# AUCoFF Backend Spec (FastAPI + Agent Services)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Status | Draft |
| Version | 0.2.0 |
| Owner | Praveen Darshanam |
| Last updated | 2026-10-18 |

> Purpose: services, domain logic, agent microservices and persistence behind the API defined in [api-contract.md](api-contract.md).

Related: [spec.md](spec.md) · [design.md](design.md) · [agent.md](agent.md) · [infrastructure-spec.md](infrastructure-spec.md) · [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) · [constitution.md](constitution.md)

## 1. Tech Choices
| Area | Choice | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| Language | Python (version TODO, pinned) | COD-1 |
| API | FastAPI + Pydantic v2 | OpenAPI 3.1 generated and committed |
| ORM / migrations | SQLAlchemy 2.x (async) + Alembic | [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) |
| Database | PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector | RLS; `SET LOCAL app.tenant_id` per transaction |
| Queue | RabbitMQ via `aio-pika` | Jobs from API to agent services |
| Agent orchestration | LangGraph | Checkpoints in PostgreSQL; interrupt nodes for human approval |
| LLM access | Provider-agnostic interface; Claude default | ARC-5, AI-8, AI-12 |
| Object store | S3 API (MinIO locally, S3 on AWS) via `boto3` | Presigned URLs |
| Cloud/SaaS SDKs | boto3, Google, Azure, GitHub/Bitbucket, Microsoft Graph, Metabase API | Read-only scopes only |
| Logging / tracing | structlog (JSON), OpenTelemetry | COD-8 |
| Tooling | Ruff, mypy, pytest, httpx, testcontainers | COD-1, QA |

## 2. Architecture
FastAPI is the single gateway for the frontend (ARC-1). Long-running work is published to RabbitMQ and executed by Python agent services; results go to PostgreSQL and progress events to the API for SSE.
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  UI[Next.js] --> API[FastAPI gateway]
  API --> DB[(PostgreSQL + pgvector)]
  API --> MQ[[RabbitMQ]]
  MQ --> ORCH[assessment-orchestrator]
  ORCH --> MQ
  MQ --> SC[scanner / agent services]
  SC --> DB
  SC --> OBJ[(S3 / MinIO)]
  SC --> LLM[LLM provider]
  SC -->|read-only| EXT[Cloud, K8s, repos, SaaS]
  SC -->|events| MQ
  MQ -->|run events| API
```

## 3. Project Layout
```
backend/
  app/                    # gateway
    api/                  # routers, dependencies, schemas
    core/                 # config, security, tenancy, errors
    domain/               # entities and business rules (no I/O imports)
    db/                   # models, repositories, migrations
    messaging/            # publishers, message schemas
    integrations/         # Jira, ServiceNow, Slack, Teams, email
    llm/                  # provider interface and adapters, redaction
  services/               # one package per agent microservice
    common/               # shared worker base, queue, LLM, tracing
    mapping_agent/
    cloud_scanner/
    k8s_scanner/
    repo_scanner/
    saas_scanner/
    document_analyzer/
    assessment_orchestrator/
    remediation_advisor/
    report_generator/
  tests/
```
Rules: `api -> domain -> db/messaging/llm` only (ARC-3); services reuse `domain` and `db` packages, not `api`.

## 4. Services
| Service | Responsibility | Consumes | Produces | Spec refs |
|---------|----------------|----------|----------|-----------|
| gateway (`app`) | REST API, auth, RBAC, SSE, presigned URLs | HTTP, run events | jobs | FR-1..15 |
| `assessment-orchestrator` | Builds the LangGraph plan per assessment, fans out scanner jobs, aggregates control results | `assessment.requested` | `scan.*`, `analysis.*`, `assessment.completed` | FR-3, FR-7 |
| `mapping-agent` | Proposes requirement-to-control mappings | `mapping.requested` | mapping proposals (pending approval) | FR-2 |
| `cloud-scanner` | AWS/GCP/Azure read-only configuration collection and checks | `scan.cloud` | evidence + checks | FR-6 |
| `k8s-scanner` | Cluster/Helm/RBAC/image configuration checks | `scan.k8s` | evidence + checks | FR-6 |
| `repo-scanner` | GitHub/Bitbucket and CI/CD settings | `scan.repo` | evidence + checks | FR-6 |
| `saas-scanner` | Entra ID, Metabase | `scan.saas` | evidence + checks | FR-6 |
| `document-analyzer` | Parse, chunk, embed, RAG-assess documents | `analysis.document` | evidence + candidate results | FR-5, FR-7 |
| `remediation-advisor` | Findings and advisory remediation | `finding.requested` | findings | FR-8 |
| `report-generator` | Cited reports and evidence packs | `report.requested` | report objects | FR-12 |
All scanners are read-only (spec.md 5.5, AI-1, AI-6).

## 5. Messaging
- Broker: RabbitMQ; durable topic exchange `aucoff.jobs`, per-service queues, dead-letter exchange `aucoff.dlx` with per-queue DLQs.
- Message envelope (JSON): `message_id`, `idempotency_key`, `tenant_id`, `assessment_id`, `agent_run_id`, `type`, `schema_version`, `payload`, `trace_context`, `created_at`.
- Delivery: at-least-once; consumers MUST be idempotent (DES-4); manual acks after commit; retries with exponential backoff, max attempts then DLQ and alert.
- Outbox: the API writes the job row and an outbox record in one transaction; a relay publishes to RabbitMQ (avoids lost messages).
- Tenant context travels in the envelope; consumers set `app.tenant_id` before any DB access.
- Run events (`run.step`, `run.status`, `run.cost`) published to `aucoff.events` and relayed by the gateway as SSE.

## 6. Job and Run Lifecycle
`queued -> running -> awaiting_approval -> completed` with `failed`, `cancelled`, `budget_exceeded` terminals. Transitions are validated in `domain`, persisted in `agent_runs`, and audit-logged. Cancellation propagates through the queue. Time, step and cost budgets enforced per run (AI-12).

## 7. Connectors
- A connector per source type with a common interface: `validate()`, `collect(scope)`, `describe_permissions()`.
- Credentials: per-tenant secret references (`integrations.config_ref`); secrets retrieved at run time from the secret store, held in memory only, never logged or sent to LLMs (SEC-3).
- Required permissions are read-only and documented per connector; `validate()` fails if broader permissions are detected (warning to admin).
- Rate limiting and backoff per provider API; partial failure recorded as `unknown` results, not silently skipped.
- Evidence stored in the object store with SHA-256 and provenance (source, time, collector version).

## 8. Auth, RBAC and Tenancy
- JWTs from the external OIDC provider are validated (signature via JWKS, issuer, audience, expiry); tenant and roles mapped from claims.
- Roles: compliance_officer, auditor, engineer, executive, ciso, admin (database-spec `roles`). Permission matrix (TODO to finalise):

| Capability | compliance_officer | auditor | engineer | executive | ciso | admin |
|------------|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| View catalogues | x | x | x | x | x | x |
| Approve mappings | x | | | | x | |
| Manage scopes / run assessments | x | | | | x | |
| Manage connectors | | | x | | | x |
| Review / approve results | x | | | | x | |
| View evidence | x | x | x | | x | |
| Manage findings | x | | x | | x | |
| Generate / download reports | x | x | | x | x | |
| View audit log | | x | | | x | x |
| Manage users / SSO / integrations | | | | | | x |

- Every request opens a transaction with `SET LOCAL app.tenant_id`; missing tenant fails closed (DB-3).
- Authorisation checks in `domain`/dependencies, never only in routers (SEC-1).

## 9. LLM and Agent Integration
- `llm` package defines `LLMProvider` (chat, tool use, embeddings) with adapters (Claude default); model, version and parameters from configuration.
- Redaction pipeline (PII/secrets) runs before every outbound call (AI-8); redaction rules versioned and tested.
- Prompts live in versioned files; every run records `prompt_version`, model, token usage and cost (AI-10).
- LangGraph graphs: state persisted via the Postgres checkpointer; approval steps use interrupts so a run resumes only after an `approvals` decision (AI-2). Details in [agent.md](agent.md).
- Structured outputs validated by Pydantic; invalid output retried within limits then escalated (AI-5).
- Retrieval: tenant-filtered pgvector queries only (DB-6).

## 10. Integrations
| System | Direction | Notes |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| Jira, ServiceNow | Create/update tickets for findings; sync status | Webhook or polling (TODO) |
| Slack, Microsoft Teams, email | Notifications for findings and approvals | Per-event preferences |
| Identity provider | OIDC login, SAML via IdP | Admin configured |
Credentials via secret references; outbound calls have timeouts, retries and circuit breakers.

## 11. Configuration and Secrets
12-factor environment config (ARC-8) validated by Pydantic Settings at start-up; values from Helm values/ConfigMaps; secrets from Kubernetes Secrets (Secrets Manager on AWS); no defaults for secrets; config documented in [infrastructure-spec.md](infrastructure-spec.md).

## 12. Observability
Structured JSON logs with `request_id`, `tenant_id`, `agent_run_id` (no PII or secrets); OpenTelemetry traces across API, queue and services; Prometheus metrics (request latency, queue depth, run durations, LLM tokens/cost, scanner errors); health endpoints (`/health/live`, `/health/ready`).

## 13. Error Handling
Domain exceptions map to the problem-detail format in [api-contract.md](api-contract.md); unexpected errors return a generic message with a request ID and are logged with stack traces; no internals leaked (COD-6).

## 14. OWASP API Security Top 10 Mapping (NFR-1)
| Risk | Control |
|------|---------|
| API1 Broken object level authorisation | Tenant RLS + per-object ownership checks; UUIDs |
| API2 Broken authentication | OIDC JWT validation, short-lived tokens |
| API3 Broken object property level authorisation | Explicit response schemas; no mass assignment |
| API4 Unrestricted resource consumption | Rate limits, pagination caps, upload limits, LLM budgets |
| API5 Broken function level authorisation | RBAC matrix enforced in domain |
| API6 Unrestricted access to sensitive business flows | Approval gates, idempotency keys, quotas |
| API7 Server-side request forgery | Allow-listed connector endpoints, no user-supplied URLs fetched blindly |
| API8 Security misconfiguration | Hardened images, secure defaults, config validation, security headers |
| API9 Improper inventory management | OpenAPI as the only source of routes; deprecation policy |
| API10 Unsafe consumption of APIs | Validate third-party and LLM responses; timeouts |

## 15. Testing Plan
- Unit: `domain` at >= 90% coverage (QA-3).
- Integration: PostgreSQL 18.6 + RabbitMQ via testcontainers; migrations, RLS and privilege tests ([database-spec.md](database-spec.md) section 10).
- Contract: generated OpenAPI equals committed `openapi.yaml`; schemathesis-style fuzz against it.
- Messaging: idempotency, retry, DLQ behaviour.
- Agents: evaluation suites with golden datasets; LLM calls mocked or replayed in CI (QA-6, QA-8).
- Security: SAST, dependency audit, DAST/API scan against kind deployment.

## 16. Open Questions
- [ ] Python and FastAPI versions.
- [ ] Final permission matrix and custom roles.
- [ ] Ticket sync: webhook vs polling.
- [ ] Per-scanner concurrency and rate limits.
- [ ] Embedding model and dimension.
- [ ] Checkpointer retention policy for LangGraph state.

# AUCoFF API Contract

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Status | Draft |
| Version | 0.2.0 |
| Owner | Praveen Darshanam |
| Last updated | 2026-10-18 |

> Purpose: the contract between frontend and backend. The OpenAPI 3.1 document generated by FastAPI is the source of truth and MUST match this specification. Every endpoint MUST be documented.

Related: [frontend-spec.md](frontend-spec.md) · [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) · [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) · [spec.md](spec.md) · [constitution.md](constitution.md)

## 1. Conventions
| Topic | Rule |
|-------|------|
| Base path | `/api/v1` |
| Format | JSON (`application/json`), UTF-8; errors `application/problem+json` |
| Identifiers | UUID v7 strings; timestamps ISO 8601 UTC |
| Tenancy | Derived from the authenticated token, never from client-supplied parameters (see [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) section 6.2) |
| Auth | `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` issued by the OIDC provider |
| Naming | Plural nouns, kebab-case paths, snake_case JSON fields |
| Versioning | URI major version; additive changes allowed within `v1`; breaking changes require `v2` and a deprecation period (TODO length, proposal 6 months) with `Deprecation`/`Sunset` headers |
| Pagination | Cursor-based: `?limit=` (default 25, max 100) and `?cursor=`; response `{ "items": [], "next_cursor": "..." \| null }` |
| Filtering / sorting | `?filter[field]=value`, `?sort=field,-other` (allow-listed fields only) |
| Idempotency | All `POST` that create or trigger work accept `Idempotency-Key` (UUID); same key + same body returns the original response for 24 h (proposal); same key + different body returns 422 |
| Rate limiting | Per tenant and user; headers `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset`; 429 with `Retry-After` |
| Request tracing | Client may send `X-Request-ID`; always echoed in responses and errors |
| Concurrency | `ETag` / `If-Match` on mutable resources (optional per endpoint) |
| Long-running work | `202 Accepted` with a resource to poll plus SSE stream |

## 2. API Documentation (Swagger / OpenAPI) - Required
- FastAPI generates an **OpenAPI 3.1** document at `/api/v1/openapi.json`; a copy is committed as `specs/openapi.yaml` (or `backend/openapi.yaml` - TODO location).
- **Swagger UI** at `/docs` and **ReDoc** at `/redoc` document all endpoints. In production they require authentication or are disabled per tenant policy (TODO decision).
- Every operation MUST have: `operationId`, summary, description, tags, request/response schemas with examples, all error responses, required scopes (security requirement), and pagination/idempotency parameters where applicable.
- Every schema field MUST have a type, description, and constraints (format, min/max, enum).
- CI MUST fail when: generated OpenAPI differs from the committed file; any route lacks documentation or an error response; the document fails linting (Spectral or equivalent - TODO); frontend client generation or contract tests break.
- The frontend TypeScript client is generated from this document.

## 3. Error Format (RFC 9457 problem details)
```json
{
  "type": "https://aucoff.example/problems/validation-error",
  "title": "Validation failed",
  "status": 422,
  "detail": "Field 'name' is required.",
  "instance": "/api/v1/scopes",
  "code": "validation_error",
  "request_id": "0192f0b2-...",
  "errors": [{ "field": "name", "message": "Field required" }]
}
```
| Status | Use |
|--------|-----|
| 400 | Malformed request |
| 401 | Missing/invalid token |
| 403 | Authenticated but not permitted |
| 404 | Not found (also used for other tenants' objects) |
| 409 | State conflict (e.g. approving a result already decided) |
| 412 | `If-Match` mismatch |
| 413 | Payload too large |
| 415 | Unsupported media type |
| 422 | Validation error |
| 429 | Rate limited |
| 500 / 503 | Server error / dependency unavailable (no internal detail) |

## 4. Auth Scopes and Roles
| Scope | Description | Roles |
|-------|-------------|-------|
| `catalog:read` | Read frameworks, requirements, controls | all |
| `mapping:write` | Propose/approve mappings | compliance_officer, ciso |
| `scope:write` | Manage scopes and schedules | compliance_officer, ciso |
| `assessment:run` | Start/cancel assessments | compliance_officer, ciso |
| `connector:write` | Manage connectors | engineer, admin |
| `evidence:read` / `evidence:write` | View / upload evidence | per matrix in [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) |
| `result:review` | Approve/reject control results | compliance_officer, ciso |
| `finding:write` | Manage findings and tickets | compliance_officer, engineer, ciso |
| `report:read` / `report:generate` | Reports | compliance_officer, auditor, executive, ciso |
| `audit:read` | Audit log | auditor, ciso, admin |
| `admin:write` | Users, roles, SSO, integrations | admin |
Scopes derive from roles; the matrix in [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) section 8 is authoritative.

## 5. Endpoints
All paths are under `/api/v1`. Status shows the success code.

### 5.1 Session and identity
| ID | Method | Path | Summary | Scope | OK | Refs |
|----|--------|------|---------|-------|----|------|
| API-1 | GET | `/me` | Current user, tenant, roles | any | 200 | US-10 |
| API-2 | GET | `/health/live`, `/health/ready` | Probes (no auth) | none | 200 | - |

### 5.2 Administration
| ID | Method | Path | Summary | Scope | OK | Refs |
|----|--------|------|---------|-------|----|------|
| API-10 | GET/POST | `/users` | List / invite users | admin:write | 200/201 | US-10, FR-13 |
| API-11 | GET/PATCH/DELETE | `/users/{user_id}` | Read, update, deactivate | admin:write | 200/204 | FR-13 |
| API-12 | GET | `/roles` | List roles | admin:write | 200 | FR-13 |
| API-13 | PUT | `/users/{user_id}/roles` | Replace role assignment | admin:write | 200 | FR-13 |
| API-14 | GET/PUT | `/settings/sso` | SSO configuration | admin:write | 200 | US-10 |
| API-15 | GET/POST | `/integrations` | Ticketing/notification integrations | admin:write | 200/201 | US-11, FR-9, FR-14 |
| API-16 | PATCH/DELETE | `/integrations/{id}` | Update/remove | admin:write | 200/204 | FR-14 |

### 5.3 Catalogue and mappings
| ID | Method | Path | Summary | Scope | OK | Refs |
|----|--------|------|---------|-------|----|------|
| API-20 | GET | `/frameworks` | List frameworks (filter by jurisdiction/type) | catalog:read | 200 | US-1, US-13, FR-1 |
| API-21 | GET | `/frameworks/{id}/requirements` | Requirements (paged) | catalog:read | 200 | FR-1 |
| API-22 | GET | `/unified-controls` | Unified controls (filter by framework, domain) | catalog:read | 200 | US-1 |
| API-23 | GET | `/control-mappings` | Mappings with status | catalog:read | 200 | FR-2 |
| API-24 | POST | `/control-mappings:propose` | Ask mapping agent to propose mappings | mapping:write | 202 | FR-2 |
| API-25 | POST | `/control-mappings/{id}/decision` | Approve/reject mapping | mapping:write | 200 | FR-2 |

### 5.4 Connectors, scopes and evidence
| ID | Method | Path | Summary | Scope | OK | Refs |
|----|--------|------|---------|-------|----|------|
| API-30 | GET/POST | `/connectors` | List / create connector | connector:write | 200/201 | US-3, FR-4 |
| API-31 | POST | `/connectors/{id}:test` | Validate read-only access | connector:write | 200 | FR-4 |
| API-32 | PATCH/DELETE | `/connectors/{id}` | Update/remove | connector:write | 200/204 | FR-4 |
| API-33 | GET/POST | `/scopes` | List / create assessment scopes | scope:write | 200/201 | US-2, FR-3 |
| API-34 | GET/PATCH/DELETE | `/scopes/{id}` | Read/update/delete (incl. schedule) | scope:write | 200/204 | US-12 |
| API-35 | POST | `/evidence/uploads` | Create upload (returns presigned URL) | evidence:write | 201 | US-4, FR-5 |
| API-36 | POST | `/evidence/uploads/{id}:complete` | Finalise upload and start analysis | evidence:write | 202 | FR-5 |
| API-37 | GET | `/evidence` | List evidence (filter by scope, source) | evidence:read | 200 | FR-6 |
| API-38 | GET | `/evidence/{id}` | Metadata and short-lived download URL | evidence:read | 200 | US-7 |

### 5.5 Assessments, results and findings
| ID | Method | Path | Summary | Scope | OK | Refs |
|----|--------|------|---------|-------|----|------|
| API-40 | POST | `/assessments` | Start assessment (async) | assessment:run | 202 | US-5, FR-3 |
| API-41 | GET | `/assessments` | List assessments | assessment:run / report:read | 200 | FR-3 |
| API-42 | GET | `/assessments/{id}` | Status and summary | same | 200 | FR-3 |
| API-43 | POST | `/assessments/{id}:cancel` | Cancel | assessment:run | 202 | FR-3 |
| API-44 | GET | `/assessments/{id}/control-results` | Results with citations | result:review / evidence:read | 200 | US-5, FR-7 |
| API-45 | GET | `/control-results/{id}` | Detail incl. evidence and run metadata | same | 200 | FR-7 |
| API-46 | POST | `/control-results/{id}/decision` | Approve/reject/edit with comment | result:review | 200 | US-5, FR-7 |
| API-47 | GET | `/findings` | List findings (filter severity, framework, status) | finding:write / read | 200 | US-6, FR-8 |
| API-48 | GET/PATCH | `/findings/{id}` | Read / update status (accept risk requires approval) | finding:write | 200 | FR-8 |
| API-49 | POST | `/findings/{id}/tickets` | Create Jira/ServiceNow ticket | finding:write | 201 | FR-9 |

### 5.6 Agent runs, approvals, reports, dashboards, audit
| ID | Method | Path | Summary | Scope | OK | Refs |
|----|--------|------|---------|-------|----|------|
| API-50 | GET | `/agent-runs/{id}` | Run metadata, model, prompt version, cost | assessment:run | 200 | FR-15 |
| API-51 | GET | `/agent-runs/{id}/events` | SSE stream of run progress (section 6) | assessment:run | 200 | FR-15 |
| API-52 | GET | `/approvals` | Pending/decided approvals | result:review | 200 | FR-7 |
| API-53 | POST | `/approvals/{id}/decision` | Decide an agent action | result:review | 200 | AI-2 |
| API-60 | POST | `/reports` | Generate report (async) | report:generate | 202 | US-9, FR-12 |
| API-61 | GET | `/reports`, `/reports/{id}` | List / read / download link | report:read | 200 | FR-12 |
| API-70 | GET | `/dashboards/posture` | Coverage, findings, trends (by framework/jurisdiction) | report:read | 200 | US-8, FR-11 |
| API-80 | GET | `/audit-log` | Audit events (paged, filtered) | audit:read | 200 | US-7, FR-10 |
| API-81 | POST | `/audit-log:verify` | Verify hash-chain integrity for a range | audit:read | 200 | SEC-10 |
| API-90 | GET/PUT | `/notification-preferences` | Per-user event channels | any | 200 | US-11, FR-14 |

## 6. Streaming (SSE)
- Endpoint: `GET /agent-runs/{id}/events`, `Accept: text/event-stream`, auth by the same session/token.
- Event types: `run.status`, `run.step`, `run.evidence`, `run.result`, `run.approval_required`, `run.cost`, `run.error`, `heartbeat` (every 15 s).
- Each event has `id` (monotonic per run) and JSON `data`; clients reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` and receive missed events.
- Stream ends after a terminal status; server enforces per-user connection limits.

## 7. Key Schemas (outline; full definitions live in OpenAPI)
| Schema | Key fields |
|--------|-----------|
| `Problem` | type, title, status, detail, instance, code, request_id, errors[] |
| `Page<T>` | items[], next_cursor |
| `Framework` | id, code, name, version, jurisdiction, type |
| `Requirement` | id, framework_id, ref, title, text? |
| `UnifiedControl` | id, code, title, description, domain |
| `ControlMapping` | id, requirement_id, unified_control_id, strength, rationale, source, status |
| `Scope` | id, name, framework_ids[], target_refs, schedule? |
| `Evidence` | id, scope_id, source_type, source_ref, sha256, collected_at, classification |
| `Assessment` | id, scope_id, status, started_at, completed_at, agent_run_id |
| `ControlResult` | id, unified_control_id, status, confidence, summary, citations[], review{status,by,at} |
| `Citation` | evidence_id, locator, excerpt |
| `Finding` | id, control_result_id, severity, title, description, recommendation, status, ticket_ref |
| `AgentRun` | id, agent_id, model, prompt_version, status, tokens, cost_usd |
| `Approval` | id, action, requested_at, decided_by, decision, decided_at, comment |
| `Report` | id, assessment_id, format, status, download_url? |
| `AuditEvent` | id, occurred_at, actor, action, target, outcome, request_id |

## 8. Webhooks (inbound)
Jira/ServiceNow status callbacks to `POST /integrations/{id}/webhook`: signature (HMAC) verified, replay-protected by timestamp, rate-limited, payload schema validated. Details TODO.

## 9. Security Requirements (NFR-1)
OWASP API Security Top 10 mapping in [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) section 14; TLS only; CORS limited to the frontend origin; no sensitive data in URLs or logs; response schemas explicit; request size limits; upload content-type/size checks and malware scan (TODO); no secrets or PII in error messages.

## 10. Changelog
| Version | Date | Change | Breaking |
|---------|------|--------|----------|
| 0.1.0 | 2026-10-18 | Initial template | - |
| 0.2.0 | 2026-10-18 | Conventions, documentation requirement, endpoint catalogue, SSE | - |

## 11. Open Questions
- [ ] Where the committed OpenAPI file lives and the lint ruleset.
- [ ] Whether `/docs` is enabled in production.
- [ ] Deprecation period and idempotency retention.
- [ ] Webhook vs polling for ticket sync.
- [ ] Bulk endpoints and export formats for reports.

# AUCoFF Infrastructure Spec

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Status | Draft |
| Version | 0.2.0 |
| Owner | Praveen Darshanam |
| Last updated | 2026-10-18 |

> Purpose: how AUCoFF is packaged, deployed and operated. Phase 1: local Kubernetes (kind) with one umbrella Helm chart. Phase 2: AWS (EKS) with Terraform.

Related: [design.md](design.md) · [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) · [frontend-spec.md](frontend-spec.md) · [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) · [constitution.md](constitution.md)

## 1. Environments
| Env | Platform | Purpose | Status |
|-----|----------|---------|--------|
| local | kind cluster on laptop | Development, integration and E2E testing; synthetic data only (ENV-2) | Phase 1 |
| ci | GitHub Actions runners + ephemeral kind | Build, test, scan, E2E | Phase 1 |
| aws | EKS + managed services (section 10) | Staging / production | Phase 2 |
Same images and chart in all environments, differing only by values (ENV-1).

## 2. Container Inventory
| Component | Image / source | Notes |
|-----------|----------------|-------|
| frontend | `frontend/` (Next.js standalone) | Port 3000 (TODO) |
| backend gateway | `backend/app` (FastAPI) | Port 8000 (TODO) |
| agent services (9) | `backend/services/*` | assessment-orchestrator, mapping-agent, cloud-scanner, k8s-scanner, repo-scanner, saas-scanner, document-analyzer, remediation-advisor, report-generator |
| PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector | Official/operator image with pgvector (TODO choose) | [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) |
| RabbitMQ | Official chart/image | Queues per [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) section 5 |
| MinIO | Official chart/image | S3-compatible evidence/report store |
| Keycloak | Official chart/image | Local OIDC/SAML IdP |
| Observability | OpenTelemetry Collector, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo | Section 8 |
| Ingress + cert-manager | NGINX Ingress (or Traefik - TODO) + cert-manager | Local CA for TLS |

### Image standards
- Multi-stage builds, minimal base (distroless or slim), non-root user, read-only root filesystem where possible (SEC-8).
- Pinned base image digests; lockfile-based installs; SBOM generated; vulnerability scan (Trivy) blocks on critical/high.
- Health endpoints for liveness/readiness; graceful shutdown.
- Images tagged with git SHA; semantic versions for releases.

## 3. Helm Chart (umbrella)
```
deploy/helm/aucoff/
  Chart.yaml
  values.yaml            # defaults
  values-local.yaml      # kind overrides
  values-aws.yaml        # placeholder for Phase 2
  charts/                # subcharts / vendored dependencies
  templates/
    frontend/ backend/ services/ migration-job/ networkpolicies/ ingress/ rbac/
```
- Dependencies (subcharts): PostgreSQL (or operator), RabbitMQ, MinIO, Keycloak, observability stack; each toggled by `<name>.enabled` so AWS can disable in-cluster versions (RDS, Amazon MQ, S3, Cognito/Entra).
- Key values: image tags/digests, replicas, resources, ingress host, feature flags, queue names, LLM provider/model, budget limits, OIDC issuer/audience, object-store endpoint.
- Migration: Helm pre-upgrade hook Job runs Alembic as `aucoff_migrator` (database-spec section 7).
- `helm lint`, `helm template | kubeconform` and policy checks run in CI.

## 4. Kubernetes Baseline
- Namespaces: `aucoff` (app), `aucoff-data` (database, broker, object store), `aucoff-observability`, `aucoff-system` (ingress, cert-manager).
- **Pod Security**: `restricted` profile; `runAsNonRoot`, drop all capabilities, `seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault`, no privileged/hostPath.
- **NetworkPolicies**: default deny ingress and egress per namespace; explicit allows:
  - ingress controller -> frontend, backend
  - frontend -> backend
  - backend and agent services -> PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, MinIO, Keycloak (JWKS)
  - only agent services -> external internet (cloud/SaaS APIs, LLM provider) via egress rules/proxy
  - everything -> OpenTelemetry Collector
  - PostgreSQL reachable only from backend, agent services and the migration Job (DB-5, SEC-2)
- **RBAC**: dedicated ServiceAccounts per workload, least privilege, no cluster-admin; `automountServiceAccountToken: false` unless required.
- Resource requests/limits on every container; PodDisruptionBudgets for stateless services; HPA for scanners based on queue depth (KEDA - TODO) or CPU.
- Anti-affinity/topology spread for multi-replica services on AWS.

## 5. Configuration and Secrets
- ConfigMaps for non-secret config; Kubernetes Secrets for credentials (DB, RabbitMQ, MinIO, OIDC client secret, LLM API key, encryption keys). Secrets never committed; local secrets generated by a bootstrap script into the cluster (SEC-3).
- Per-tenant connector credentials are NOT stored in Helm secrets; they are referenced via `config_ref` and kept in the secret store (Kubernetes Secrets locally under a dedicated namespace/prefix; AWS Secrets Manager later).
- cert-manager issues TLS certificates (local CA now, ACM/Let's Encrypt later); in-cluster traffic TLS for DB and broker (mTLS between services is a TODO decision).
- Secret rotation procedure TODO; Gitleaks pre-commit stays enabled.

## 6. Local Workflow
Prerequisites: Docker, kind, kubectl, helm, make, (optional) k9s.
```
make cluster-up     # kind create cluster with ingress ports (config in deploy/kind/)
make images         # build images
make load           # kind load docker-image ...
make secrets        # generate local secrets
make deploy         # helm upgrade --install aucoff deploy/helm/aucoff -f values-local.yaml
make seed           # load synthetic seed data and framework catalogue
make e2e            # Playwright E2E against the cluster
make logs / make down / make cluster-down
```
- Access via ingress hostnames (e.g. `aucoff.localtest.me`, TODO) or `kubectl port-forward`.
- Target: cold start of the full stack on a 16 GB laptop in < 10 minutes (proposal); lightweight profile (`values-local-min.yaml`) disables observability and extra scanners.
- LLM calls: real provider key optional locally; default to a recorded/mock provider for tests (QA-8).

## 7. CI/CD (GitHub Actions)
| Stage | Checks |
|-------|--------|
| PR | Lint, type check, unit tests (QA-7), OpenAPI drift and lint ([api-contract.md](api-contract.md) section 2), generated client build, Gitleaks, dependency audit, license check |
| Build | Docker build, Trivy scan, SBOM, sign images (cosign - TODO) |
| Chart | `helm lint`, kubeconform, policy checks (Kyverno/conftest - TODO) |
| Integration/E2E | Ephemeral kind: deploy chart, run migrations, API tests, Playwright, axe, DAST/API scan |
| Release | Tag, publish images to registry (GHCR now, ECR later), publish chart |
| Deploy (Phase 2) | Terraform plan/apply with approval; Helm deploy to EKS |
Branch protection requires all checks; required reviews per constitution.

## 8. Observability
- OpenTelemetry SDKs in all services export traces, metrics, logs to the OpenTelemetry Collector.
- Backends: Prometheus (metrics), Loki (logs), Tempo (traces), Grafana (dashboards, alerts).
- Standard dashboards: API latency/errors, queue depth and DLQ, agent run duration/cost/tokens, scanner errors, DB health, SLO (NFR-3).
- Alerts: SLO burn rate, DLQ growth, budget exceeded, failed migrations, certificate expiry.
- Logs contain no secrets or PII (COD-8); retention TODO.

## 9. Backup and Recovery
- Local: scripted `pg_dump` and MinIO bucket export (database-spec section 11).
- AWS: RDS automated backups + PITR, S3 versioning, cross-region replication per residency rules; RPO/RTO from database-spec TODO.
- Restore drills documented and executed per phase.

## 10. AWS Migration Notes (Phase 2)
| Local | AWS equivalent | Notes |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| kind | EKS | Managed node groups; Pod Security and NetworkPolicy (VPC CNI or Cilium - TODO) |
| In-cluster PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector | RDS/Aurora PostgreSQL | Confirm 18.x and pgvector support ([database-spec.md](database-spec.md) section 12) |
| RabbitMQ | Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ (or self-managed) | Check engine version and DLQ setup |
| MinIO | S3 | KMS-encrypted buckets, per-region for residency |
| Keycloak | Entra ID / Cognito | OIDC issuer change only; SAML via IdP |
| K8s Secrets | Secrets Manager + External Secrets Operator | Rotation |
| cert-manager local CA | ACM + cert-manager (Let's Encrypt) | |
| NGINX ingress | ALB Ingress Controller / NLB | WAF in front (AWS WAF) |
| Prometheus/Grafana/Loki/Tempo | Amazon Managed Prometheus/Grafana + CloudWatch / or keep self-hosted | Decide on cost |
| GHCR | ECR | |
| Helm values | `values-aws.yaml` | Disable in-cluster data services |
| Manual | Terraform | Modules: network, eks, rds, mq, s3, iam (IRSA), secrets, observability; state in S3 + DynamoDB lock |
Scanners access customer accounts via customer-granted read-only roles (cross-account assume-role with external ID).

## 11. Security and Compliance
Controls referenced from constitution section 6: network policies, image scanning, non-root, RBAC least privilege, encryption in transit and at rest, audit logging of cluster changes (AWS CloudTrail/EKS audit later), no manual changes (ARC-11), dependency and SBOM tracking, regional deployment for data residency (SEC-14).

## 12. Open Questions
- [ ] Ingress controller choice; local hostnames.
- [ ] PostgreSQL deployment (StatefulSet vs CloudNativePG) and pgvector image.
- [ ] Queue autoscaling approach (KEDA).
- [ ] mTLS/service mesh need.
- [ ] Image registry and signing.
- [ ] Observability on AWS: managed vs self-hosted.
- [ ] Multi-region residency model and per-region deployments.

## 3. Orchestration
- Framework: LangGraph. The `assessment-orchestrator` builds a graph per assessment (plan -> fan-out scan/analysis nodes -> aggregate -> assess controls -> propose findings -> approval interrupt -> finalise).
- State and checkpoints persisted in PostgreSQL (checkpointer); runs are resumable after restart or approval.
- Human approval nodes use LangGraph interrupts; the run resumes only after a recorded decision in `approvals` (constitution AI-2).
- Scanner and analysis services run as separate microservices fed by RabbitMQ (see [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) sections 4 and 5); graph nodes publish jobs and await results.
- Retries/backoff and DLQs handled at the queue layer; node-level retries bounded; budgets (steps, time, tokens, cost) enforced per run (AI-12).
- Service roster and names: [spec.md](spec.md) section 5.6.

## 8. Spec-Driven Development Rules
new_string
## 7b. API Rules

Detail in [api-contract.md](api-contract.md).

| ID | Rule |
|----|------|
| API-1 | Every endpoint MUST be documented in the generated OpenAPI 3.1 spec (Swagger UI/ReDoc) with schemas, examples, errors and required scopes; undocumented routes MUST NOT merge. |
| API-2 | The committed OpenAPI file MUST match the generated one; CI fails on drift, and the frontend client is generated from it. |
| API-3 | Endpoints are versioned under `/api/v1`; breaking changes need a new major version and deprecation period. |
| API-4 | State-changing POSTs that create or trigger work MUST support `Idempotency-Key`; list endpoints MUST use cursor pagination. |
| API-5 | Errors use RFC 9457 problem details with a request ID and never expose internals. |
| API-6 | The OWASP Top 10 and OWASP API Security Top 10 are release gates (NFR-1). |

# Plan: finish design.md (architecture + UX/visual design)

## Context
design.md (v0.1.0) has architecture, components, data-model pointer, ADR-1..7 but still has TODO sections (system context, data flows, security architecture, observability, risks) and no UX/visual design. Owner wants it finished and wants closure on colour usage, page layout, and the information/metrics shown in the frontend. Owner stays in plan mode until they say go. After writing: align frontend-spec.md (link to design tokens/screens), spec.md metrics (if new ones), tasks.md, then commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

## design.md changes
1. Fill System Context (users/personas, IdP, LLM provider, evidence sources, ticketing, notifications) with Mermaid context diagram.
2. Key Data Flows: evidence ingestion -> analysis -> approval -> findings -> report (Mermaid sequence); assessment run via RabbitMQ/LangGraph; SSE progress.
3. Security Architecture: authN/authZ, tenancy, encryption, secrets, trust boundaries, LLM data boundary, threat model summary (STRIDE table) referencing constitution SEC/AI rules.
4. Observability summary + SLOs link to infrastructure-spec.
5. Trade-offs/risks and open questions (replace TODO).
6. NEW section "UX & Visual Design":
   - Design principles (number-first, evidence-first, trust through transparency, calm by default, accessible).
   - Colour tokens (CSS variables, light and dark): brand (deep blue 900-50 scale, blue, teal), neutrals (gray/slate), semantic status (pass, partial, fail, unknown, n/a, pending-approval in blue), severity scale (critical red, high orange/amber, medium yellow, low blue/teal, info gray), data-viz palette (colour-blind-safe categorical + sequential/diverging), chart rules; concrete hex values proposed with WCAG AA contrast checks for text/UI; usage rules (colour never sole indicator, status icons, max accent usage, gradients only on hero KPI cards).
   - Typography (e.g. Inter or Geist; scale; tabular numerals for KPIs), spacing (4/8 grid), radius, elevation, motion (durations, reduced-motion), iconography (Lucide), illustrations.
   - Layout & grid: app shell wireframes (ASCII), sidebar items by role, top bar, page header pattern, drawer pattern, breakpoints (desktop-first; tablet; mobile subset), density toggle.
   - Screen specs with wireframes and data shown: Executive/Posture dashboard (KPI strip, coverage by framework, severity trend vs last 2 scans, regional heatmap, approvals/agent activity, upcoming audits), Assessments, Control result review, Findings, Evidence, Reports, Audit log, Agent run timeline, Admin.
   - Metrics catalogue: table of each metric with ID (M-01...), definition/formula, data source (table/endpoint), chart type, refresh, drill-down, roles, thresholds/colour rules. Include: posture score, framework coverage %, pass/partial/fail distribution, control severity counts vs last 2 scans (delta arrows), open findings by severity + aging buckets, MTTR/remediation cycle time, time to audit readiness, evidence freshness, scan duration, agent citation correctness, avg confidence, reviewer override rate, LLM tokens/cost vs budget, pending approvals, jurisdiction coverage matrix.
   - Persona-to-dashboard mapping (executive, CISO, compliance officer, engineer, auditor, admin).
   - Empty/loading/error state patterns; AI content presentation (AiBadge, citations, confidence).
   - Accessibility: contrast, focus, keyboard, chart alternatives (data table toggle), reduced motion.
7. Update header version to 0.2.0, owner/date; Related links.

## Alignment edits
- frontend-spec.md: reference design.md tokens, layout and metrics catalogue; add chart library decision (proposal Recharts or visx) and dark-mode support; dashboard component list.
- api-contract.md: add dashboard/metrics endpoints (e.g. `/dashboards/posture`, `/metrics/{id}`, `/metrics/severity-trend?compare_last=2`) mapped to M- IDs.
- database-spec.md: add snapshot/rollup tables or materialised views for metric history (assessment snapshots, severity counts per assessment) so "compared to last 2 scans" is queryable.
- spec.md: success metrics reference M- IDs; tasks.md: design-system/dashboard tasks.

## Execution (after owner says go)
Exit plan mode, write/edit files, `git add specs`, commit with Co-Authored-By trailer, `git pull --rebase origin main`, `git push origin main`, then re-enter plan mode.

## Verification
- design.md has no TODO-only sections except marked open questions; metrics catalogue IDs unique and referenced from frontend-spec/api-contract.
- Hex colour pairs listed with computed contrast ratios >= 4.5:1 (text) / 3:1 (UI) in both themes.
- Mermaid/ASCII blocks well-formed; `git status` clean and push confirmed.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).
- database-spec.md: new `assessment_snapshots`, `severity_counts`/`metric_points` (tenant_id, metric_id, assessment_id, scope_id, framework_id, value, captured_at), monthly partitions, retention row (>= 13 months, tenant-configurable up, never below 12), RLS, backup coverage; ensure results of deleted evidence keep metadata so history stays comparable.
- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

# AUCoFF Agent Spec

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Status | Draft |
| Version | 0.2.0 |
| Owner | Praveen Darshanam |
| Last updated | 2026-10-18 |

> Purpose: defines the agentic AI layer: roles, orchestration, models, tools, knowledge, guardrails, human approvals and evaluation. All agents obey constitution section 7 (AI-1 to AI-16).

Related: [constitution.md](constitution.md) · [spec.md](spec.md) · [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) · [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) · [api-contract.md](api-contract.md) · [design.md](design.md)

## 1. Overview and Principles
- AUCoFF runs 13 agents as Python microservices fed by RabbitMQ and orchestrated with LangGraph (ADR-3, ADR-4).
- **Deterministic first:** scanners run policy-as-code checks that produce facts (pass/fail with raw evidence). LLMs interpret, map, explain, summarise documents and draft text. LLMs never decide whether a configuration value is compliant when a deterministic rule exists.
- **Read-only:** no agent changes customer systems (spec.md 5.5, AI-1, AI-6).
- **Advisory with approval:** consequential outputs need human approval (AI-2). Outputs leaving the tenant need approval and redaction (AI-16).
- **Grounded:** every claim cites evidence or source text (AI-3); no evidence means `unknown`, not a guess (AI-4).
- **Tenant-isolated:** retrieval and tools are always tenant-scoped (DB-3, DB-6).

## 2. Agent Roster
Autonomy levels: **A0** deterministic, no LLM; **A1** LLM drafts, human decides; **A2** LLM acts inside bounded, reversible, internal steps (no external effects).

| ID | Agent (service) | Responsibility | Trigger / queue | Model tier | Autonomy | Approval gate | Refs |
|----|-----------------|----------------|-----------------|-----------|----------|---------------|------|
| AG-1 | `assessment-orchestrator` | Plans assessment graph, fans out scans, aggregates control results, requests review | `assessment.requested` | Strong (planning only) | A2 | Result finalisation | FR-3, FR-7 |
| AG-2 | `mapping-agent` | Proposes requirement-to-unified-control mappings with rationale | `mapping.requested` | Strong | A1 | Mapping approval | FR-2 |
| AG-3 | `cloud-scanner` | AWS/GCP/Azure read-only checks and evidence | `scan.cloud` | None for checks; small for summarising | A0/A2 | - | FR-6 |
| AG-4 | `k8s-scanner` | Kubernetes, Helm, RBAC, image checks | `scan.k8s` | Small | A0/A2 | - | FR-6 |
| AG-5 | `repo-scanner` | GitHub/Bitbucket and CI/CD checks | `scan.repo` | Small | A0/A2 | - | FR-6 |
| AG-6 | `saas-scanner` | Entra ID and Metabase checks | `scan.saas` | Small | A0/A2 | - | FR-6 |
| AG-7 | `document-analyzer` | Parse, chunk, embed and assess uploaded documents | `analysis.document` | Small (extraction) + Strong (assessment) | A1 | Result finalisation | FR-5, FR-7 |
| AG-8 | `remediation-advisor` | Drafts findings and advisory remediation | `finding.requested` | Strong | A1 | Risk acceptance, ticket creation | FR-8, FR-9 |
| AG-9 | `report-generator` | Builds cited reports and evidence packs | `report.requested` | Strong | A1 | Report publish | FR-12 |
| AG-10 | `reviewer-agent` | Independent second pass: checks citations resolve, claims match evidence, flags contradictions and low confidence before human review | `review.requested` | Strong (different prompt; different model where possible) | A2 | - (advisory to human) | AI-3, AI-9 |
| AG-11 | `regulatory-change-agent` | Monitors allow-listed official sources, diffs new regulation/standard versions, proposes catalogue and mapping changes | scheduled; `regchange.scan` | Strong | A1 | Catalogue/mapping change approval | FR-1, FR-2 |
| AG-12 | `copilot-agent` | Answers user questions about posture, controls, findings with citations; navigates the UI; no state changes | HTTP/SSE via gateway | Strong | A1 | - (read-only) | US-8 |
| AG-13 | `questionnaire-agent` | Drafts answers to customer due-diligence questionnaires from the answer library and live evidence | `questionnaire.requested` | Strong (answers) + Small (parsing/classification) | A1 | Answer approval; export approval | US-14 to US-17, FR-16 to FR-20 |

Agents AG-10 to AG-13 are new relative to the original service list in spec.md; see [spec.md](spec.md) section 5.6.

## 3. Orchestration (LangGraph)
- One graph per workflow, run by the owning service; state persisted with the Postgres checkpointer (`app` schema, tenant-scoped).
- Graphs:
  1. **Assessment**: plan -> fan-out scan/analysis nodes -> collect evidence -> deterministic checks -> LLM interpretation -> aggregate -> reviewer-agent -> **approval interrupt** -> finalise -> findings -> snapshot.
  2. **Mapping**: select requirements -> propose mappings -> reviewer-agent -> **approval interrupt** -> persist.
  3. **Questionnaire**: see section 10.
  4. **Regulatory change**: fetch source -> detect change -> diff -> impact analysis (affected mappings/controls) -> proposal -> **approval interrupt**.
  5. **Report**: gather approved results -> compose -> citation check -> **approval interrupt** -> render.
  6. **Copilot**: retrieve (tenant-scoped) -> answer with citations -> refuse if no grounding.
- **State** (all graphs): `tenant_id`, `agent_run_id`, `idempotency_key`, `inputs_ref`, `evidence_refs[]`, `intermediate[]`, `budget{tokens,usd,steps,deadline}`, `status`, `approvals[]`.
- **Interrupts:** a run pauses at approval nodes and resumes only when `approvals` has a decision (AI-2). Approvals expire after 7 days: the item returns to the queue and the approver is notified; nothing auto-approves.
- **Retries:** queue-level retry with exponential backoff and DLQ; node-level retries bounded (default 2); failures degrade to `unknown` with reason, never silent skips.
- **Concurrency:** fan-out limited per tenant and per provider API (TODO limits).
- **Cancellation and kill switch:** per run and per tenant (AI-12).

## 4. Model Strategy
| Tier | Used for | Default (provider-agnostic; configurable) | Notes |
|------|----------|-------------------------------------------|-------|
| Strong | Assessment interpretation, mapping, remediation, report text, questionnaire answers, reviewer, copilot, regulatory analysis | Anthropic Claude (strongest available model; ID in config) | Lower temperature; structured outputs |
| Small | Extraction, classification, routing, question parsing, summarising evidence | Anthropic Claude (small/fast model; ID in config) | Cheap, high volume |
| Embeddings | Retrieval | Provider-agnostic embedding interface; model and dimension decided at build | Dimension fixed per index (database-spec §3.4) |

- All calls go through the `LLMProvider` interface (ARC-5); model IDs, versions and parameters live in configuration and are recorded per run (AI-10).
- Routing: deterministic rules by task type; escalate small -> strong when confidence below threshold or schema validation fails twice.
- Reviewer uses a different prompt and, where available, a different model from the producer to reduce correlated errors.
- Parameters: temperature <= 0.2 for assessments and answers (TODO tune); max tokens per node; prompt caching where supported.
- Fallback: secondary provider/model on outage (TODO choice), else degrade to manual workflow (AI-15).
- **Budgets:** USD 25 cap per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, configurable tenant monthly cap; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (`budget_exceeded`) (AI-12, NFR-8). Step, time and token budgets also per run.

## 5. Tools
All tools are allow-listed per agent, tenant-scoped, rate-limited and audit-logged (AI-6).

| Tool | Description | Access | Side effects | Agents | Approval |
|------|-------------|--------|--------------|--------|----------|
| `cloud.read` | Read-only AWS/GCP/Azure config APIs | Read | None | AG-3 | No |
| `k8s.read` | Read cluster/manifest/RBAC/image data | Read | None | AG-4 | No |
| `repo.read` | GitHub/Bitbucket settings, branch protection, CI config, scan results | Read | None | AG-5 | No |
| `saas.read` | Entra ID, Metabase configuration | Read | None | AG-6 | No |
| `evidence.store` | Write evidence (hash, provenance) to object store + DB | Write (internal) | Creates evidence rows | scanners, AG-7 | No |
| `evidence.read` | Read evidence for tenant | Read | None | most | No |
| `vector.search` | Hybrid search (pgvector + full-text) with reranking, always tenant-filtered | Read | None | AG-1, 2, 7, 8, 10, 12, 13 | No |
| `catalog.read` | Frameworks, requirements, unified controls | Read | None | most | No |
| `results.propose` | Create proposed control results/findings/mappings (status `proposed`) | Write (internal) | Creates proposals | AG-1, 2, 7, 8, 11 | Finalisation needs human |
| `doc.parse` | Parse PDF/DOCX/XLSX into text/structure | Read | None | AG-7, AG-13 | No |
| `answerlib.read` / `answerlib.propose` | Read approved answers; propose new library entries | Read / internal write | Proposal only | AG-13 | Library entry approval |
| `ticket.create` | Jira/ServiceNow ticket for a finding | Write (external) | Creates ticket | AG-8 (via gateway) | Yes |
| `notify.send` | Email/Slack/Teams notification | Write (external) | Message sent | gateway | No (configured events) |
| `web.fetch` | Fetch from allow-listed official regulatory sources | Read (external) | None | AG-11 | No (allow-list only) |
| `export.render` | Produce Excel/Word/PDF output | Internal | Creates file | AG-9, AG-13 | Export approval |
No tool performs writes against customer systems.

## 6. Knowledge and Memory
| Source | Scope | Contents | Notes |
|--------|-------|----------|-------|
| Framework/regulation texts and unified controls | Shared, read-only | Requirement text or summaries, control descriptions | Subject to licensing (spec.md R-2) |
| Tenant documents | Tenant | Policies, SOPs, audit reports | Isolated embeddings (DB-6) |
| Evidence summaries and prior results | Tenant | Summaries of collected evidence, past assessments, 12-month history snapshots | For consistency and trend context |
| Remediation playbooks / best practices | Shared or tenant | Curated guidance | Versioned |
| Answer library | Tenant | Approved questionnaire answers with source questions, evidence, approval, freshness | See section 10 |

- Chunking: structure-aware (headings/clauses/tables); chunk size and overlap TODO tune; each chunk keeps source, locator and version.
- Retrieval: hybrid (vector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; top-k and score thresholds TODO; tenant filter mandatory.
- Citation format: `{source_type, source_id, locator, excerpt, version}`; citations are resolved and verified by code (section 8).
- Freshness: evidence and answers carry timestamps; staleness thresholds per evidence type (TODO defaults, proposal 30 days for configuration evidence, 12 months for policy documents).
- Memory: short-term = graph state; long-term = database (results, snapshots, answer library). No free-form agent memory outside governed tables.
- Answer library lifecycle: `draft -> approved -> stale -> retired`; stale when underlying evidence changed or age threshold passed; retired entries not used for new answers.

## 7. Prompts
- Stored in `backend/services/<agent>/prompts/` as versioned templates; semantic version per prompt; every run records `prompt_version` (AI-10).
- Structure: system role and rules; task; schema for output; retrieved sources inside clearly delimited data blocks marked untrusted (AI-7).
- Changes go through PR with evaluation results (AI-11); no prompts edited in production.
- No secrets or PII in prompts beyond what redaction permits (AI-8).

## 8. Guardrails
| Layer | Control |
|-------|---------|
| Input | Validate sizes/types; strip hidden text/markup; detect prompt-injection patterns; treat all documents, evidence and questionnaire content as data, never instructions (AI-7) |
| Redaction | PII and secrets detected and replaced with tokens before any LLM call; reversible mapping kept server-side; redaction recall gate >= 99% |
| Tool use | Allow-list per agent; schema-validated arguments; tenant ID injected by runtime, never from model output; no tool calls that originate solely from document content without validation |
| Output | Pydantic schemas; retry/repair within limits then escalate (AI-5) |
| Citations | Citation validator: every claim must reference an existing evidence/source ID in the tenant scope, and excerpt must match source; uncited or unresolved claims are dropped or marked `unverified` (AI-3, AI-4) |
| Confidence | Model-reported plus rule-based signals (evidence freshness, coverage, reviewer disagreement); below threshold -> human queue (AI-9) |
| Disallowed | Legal conclusions or certifications, changing customer systems, exporting data outside the tenant without approval, answering from another tenant's data |
| Rate/budget | Per run and per tenant budgets, rate limits, loop detection (AI-12) |
| Egress | LLM calls only to approved providers and regions (SEC-14) |

## 9. Human-in-the-Loop Matrix
| Action | Trigger | Approver role | Timeout / default |
|--------|---------|---------------|-------------------|
| Finalise control result | Assessment graph reaches review | compliance_officer, ciso | 7 days, then back to queue + reminder; never auto-approved |
| Approve requirement-to-control mapping | Mapping or regulatory-change proposal | compliance_officer, ciso | Same |
| Accept risk on a finding | User request | ciso | Same |
| Create external ticket | User action on finding | compliance_officer, engineer | Same |
| Publish / download final report | Report graph | compliance_officer, ciso | Same |
| Approve questionnaire answer (per answer or batch) | Draft ready | compliance_officer, ciso | Same |
| Approve questionnaire export | After all selected answers approved | compliance_officer, ciso | Same |
| Apply regulatory catalogue change | Regulatory-change proposal | compliance_officer, ciso | Same |
| Add/replace answer-library entry | Approved answer | compliance_officer | Same |
Approvals record approver, time, decision and comment in `approvals` and the audit log (SEC-9).

## 10. Questionnaire Agent (AG-13) Workflow
Supports: uploaded Excel/Word/PDF questionnaires; standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA); link/portal questionnaires (answers drafted for manual entry; **no auto-submission**); reuse of approved prior answers.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant G as Gateway
  participant Q as questionnaire-agent
  participant L as Answer library
  participant S as Scanners
  participant R as reviewer-agent
  U->>G: Upload or paste questionnaire
  G->>Q: questionnaire.requested
  Q->>Q: Parse, normalise questions, classify, map to unified controls
  Q->>L: Look up approved answers (fresh?)
  alt answer fresh and matching
    L-->>Q: Reuse with citations
  else stale or missing
    Q->>S: Request read-only evidence / re-scan
    S-->>Q: Fresh evidence + timestamps
    Q->>Q: Draft answer with confidence and citations
  end
  Q->>R: Verify citations and consistency
  R-->>Q: Pass / flags
  Q->>G: Drafts ready (awaiting approval)
  U->>G: Approve / edit / reject per answer or batch
  G->>Q: Resume with decisions
  Q->>Q: Redact sensitive details, render output
  U->>G: Approve export
  G-->>U: Download approved answers
  Q->>L: Propose library entries
```
Rules:
- Answer order of preference: approved fresh library answer; fresh scan evidence; stale evidence triggers a read-only re-scan; if still insufficient the answer is `needs input` (never invented).
- Each answer shows: text, confidence, citations (evidence IDs and timestamps), source (library vs live), reviewer-agent flags, redaction summary.
- **Redaction by default:** account IDs, resource IDs, IP addresses, internal hostnames, employee names/emails, secrets. Tenant-configurable "shareable detail level" (minimal, standard, detailed); reviewer can override per answer with a reason.
- Only approved answers are exported; each export is audit-logged (who, what, when, format, recipient label).
- Answers copied into the library only after approval; library entries link to evidence and expire on staleness.
- Questionnaire documents are untrusted input (AI-7); the same guardrails apply.
- Data model (see [database-spec.md](database-spec.md)): `questionnaires`, `questionnaire_questions`, `questionnaire_answers`, `answer_library`.

## 11. Evaluation
| Area | Dataset | Metric | Initial gate |
|------|---------|--------|--------------|
| Control results | Golden evidence + expected results per framework | Agreement with reviewer judgement | >= 90% |
| Citations | All outputs | Citation correctness (citation resolves and supports claim) | >= 98% |
| Hallucination | Adversarial and sparse-evidence cases | Hallucinated/unsupported claims | <= 1% |
| Redaction | Seeded PII/secret corpus | Redaction recall | >= 99% |
| Mapping | Expert-labelled mappings | Precision/recall (TODO targets) | TODO |
| Questionnaire | Past answered questionnaires | Answer accuracy vs approved answers; reuse correctness; needs-input recall | TODO targets |
| Reviewer override | Production | Human override rate (monitor, no gate) | Track |
| Security | Prompt-injection and exfiltration suite | Attack success rate | 0 critical |
- Gates run in CI on prompt, model or agent-code changes; failures block merge (AI-11, QA-6).
- LLM calls in CI are recorded/replayed or mocked for determinism (QA-8); periodic live evaluation on schedule.
- Human feedback (approvals, edits, rejects) feeds new golden cases after review.
- Thresholds are initial and tunable by owner; changes recorded in this document.

## 12. Audit Logging and Traceability
Each run writes `agent_runs` and `agent_steps` ([database-spec.md](database-spec.md)): agent, model and version, prompt version, redacted inputs, retrieved source IDs, tool calls and results, outputs, tokens, cost, timings, approvals. Security-relevant events (approvals, exports, budget stops, guardrail blocks) also go to the immutable `audit_log` (AI-10, SEC-9). Retention per database-spec section 9.

## 13. Failure Handling and Degradation
| Failure | Behaviour |
|---------|-----------|
| LLM timeout/outage | Retry with backoff, fallback model if configured, else mark steps `failed`, keep deterministic results, notify; manual workflow remains (AI-15) |
| Invalid structured output | Repair retry (<= 2), escalate model tier, then human queue |
| Scanner/API failure or missing permission | Result `unknown` with reason; never treated as pass |
| Budget exceeded | Stop run (`budget_exceeded`), keep partial results, alert |
| Guardrail violation | Block output, log, flag for review |
| Poison message | DLQ + alert |
| Kill switch | Admin can stop a run or disable an agent per tenant |

## 14. Agent Threat Model
| Threat | Mitigation |
|--------|-----------|
| Prompt injection via documents, evidence or questionnaires | Data/instruction separation, input sanitising, no tool calls driven by content without validation, injection test suite |
| Data exfiltration through answers or exports | Redaction by default, approval before export, export audit, tenant-configurable detail level |
| Cross-tenant leakage via retrieval | Mandatory tenant filter + RLS, tenant tests (DB-6), per-tenant caches only |
| Over-privileged tools or credentials | Read-only scoped credentials, per-agent allow-lists, secret references only |
| Hallucinated compliance claims | Citation validator, reviewer-agent, confidence routing, evaluation gate |
| Cost abuse / runaway loops | Budgets, step limits, rate limits, kill switch |
| Poisoned answer library | Only approved entries, staleness, provenance links, retire workflow |
| Malicious regulatory source content | Allow-list of official sources, diffs reviewed by humans, no auto-apply |
| Model/provider data retention | Approved providers only, data class rules, region pinning (SEC-14) |

## 15. Open Questions
- [ ] Final model IDs per tier and fallback provider.
- [ ] Embedding model and dimension; reranker choice.
- [ ] Staleness thresholds per evidence type.
- [ ] Targets for mapping and questionnaire evaluation metrics.
- [ ] Allow-listed regulatory sources per jurisdiction.
- [ ] Questionnaire template licensing/format details (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA).
- [ ] Concurrency limits per tenant and provider.
- [ ] Redaction tooling (library vs model-based) and entity list.

# Plan: finish design.md (architecture + UX/visual design)

## Context
design.md (v0.1.0) has architecture, components, data-model pointer, ADR-1..7 but still has TODO sections (system context, data flows, security architecture, observability, risks) and no UX/visual design. Owner wants it finished and wants closure on colour usage, page layout, and the information/metrics shown in the frontend. Owner stays in plan mode until they say go. After writing: align frontend-spec.md (link to design tokens/screens), spec.md metrics (if new ones), tasks.md, then commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

def L(h):
    h=h.lstrip('#'); r,g,b=[int(h[i:i+2],16)/255 for i in (0,2,4)]
    f=lambda c: c/12.92 if c<=0.03928 else ((c+0.055)/1.055)**2.4
    return 0.2126*f(r)+0.7152*f(g)+0.0722*f(b)
def cr(a,b):
