# AUCoFF Design

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Status | Draft |
| Version | 0.2.0 |
| Owner | Praveen Darshanam |
| Last updated | 2026-10-19 |

> Purpose: system architecture, key technical decisions, and the UX and visual design (colour, layout, information and metrics) that satisfy [spec.md](spec.md) within [constitution.md](constitution.md).

Related: [frontend-spec.md](frontend-spec.md) · [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) · [agent.md](agent.md) · [api-contract.md](api-contract.md) · [infrastructure-spec.md](infrastructure-spec.md) · [database-spec.md](database-spec.md)

## 1. System Context
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Users
    CO[Compliance officer] & AU[Auditor] & EN[Engineer] & EX[Executive / CISO] & AD[Tenant admin]
  end
  Users --> AUCOFF[AUCoFF SaaS]
  AUCOFF -->|read-only| CLOUD[AWS / GCP / Azure]
  AUCOFF -->|read-only| K8S[Kubernetes / containers]
  AUCOFF -->|read-only| REPOS[GitHub / Bitbucket / CI]
  AUCOFF -->|read-only| SAAS[Entra ID / Metabase]
  AUCOFF --> LLM[LLM provider - Claude default]
  AUCOFF <--> IDP[Identity provider - OIDC/SAML]
  AUCOFF --> TICKET[Jira / ServiceNow]
  AUCOFF --> NOTIFY[Email / Slack / Teams]
  AUCOFF -->|allow-listed fetch| REG[Official regulatory sources]
  CUST[Customers' due-diligence questionnaires] --> AUCOFF
```
Trust boundaries: (1) browser/user, (2) AUCoFF platform, (3) customer environments (read-only), (4) LLM provider (redacted data only), (5) external recipients of exports (approved, redacted data only).

## 2. Architecture Overview
Next.js frontend (BFF session) -> FastAPI gateway -> PostgreSQL (+ pgvector) and RabbitMQ -> Python agent microservices (LangGraph) -> read-only external sources, object store and LLM provider. Diagram in [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) section 2; deployment topology in [infrastructure-spec.md](infrastructure-spec.md).

## 3. Components
| Component | Responsibility | Tech | Spec |
|-----------|----------------|------|------|
| Web UI | Dashboards, review and approval workflows | Next.js | [frontend-spec.md](frontend-spec.md) |
| API | REST gateway, auth, RBAC, SSE | FastAPI | [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) |
| Agent runtime | 13 agents / microservices, LangGraph graphs | Python, LangGraph | [agent.md](agent.md) |
| Relational DB + vector store | System of record, RLS tenancy, embeddings, history snapshots | PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector | [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) |
| Queue | Job and event transport | RabbitMQ (AWS: Amazon MQ) | [backend-spec.md](backend-spec.md) §5 |
| Object store | Evidence files, reports, exports | MinIO locally, S3 on AWS | [infrastructure-spec.md](infrastructure-spec.md) |
| Identity provider | OIDC login, SAML brokering | Keycloak locally; Entra ID/Cognito later | [frontend-spec.md](frontend-spec.md) §5 |
| Observability | Logs, metrics, traces | OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo | [infrastructure-spec.md](infrastructure-spec.md) §8 |

## 4. Data Model
Defined in [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) sections 3 to 5 (tables, ER diagram, indexes). Design-level decisions:
- Single database; tenant isolation by `tenant_id` + Row-Level Security.
- Append-only audit and agent-step tables with hash-chained audit rows.
- Embeddings stored in PostgreSQL via `pgvector`.
- **History:** each completed assessment writes an immutable snapshot and metric points; at least 12 months (stored 13) of history are queryable for any-to-any scan comparison (section 12; [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) section 3.6).

## 5. Key Data Flows
### 5.1 Assessment run
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant API as FastAPI
  participant MQ as RabbitMQ
  participant O as Orchestrator (LangGraph)
  participant S as Scanners
  participant DB as PostgreSQL
  U->>API: POST /assessments
  API->>DB: assessment + outbox (one transaction)
  API-->>U: 202 + run id
  DB-->>MQ: outbox relay publishes assessment.requested
  MQ->>O: assessment.requested
  O->>MQ: scan.* jobs
  MQ->>S: scan jobs (read-only)
  S->>DB: evidence + check results
  S-->>O: done
  O->>O: LLM interpretation, reviewer-agent
  O->>DB: proposed control results, awaiting_approval
  API-->>U: SSE progress events
  U->>API: approve control results
  API->>DB: approvals + audit log
  O->>DB: finalise, findings, snapshot + metric points
```
### 5.2 Evidence to report
Evidence collected/uploaded -> hashed and stored -> checks/analysis -> proposed results with citations -> reviewer-agent -> human approval -> findings and remediation advice -> snapshot (history) -> report generation -> approval -> download.
### 5.3 Questionnaire
Detailed in [agent.md](agent.md) section 10.
### 5.4 Progress streaming
Services publish run events to RabbitMQ; the gateway relays them to the browser via SSE ([api-contract.md](api-contract.md) section 6).

## 6. Security Architecture
- **AuthN/AuthZ:** external OIDC IdP; JWT validated by the API; BFF session cookie for the browser; RBAC enforced in domain code (SEC-1).
- **Tenancy:** `tenant_id` + forced RLS; tenant context set per transaction; tenant-filtered vector queries (SEC-11, DB-3, DB-6).
- **Data protection:** TLS everywhere; encryption at rest; column-level encryption for restricted fields; classification and retention in [database-spec.md](database-spec.md) (SEC-4, SEC-5).
- **Secrets:** Kubernetes Secrets locally, Secrets Manager on AWS; connector credentials only by reference (SEC-3).
- **LLM data boundary:** only redacted data to approved providers/regions (AI-8, SEC-14).
- **Outputs leaving the tenant:** approved, redacted, audit-logged (AI-16).
- **Network:** default-deny NetworkPolicies; DB reachable only from backend/agents ([infrastructure-spec.md](infrastructure-spec.md) §4).
- **Supply chain:** pinned dependencies, SBOM, image scanning, secret scanning (COD-7, SEC-8).

### Threat model summary (STRIDE)
| Threat | Example | Mitigation |
|--------|---------|-----------|
| Spoofing | Forged token, stolen session | OIDC validation, short-lived tokens, httpOnly cookies, MFA at IdP |
| Tampering | Edit audit trail or evidence | Append-only audit with hash chain, evidence SHA-256, immutable snapshots |
| Repudiation | Denied approval | Approvals with actor/time in audit log |
| Information disclosure | Cross-tenant read, prompt/export leak | RLS, tenant-filtered retrieval, redaction, export approval |
| Denial of service | Runaway scans/LLM spend | Rate limits, budgets, kill switch, queue backpressure |
| Elevation of privilege | Over-broad connector or role | Read-only scoped credentials, RBAC matrix, least privilege roles |
| Prompt injection | Malicious document content | Data/instruction separation, validation, injection tests ([agent.md](agent.md) §8, §14) |

## 7. Observability
Logs, metrics, traces via OpenTelemetry into Loki, Prometheus and Tempo, shown in Grafana; SLOs from NFR-3/NFR-4 with burn-rate alerts ([infrastructure-spec.md](infrastructure-spec.md) §8). Product-level metrics shown to users are defined in section 11 and are separate from operational telemetry.

## 8. Decision Log (ADRs)
| ID | Decision | Alternatives | Rationale | Status |
|----|----------|--------------|-----------|--------|
| ADR-1 | PostgreSQL 18.6 with pgvector as the single data store (relational + vectors) | Separate vector DB (e.g. Qdrant), MySQL | One engine to secure and operate; RLS for multi-tenancy; maps to RDS/Aurora | Accepted (owner) |
| ADR-2 | Multi-tenant SaaS with RLS isolation | Single-tenant per deployment | Required by [spec.md](spec.md) section 5.4 | Accepted (owner) |
| ADR-3 | LangGraph for agent orchestration with Postgres checkpoints | Claude Agent SDK/plain loops, Temporal | Graph state, interrupts for human approval | Accepted (owner) |
| ADR-4 | FastAPI gateway + Python agent services over RabbitMQ | Sync gRPC/HTTP, modular monolith | Decouples long-running scans; retries and DLQs | Accepted (owner) |
| ADR-5 | External OIDC IdP (Keycloak locally) with BFF session in Next.js | Built-in auth, SaaS auth | Enterprise SSO/SAML, no tokens in browser storage | Accepted (owner) |
| ADR-6 | OpenAPI 3.1 as source of truth; generated TS client; Swagger UI for all endpoints | Hand-written clients | Prevents contract drift | Accepted (owner) |
| ADR-7 | kind + umbrella Helm chart locally; Terraform + EKS later | minikube, per-service charts | Same chart across environments | Accepted (owner) |
| ADR-8 | Immutable per-assessment snapshots + metric points for 12-month history, rollups for trends | Recompute from live data | Reproducible comparisons independent of later data changes | Proposed |
| ADR-9 | Light-default theme with dark mode, token-based design system (shadcn/ui + Tailwind) | Single theme, other UI kits | Owner choice; accessibility and consistency | Accepted (owner) |

## 9. Trade-offs and Risks
- Single PostgreSQL for relational, vector and history data simplifies operations but concentrates load; mitigate with partitioning, read replicas and PgBouncer when needed.
- Doing all frameworks in v1 is a scope risk (spec.md R-1); internal milestones in [tasks.md](tasks.md).
- LLM-dependent features (interpretation, questionnaires) add cost and variability; mitigated by deterministic-first checks, budgets and evaluation gates.
- Storing snapshots for 13 months increases storage; mitigated by compact metric points and partition dropping.
- Hybrid RAG quality depends on embedding choice, deferred to build.

## 10. UX and Visual Design

### 10.1 Principles
1. **Number-first:** every screen leads with quantified, comparable data; narrative comes second.
2. **Evidence-first:** any claim is one click from its source and timestamp.
3. **Trust through transparency:** AI output is labelled, cited, and shows confidence and approval state.
4. **Calm by default:** quiet neutral canvas; colour is reserved for meaning (status, severity, action).
5. **Accessible and inclusive:** WCAG 2.2 AA; colour is never the only signal.
6. **Professional with personality:** modern, friendly (Gen-Z) touches that never reduce clarity.

### 10.2 Colour system
Implemented as CSS variables (Tailwind theme tokens); light is the default and dark mode follows `prefers-color-scheme` with a user override. Contrast ratios below were computed against the stated backgrounds (WCAG 2.2: text >= 4.5:1, UI components >= 3:1).

**Surfaces and text**
| Token | Light | Dark |
|-------|-------|------|
| `bg` | `#FFFFFF` | `#0B1220` |
| `surface` (cards) | `#F8FAFC` | `#111A2E` |
| `border-subtle` (decorative) | `#E2E8F0` | `#1E293B` |
| `border-control` (inputs, focusable UI) | `#64748B` (4.76:1 on `bg`) | `#64748B` (3.93:1 on `bg`) |
| `text` | `#0F172A` (17.85:1) | `#E5E7EB` (15.12:1) |
| `text-muted` | `#475569` (7.58:1) | `#9CA3AF` (7.37:1) |

**Brand and accent**
| Token | Light | Dark | Use |
|-------|-------|------|-----|
| `brand-deep` | `#0B2A6F` (13.33:1; white text on it 13.33:1) | `#93C5FD` | Sidebar, headings accents, hero KPI backgrounds |
| `brand` (blue) | `#1D4ED8` (6.70:1; white text on it 6.70:1) | `#60A5FA` (7.36:1) | Primary buttons, links, focus ring |
| `accent-teal` | `#0F766E` (5.47:1; white text 5.47:1) | `#2DD4BF` (10.06:1) | Secondary actions, highlights, positive-neutral accents |
| `highlight-yellow` | `#FACC15` (fill only; use `#854D0E` text on it, 6.85:1 on white) | `#FACC15` | Callouts, "new" badges |

Brand scale for hover/pressed/tint states: deep blue 900 `#0B2A6F`, 700 `#123C99`, 600 `#1D4ED8`, 100 `#DBEAFE`, 50 `#EFF6FF` (tints are fills only).

**Compliance status (always icon + label + colour)**
| Status | Icon | Light text/icon | Dark text/icon | Tint fill (light / dark) |
|--------|------|-----------------|----------------|--------------------------|
| Pass | check-circle | `#15803D` (5.02:1) | `#4ADE80` (10.74:1) | `#DCFCE7` / `#052E16` |
| Partial | alert-triangle | `#B45309` (5.02:1) | `#FBBF24` (11.22:1) | `#FEF3C7` / `#422006` |
| Fail | x-circle | `#B91C1C` (6.47:1) | `#F87171` (6.77:1) | `#FEE2E2` / `#450A0A` |
| Unknown | help-circle | `#4B5563` (7.56:1) | `#9CA3AF` (7.37:1) | `#F3F4F6` / `#1F2937` |
| Not applicable | minus-circle | `#475569` (7.58:1) | `#94A3B8` (7.30:1) | `#F1F5F9` / `#1E293B` |
| Awaiting approval | clock | `#1D4ED8` (6.70:1) | `#60A5FA` (7.36:1) | `#DBEAFE` / `#172554` |

**Severity (findings and failing controls)**
| Severity | Light | Dark | Icon/shape |
|----------|-------|------|------------|
| Critical | `#B91C1C` (6.47:1) | `#F87171` (6.77:1) | double-chevron up |
| High | `#C2410C` (5.18:1) | `#FB923C` (8.27:1) | chevron up |
| Medium | `#A16207` (4.92:1) | `#FACC15` (12.23:1) | dash |
| Low | `#0369A1` (5.93:1) | `#38BDF8` (8.74:1) | chevron down |
| Info | `#4B5563` (7.56:1) | `#9CA3AF` (7.37:1) | info |
Severity order is also encoded by icon shape and label, so Critical vs High is distinguishable without colour.

**Data-visualisation palette** (colour-blind-safe categorical, used for frameworks/series, max 8): `#1D4ED8` blue, `#0F766E` teal, `#B45309` amber, `#7C3AED` violet, `#BE185D` magenta, `#4B5563` grey, `#0369A1` sky, `#65A30D` lime; dark mode uses the same hues lightened (+2 steps). Sequential scale for coverage/heatmaps: blue tints `#EFF6FF` -> `#1D4ED8`; diverging for deltas: red (worse) <-> neutral <-> green (better) with arrows and +/- text. Status colours are used in charts only for status/severity data, never for arbitrary series.

**Usage rules**
- Colour never carries meaning alone: pair with icon, label or pattern (stripes for fail in print/greyscale).
- Gradients and glass/blur are allowed only on hero KPI cards (brand-deep to blue at low angle, text white >= 4.5:1).
- One primary action per view in `brand`; destructive actions in `fail` red with confirmation.
- Focus ring: 2 px `brand` with 2 px offset, visible in both themes.
- Do not use yellow for text; use `#854D0E` text on yellow fill.
- Hex values are a starting proposal and live in one tokens file; any change re-runs the contrast check.

### 10.3 Typography, shape and motion
- **Font:** Inter (UI) with system fallback; tabular numerals for all metrics and tables; large bold numerals for KPIs (32-48 px).
- **Scale (px):** 12 caption, 14 body/table, 16 default, 20 section title, 24 page title, 32-48 KPI.
- **Spacing:** 4 px base grid (4/8/12/16/24/32/48).
- **Shape and depth:** radius 8 px (controls), 12 px (cards, dialogs); soft shadows (`0 1px 2px` and `0 8px 24px` at low opacity); generous whitespace; 1 px subtle borders.
- **Icons:** Lucide, 16/20 px, stroke 1.75.
- **Motion:** 120-200 ms ease-out micro-interactions (hover lift, count-up for KPIs, progress shimmer, check-mark pop on approval); all motion disabled or reduced under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Empty states:** friendly line illustrations (monochrome with a brand accent) with a clear next action.
- **Voice:** concise, plain, supportive; avoids jargon where possible.

### 10.4 Layout
App shell:
```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
| TOP BAR: [Tenant v]  [ Search (Ctrl+K) ........ ]  [Bell] [Theme] [User v] |
+-----------+------------------------------------------------------+
| SIDEBAR   | Breadcrumbs                                          |
| (collaps- | Page title ........................ [Primary action]  |
|  ible)    | [Filters / time range / framework / jurisdiction]    |
| Dashboard | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Assess-   |  CONTENT (cards / tables / charts)        | DRAWER   |
|  ments    |                                           | (detail, |
| Controls  |                                           |  evidence|
| Findings  |                                           |  citation)|
| Evidence  |                                           |          |
| Question- |                                           |          |
|  naires   |                                           |          |
| Reports   |                                           |          |
| Audit log |                                           |          |
| Settings  |                                           |          |
+-----------+------------------------------------------------------+
```
- **Sidebar:** deep-blue (`brand-deep`) in both themes; icon + label; collapses to icons; items filtered by role (e.g. auditors see Evidence, Reports, Audit log; admins see Settings). Copilot opens as a right-side panel from the top bar.
- **Top bar:** tenant switcher, global command/search, notifications, theme toggle, user menu, and a **global time-range and scan selector** that drives trend widgets.
- **Page header:** title, status chips, primary action, secondary actions in an overflow menu.
- **Detail drawer:** right-side, 480-640 px, for control result, finding and evidence details without losing list context.
- **Grid:** 12 columns, 24 px gutters; max content width 1440 px.
- **Breakpoints:** desktop >= 1280 (full), tablet 768-1279 (sidebar collapsed, drawer becomes overlay), mobile < 768 (dashboard, approvals and notifications only; other routes show a read-only simplified view).
- **Density:** comfortable by default (row 48 px); compact toggle (row 36 px), remembered per user.

### 10.5 Screens and information shown
**Dashboard (landing; metrics first).** Role-aware presets (section 10.7).
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
| KPI strip (hero cards): Posture score | Coverage % | Open findings |
|                         Pending approvals | Evidence freshness   |
+-----------------------------------+-----------------------------+
| Coverage by framework (bars/rings)| Control status distribution |
| with delta vs previous scan       | (pass/partial/fail/unknown) |
+-----------------------------------+-----------------------------+
| Severity counts: now vs last 2    | Findings aging + MTTR       |
| scans (grouped bars, delta arrows)|                             |
+-----------------------------------+-----------------------------+
| 12-month trend (posture score,    | Jurisdiction heatmap        |
| coverage, open critical/high)     | (India / EU / US x framework)|
+-----------------------------------+-----------------------------+
| Pending approvals + agent activity| Upcoming audits / expiries  |
+-----------------------------------+-----------------------------+
| Agent quality + LLM cost vs budget (collapsible section)        |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Every card shows: value, unit, delta vs comparison scan (arrow + number + colour), small sparkline, last updated time, and a link to drill down.

**Other screens**
| Screen | Primary content |
|--------|-----------------|
| Assessments | Table of runs (status, scope, frameworks, started, duration, coverage, cost); run detail with live timeline (SSE), per-scanner status, budget gauge |
| Assessment compare | Pick any two scans: summary deltas, lists of new / resolved / regressed / unchanged controls and findings, severity delta chart |
| Control result review | Controls table with status, confidence, severity; drawer with AI summary (AI badge), citations, evidence, history timeline, approve/reject/edit |
| Control history | Per-control timeline over the last 12 months with status changes, evidence changes, approvals |
| Findings | Table + board view; filters by severity, framework, jurisdiction, status, age; aging chart; ticket links |
| Evidence | List with source, freshness, classification; viewer with highlights; upload |
| Questionnaires | Queue; side-by-side question | draft answer | citations/evidence | status/approval; redaction preview; export approval; answer library tab |
| Reports | Generate/list/download; selected framework, period, included approvals |
| Audit log | Filterable events; integrity check button |
| Regulatory changes | Proposed diffs with impact on mappings; approve/reject |
| Copilot panel | Chat with cited answers; refusal when ungrounded |
| Admin | Users, roles, SSO, connectors, integrations, budgets, retention, detail level |

### 10.6 Interaction patterns
- Global **time range** selector: Last 2 scans (default), 30 days, 90 days, 12 months, custom; scan picker for comparisons.
- Delta display: `▲ +4.2 pts` / `▼ -3` with colour (better = green, worse = red) and text; neutral = grey.
- Drill-down: clicking any chart segment applies filters to the underlying table.
- Chart accessibility: data-table toggle for every chart; keyboard focus on points; descriptive `aria-label`s.
- AI content: `AI` badge, confidence indicator (number + bar), citation chips, approval state chip.
- States: skeleton loaders; empty states with illustration and next step; error states with request ID; partial-data banners when scanners failed.

### 10.7 Persona dashboards
| Persona | Default widgets (in order) |
|---------|---------------------------|
| Executive / risk owner | Posture score, coverage by framework, 12-month trend, severity now vs last 2 scans, jurisdiction heatmap, upcoming audits |
| CISO | Posture score, severity delta, open critical/high with aging, pending approvals, regulatory changes, agent quality, cost |
| Compliance officer | Pending approvals, coverage by framework, control status, assessments in progress, questionnaires queue, evidence freshness |
| Engineer | Open findings assigned, aging, remediation cycle time, failing controls by system, scan status |
| Auditor | Control status by framework, evidence freshness, audit-log integrity, reports, 12-month history |
| Tenant admin | Connectors health, user/role changes, budget and cost, retention settings |

## 11. Metrics Catalogue
All metrics are tenant-scoped, computed from snapshots/metric points ([database-spec.md](database-spec.md) §3.6) and exposed via the metrics endpoints ([api-contract.md](api-contract.md) §5.6). "History" = window available for comparison (all >= 12 months unless noted).

| ID | Metric | Definition / formula | Source | Visual | Roles | Colour/threshold rule |
|----|--------|----------------------|--------|--------|-------|----------------------|
| M-01 | Posture score | Weighted % of in-scope unified controls with approved `pass` (partial = 0.5; unknown = 0), weighted by control criticality; 0-100 | `control_results` snapshot | KPI + sparkline + 12-month line | All except admin | >= 85 green, 70-84 amber, < 70 red (proposal) |
| M-02 | Control coverage % | Controls with an approved result and evidence / in-scope controls | snapshot | KPI + bars per framework | All | Same as M-01 |
| M-03 | Framework coverage | M-02 per framework and jurisdiction | snapshot | Bars/rings, heatmap | All | Sequential blue; delta arrow |
| M-04 | Status distribution | Counts of pass / partial / fail / unknown / n/a / awaiting approval | snapshot | Stacked bar / donut | All | Status colours + icons |
| M-05 | Severity counts (current vs last 2 scans) | Count of open failing controls/findings by severity (critical/high/medium/low) for latest scan and two previous scans, with deltas | snapshot, `findings` | Grouped bars + delta chips | CISO, exec, compliance, engineer | Increases red, decreases green |
| M-06 | Severity trend | M-05 over 12 months by scan | metric points | Stacked area/line | CISO, exec | Severity colours |
| M-07 | Open findings aging | Open findings bucketed 0-7, 8-30, 31-90, >90 days by severity | `findings` | Stacked bars | CISO, engineer | >90 days red outline |
| M-08 | Remediation cycle time | Median (and p90) days from finding opened to resolved | `findings` | KPI + trend | CISO, engineer, exec | Lower is better |
| M-09 | Time to audit readiness | Days from scope creation to first approved report, per framework | `scopes`, `reports` | KPI + trend | Exec, CISO, compliance | Lower is better |
| M-10 | Evidence freshness | % of evidence within its freshness threshold; count of stale items | `evidence` | KPI + bar by source | Compliance, auditor, engineer | < 90% amber, < 75% red (proposal) |
| M-11 | Scan duration | Median/p95 minutes per scanner and assessment | `agent_runs` | Bar/box + trend | Engineer, admin | Over SLO amber |
| M-12 | Pending approvals | Count and oldest age by type | `approvals` | KPI + list | Compliance, CISO | > 5 days amber, > 7 days red (expiry) |
| M-13 | Agent citation correctness | % of citations verified valid by validator (and by reviewer sample) | eval/run data | KPI + trend | CISO, admin | Gate >= 98% |
| M-14 | Agent confidence | Mean confidence and % low-confidence routed to humans | `control_results` | Histogram | Compliance, CISO | Info |
| M-15 | Reviewer override rate | % of agent proposals edited/rejected by humans | `approvals` | KPI + trend | CISO, compliance | Rising rate flagged |
| M-16 | LLM tokens and cost vs budget | Tokens and USD per run, tenant per month vs cap | `agent_runs` | Gauge + trend | Admin, CISO | 80% amber, 100% red |
| M-17 | Jurisdiction coverage matrix | Coverage % by jurisdiction x framework | snapshot | Heatmap | Exec, CISO, compliance | Sequential blue |
| M-18 | Questionnaire throughput | Questionnaires received/completed, answer reuse %, median turnaround | `questionnaires`, `answer_library` | KPI + trend | Compliance, CISO | Info |
| M-19 | Scan-to-scan change | Count of new / resolved / regressed / unchanged controls between two chosen scans | snapshots | Delta table + chart | Compliance, auditor, CISO | Regressed red, resolved green |
| M-20 | Audit-log integrity | Last hash-chain verification time and result | `audit_log` | Status chip | Auditor, CISO | Failed = red alert |
Each metric stores its formula version so historical values remain interpretable if definitions change.

## 12. Historical Data and Comparison (12 months)
- Every completed assessment writes an **immutable snapshot** (control results, statuses, severities, scores, framework and jurisdiction coverage) and **metric points** for the metrics above.
- Retention: at least 13 months (12 months visible plus one month buffer); tenants may extend, never shorten below 12 months. Snapshots survive later evidence deletion (metadata and hashes retained) so comparisons stay valid.
- Comparison: any two scans can be compared (M-19); defaults are the latest vs the previous scan, and M-05 always shows the latest and the two previous scans.
- Trends: daily/weekly/monthly rollups power 30/90-day and 12-month charts.
- Export: history can be exported (CSV/JSON) for auditors.

## 13. Accessibility
WCAG 2.2 AA target: contrast verified per section 10.2; keyboard-first navigation (command palette, drawer focus trap); screen reader labels on charts with data-table alternative; reduced motion support; minimum 24 px target size; no colour-only encoding; forms with clear errors; zoom to 200% without loss.

## 14. Open Questions
- [ ] Final brand name, logo and illustration style.
- [ ] Confirm score weighting for posture score (M-01) and colour thresholds.
- [ ] Charting library (Recharts vs visx) and heatmap implementation.
- [ ] Whether to offer a high-contrast theme.
- [ ] Localisation priorities (India/EU languages).
- [ ] Print/PDF styling for reports and dashboards.
- [ ] Final snapshot retention above 13 months and storage budget.

## 4. Relationships (ER overview)
new_string
### 3.6 History and metrics (`app`) - 12-month comparison
| Table | Purpose | Key columns |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `assessment_snapshots` | Immutable summary of each completed assessment | `id`, `tenant_id`, `assessment_id`, `scope_id`, `captured_at`, `formula_version`, `posture_score numeric`, `coverage_pct numeric`, `status_counts jsonb`, `severity_counts jsonb`, `framework_coverage jsonb`, `jurisdiction_coverage jsonb` |
| `snapshot_control_results` | Per-control result as of the snapshot (append-only copy) | `snapshot_id`, `tenant_id`, `unified_control_id`, `status`, `severity`, `confidence`, `evidence_ids uuid[]`, `evidence_hashes text[]`, `approved_by`, `approved_at` |
| `snapshot_findings` | Findings as of the snapshot | `snapshot_id`, `tenant_id`, `finding_id`, `severity`, `status`, `opened_at` |
| `metric_points` | Time series of catalogue metrics | `id`, `tenant_id`, `metric_id` (M-01..M-20), `scope_id`, `framework_id` (nullable), `jurisdiction` (nullable), `dimension jsonb`, `value numeric`, `captured_at`, `assessment_id`, `formula_version` |
| `metric_rollups` | Daily/weekly/monthly aggregates (materialised views or tables) | `tenant_id`, `metric_id`, `granularity`, `period_start`, `value`, `min`, `max`, `count` |
- Snapshots and metric points are written once, in the same transaction as assessment finalisation, and are **immutable** (no UPDATE/DELETE for `aucoff_app`; DB-9).
- Snapshot rows store evidence IDs and SHA-256 hashes so history stays comparable after evidence files are deleted under retention.
- Partition `snapshot_control_results`, `snapshot_findings` and `metric_points` by month on `captured_at`.
- Indexes: (`tenant_id`, `scope_id`, `captured_at DESC`) on `assessment_snapshots`; (`tenant_id`, `metric_id`, `captured_at`) on `metric_points`; (`tenant_id`, `unified_control_id`, `snapshot_id`) on `snapshot_control_results`.
- Queries: "latest scan vs previous two" uses the three newest snapshots for a scope; any-to-any comparison joins two snapshots on `unified_control_id`; per-control history reads `snapshot_control_results` over the last 12 months.
- Changing a metric formula increments `formula_version`; old points keep their version (displayed with a marker); recompute jobs write new versions rather than editing.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### agent.md structure (v0.2.0)
1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.
3. Orchestration (LangGraph graphs per workflow: assessment, mapping, questionnaire, regulatory change, report, copilot); state schema; interrupts; checkpointing; retries; budgets.
4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).
8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.
11. Evaluation: golden datasets per agent, metrics (accuracy, citation correctness >= target, hallucination rate, override rate, answer reuse accuracy, redaction recall), thresholds (proposal), CI regression gate, human feedback loop, red-team/prompt-injection suite.
12. Audit logging and traceability: run records, steps, redacted inputs, model/prompt versions, tokens/cost, approvals (maps to agent_runs/agent_steps/approvals).
13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

- Commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.

- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

Yes. The specs have about 60 open questions, but only a handful need your answer before the build starts. Most can wait until the component they affect is built.

**Needs your decision before coding starts**
1. **Python and FastAPI versions** (`backend-spec.md`). They are needed to scaffold the repo in T-002, and the `pyproject.toml` pins depend on them.
2. **Local PostgreSQL deployment:** plain StatefulSet or the CloudNativePG operator (`database-spec.md`, `infrastructure-spec.md`). This decides the chart layout and the `pgvector` image.
3. **Ingress controller and local hostnames** (`infrastructure-spec.md`). This is needed for the Helm chart.
4. **BFF auth library and session store** (`frontend-spec.md`). It is needed for the Next.js login shell.
5. **Where the committed OpenAPI file lives and which lint ruleset** (`api-contract.md`). This is needed for the first CI pipeline.
6. **Approved LLM providers and data classes** (`constitution.md`, `agent.md`: model IDs). The LLM interface and the redaction rules depend on this.
7. **Embedding model and dimension.** It's listed in three specs, and the `embeddings` table needs the dimension.

**Needed by the time the feature is built**
- **Legal:** whether framework texts such as PCI DSS and ISO can be stored.
- **Framework data:** verifying the framework versions you supplied against official sources.
- **Table design:** the audit-log retention period, the RPO/RTO targets, and the column-level encryption approach.
- **Data layout and tenancy:** the per-region tenant model. It will matter when you move to AWS.
- **Targets:** the numeric NFR targets, the posture score weighting and thresholds, and the mapping and questionnaire evaluation targets.

**Safe to defer**
- **Visual design:** brand name and logo, the charting library, a high-contrast theme, and localisation.
- **Product scope:** pricing and tenant plan limits, and the order in which the frameworks are delivered.
- **Agent tuning:** concurrency limits, staleness thresholds, redaction tooling, and the allow-listed regulatory sources.
- **Integrations and infrastructure:**
  - KEDA autoscaling and mTLS.
  - Image signing.
  - The choice between webhooks and polling for ticket sync.
  - The observability setup on AWS.

Pending state: repo clean at c3dd93f, pushed. agent.md is still the v0.1.0 template (22 TODOs). Execute agent.md + its alignment edits first, commit/push, then design.md work.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### agent.md structure (v0.2.0)
1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.
3. Orchestration (LangGraph graphs per workflow: assessment, mapping, questionnaire, regulatory change, report, copilot); state schema; interrupts; checkpointing; retries; budgets.
4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).

- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

## NEW TASK (previous, done): complete agent.md (owner chose to do this first, then design.md below)
Pending state: repo clean at c3dd93f, pushed. agent.md is still the v0.1.0 template (22 TODOs). Execute agent.md + its alignment edits first, commit/push, then design.md work.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### agent.md structure (v0.2.0)
1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.
3. Orchestration (LangGraph graphs per workflow: assessment, mapping, questionnaire, regulatory change, report, copilot); state schema; interrupts; checkpointing; retries; budgets.
4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).
8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.
11. Evaluation: golden datasets per agent, metrics (accuracy, citation correctness >= target, hallucination rate, override rate, answer reuse accuracy, redaction recall), thresholds (proposal), CI regression gate, human feedback loop, red-team/prompt-injection suite.
12. Audit logging and traceability: run records, steps, redacted inputs, model/prompt versions, tokens/cost, approvals (maps to agent_runs/agent_steps/approvals).
13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

- api-contract.md: questionnaire endpoints (upload, list, answer review/decision, export), copilot chat endpoint (SSE), regulatory-change proposals endpoints.

- design.md / frontend-spec.md: questionnaire screens (queue, side-by-side question/answer/evidence/approval), copilot panel; tasks.md: new tasks T-208..; constitution: add AI rule for externally shared outputs (AI-16: outputs leaving the tenant require approval and redaction).
- Commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.

- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

## NEW TASK (previous, done): complete agent.md (owner chose to do this first, then design.md below)
Pending state: repo clean at c3dd93f, pushed. agent.md is still the v0.1.0 template (22 TODOs). Execute agent.md + its alignment edits first, commit/push, then design.md work.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### agent.md structure (v0.2.0)
1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.
3. Orchestration (LangGraph graphs per workflow: assessment, mapping, questionnaire, regulatory change, report, copilot); state schema; interrupts; checkpointing; retries; budgets.
4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).
8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.
11. Evaluation: golden datasets per agent, metrics (accuracy, citation correctness >= target, hallucination rate, override rate, answer reuse accuracy, redaction recall), thresholds (proposal), CI regression gate, human feedback loop, red-team/prompt-injection suite.
12. Audit logging and traceability: run records, steps, redacted inputs, model/prompt versions, tokens/cost, approvals (maps to agent_runs/agent_steps/approvals).
13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).
- database-spec.md: new `assessment_snapshots`, `severity_counts`/`metric_points` (tenant_id, metric_id, assessment_id, scope_id, framework_id, value, captured_at), monthly partitions, retention row (>= 13 months, tenant-configurable up, never below 12), RLS, backup coverage; ensure results of deleted evidence keep metadata so history stays comparable.
- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

# Plan: finish design.md (architecture + UX/visual design)

## Context
design.md (v0.1.0) has architecture, components, data-model pointer, ADR-1..7 but still has TODO sections (system context, data flows, security architecture, observability, risks) and no UX/visual design. Owner wants it finished and wants closure on colour usage, page layout, and the information/metrics shown in the frontend. Owner stays in plan mode until they say go. After writing: align frontend-spec.md (link to design tokens/screens), spec.md metrics (if new ones), tasks.md, then commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

## GAP REVIEW 2026-10-19 (before build) - findings to fix in specs
Consistency checks run: all US/FR/NFR/API/T/ADR/PER/AG/M/R IDs and constitution rule IDs referenced are defined; all cross-file links resolve. Real gaps:
A. Missing decisions/specs
 1. Deterministic check engine: how scanner rules ("policy-as-code") are authored/stored/run (build own vs integrate Prowler/ScoutSuite/Steampipe, kube-bench/Trivy/kubescape, Checkov, OPA/Rego), rule-to-unified-control mapping, rule versioning. Not specified anywhere.
 2. Unified control catalogue seed: who authors the initial unified controls + requirement mappings (own, SCF-style open set, expert-reviewed), licensing, versioning.
 3. Platform operator role & tenant lifecycle: tenant provisioning/onboarding, offboarding/data export/deletion, support/break-glass access, platform super-admin (PER-6 is only tenant admin).
 4. External auditor access: invited, time-boxed read-only access to a tenant.
 5. Connector permissions: exact least-privilege read-only policies per source (AWS SecurityAudit-style roles, GCP/Azure roles, GitHub app scopes, Entra Graph scopes, Metabase), per-tenant secret storage at scale (K8s Secrets not suitable for many tenants).
 6. Scan scheduling/drift: cron model, schedule storage (US-12), drift detection rules.
 7. Notification catalogue (events x channels), templates.
 8. Report templates/formats per framework (open), evidence upload malware scanning (TODO).
B. Inconsistencies / missing detail
 1. DB lacks tables for APIs: scope schedules (column), notification_preferences, copilot conversations/messages, regulatory_changes (proposals), evidence_uploads, sso_settings/connectors naming (API `connectors` vs DB `integrations`), tenant_settings (retention, budgets, detail level, region).
 2. embeddings RLS: shared rows have tenant_id NULL but policy is equality -> need explicit policy for shared rows.
 3. frontend-spec route table lacks questionnaires, answer library, regulatory changes, compare/history, copilot, notifications routes; backend RBAC matrix lacks questionnaire/copilot/regulatory-change/history permissions.
 4. tasks.md header (owner/date/version 0.1.0) and "Blockers and Notes" TODO; no tasks for rule engine, control catalogue seeding, tenant provisioning, connector permission policies, repo conventions.
 5. Repo conventions not specified: monorepo layout, CODEOWNERS, PR template, branch strategy, README/CLAUDE.md.
C. Verify-before-build: PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector PG18 support; CloudNativePG PG18 support; owner-supplied framework instruments; Python 3.13 compatibility of LangGraph/asyncpg etc.
D. Deferred is fine: brand, locales, KEDA, mTLS, image signing, plan limits, concurrency numbers.

## NEW TASK (previous, done): complete agent.md (owner chose to do this first, then design.md below)
Pending state: repo clean at c3dd93f, pushed. agent.md is still the v0.1.0 template (22 TODOs). Execute agent.md + its alignment edits first, commit/push, then design.md work.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### agent.md structure (v0.2.0)
1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.
3. Orchestration (LangGraph graphs per workflow: assessment, mapping, questionnaire, regulatory change, report, copilot); state schema; interrupts; checkpointing; retries; budgets.
4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).
8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.
11. Evaluation: golden datasets per agent, metrics (accuracy, citation correctness >= target, hallucination rate, override rate, answer reuse accuracy, redaction recall), thresholds (proposal), CI regression gate, human feedback loop, red-team/prompt-injection suite.
12. Audit logging and traceability: run records, steps, redacted inputs, model/prompt versions, tokens/cost, approvals (maps to agent_runs/agent_steps/approvals).
13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

### agent.md alignment edits
- spec.md: add persona/US/FR for due-diligence questionnaires (US-14.., FR-16..) and agents list 5.6 updated (13 agents); out-of-scope: auto-submission to external portals.
- database-spec.md: questionnaire tables (`questionnaires`, `questionnaire_questions`, `questionnaire_answers`, `answer_library`) with RLS, retention, redaction flags.
- api-contract.md: questionnaire endpoints (upload, list, answer review/decision, export), copilot chat endpoint (SSE), regulatory-change proposals endpoints.
- backend-spec.md: service table + queue names for the 4 new agents.
- design.md / frontend-spec.md: questionnaire screens (queue, side-by-side question/answer/evidence/approval), copilot panel; tasks.md: new tasks T-208..; constitution: add AI rule for externally shared outputs (AI-16: outputs leaving the tenant require approval and redaction).
- Commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).
- database-spec.md: new `assessment_snapshots`, `severity_counts`/`metric_points` (tenant_id, metric_id, assessment_id, scope_id, framework_id, value, captured_at), monthly partitions, retention row (>= 13 months, tenant-configurable up, never below 12), RLS, backup coverage; ensure results of deleted evidence keep metadata so history stays comparable.
- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

1. Fill System Context (users/personas, IdP, LLM provider, evidence sources, ticketing, notifications) with Mermaid context diagram.
2. Key Data Flows: evidence ingestion -> analysis -> approval -> findings -> report (Mermaid sequence); assessment run via RabbitMQ/LangGraph; SSE progress.

   - Metrics catalogue: table of each metric with ID (M-01...), definition/formula, data source (table/endpoint), chart type, refresh, drill-down, roles, thresholds/colour rules. Include: posture score, framework coverage %, pass/partial/fail distribution, control severity counts vs last 2 scans (delta arrows), open findings by severity + aging buckets, MTTR/remediation cycle time, time to audit readiness, evidence freshness, scan duration, agent citation correctness, avg confidence, reviewer override rate, LLM tokens/cost vs budget, pending approvals, jurisdiction coverage matrix.

7. Update header version to 0.2.0, owner/date; Related links.

## NEW TASK (previous, done): complete agent.md (owner chose to do this first, then design.md below)
Pending state: repo clean at c3dd93f, pushed. agent.md is still the v0.1.0 template (22 TODOs). Execute agent.md + its alignment edits first, commit/push, then design.md work.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).

8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.

10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).
- database-spec.md: new `assessment_snapshots`, `severity_counts`/`metric_points` (tenant_id, metric_id, assessment_id, scope_id, framework_id, value, captured_at), monthly partitions, retention row (>= 13 months, tenant-configurable up, never below 12), RLS, backup coverage; ensure results of deleted evidence keep metadata so history stays comparable.
- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

"""All scanners are read-only (spec.md 5.5, AI-1, AI-6).

### 4a. Scanner Adapters and Check Engine
Decision (owner): **wrap proven open-source scanners behind our own scanner interface** instead of writing all rules from scratch.
- **Adapter interface:** `collect(scope, credentials_ref) -> RawFindings`, `normalise(raw) -> CheckResult[]`, `describe() -> {tool, version, required_permissions, licence}`. One adapter per tool; adapters run inside the scanner service container or as sandboxed jobs.
- **Candidate tools (to be confirmed per source; licence and maintenance reviewed before adoption):**
  | Source | Candidates |
  |--------|-----------|
  | AWS / GCP / Azure | Prowler, Steampipe (with compliance mods), ScoutSuite |
  | Kubernetes / containers | kubescape, kube-bench, Trivy |
  | Repos / CI-CD / IaC | Checkov, Semgrep, GitHub/Bitbucket APIs (custom adapter) |
  | Entra ID, Metabase | Custom adapters (Microsoft Graph, Metabase API) |
- **Normalised result schema:** `check_id`, `tool`, `tool_version`, `rule_pack_version`, `resource_ref`, `status` (pass/fail/error/not_applicable), `severity`, `evidence_ref`, `raw_ref`, `observed_at`.
- **Rule metadata:** AUCoFF maintains `check_definitions` (tool check ID -> unified control(s), severity override, rationale, applicability) so scan results roll up into control results ([database-spec.md](database-spec.md) §3.7). Mappings are versioned and reviewed like control mappings.
- **Rule packs:** pinned tool versions + rule sets per release (`rule_pack_version`); upgrades go through the evaluation suite; results always record tool and rule versions for reproducibility.
- **Gaps:** controls with no automated check are assessed from documents/evidence uploads or marked `unknown`; custom checks (OPA/Rego or Python) may be added behind the same interface when OSS coverage is missing.
- **Supply chain:** tools pinned by digest, scanned, SBOM'd; licence compatibility reviewed (some tools have non-OSS or commercial-use restrictions) - constitution SEC-17.

# reorder spec.md rows
L=open('spec.md').read().split('\n')
def move(prefix_move, prefix_before):
    i=[k for k,l in enumerate(L) if l.startswith(prefix_move)][0]
    row=L.pop(i)
    j=[k for k,l in enumerate(L) if l.startswith(prefix_before)][0]
    L.insert(j,row)
move('| US-20 |','| US-21 |')
move('| FR-24 |','| FR-25 |')

import re,glob,os
txt={f:open(f).read() for f in glob.glob('*.md')}
allt='\n'.join(txt.values())
for p in ['US','FR','NFR','API','T','ADR','PER','AG','M']:
    d=set()
    for t in txt.values(): d|=set(re.findall(r'^\|\s*('+p+r'-\d+)\s*\|',t,re.M))
    refs=set(re.findall(r'\b('+p+r'-\d+)\b',allt))
    print(p,len(d),sorted(refs-d))
con=txt['constitution.md']
cd=set(re.findall(r'\*\*([A-Z]+-\d+)\*\*',con))|set(re.findall(r'^\|\s*([A-Z]+-\d+)\s*\|',con,re.M))
print('constitution missing',sorted(set(re.findall(r'\b((?:ARC|DES|COD|QA|SEC|AI|DB|SDD|ENV)-\d+)\b',allt))-cd))
for f in txt:
    for m in re.findall(r'\]\(([a-z\-]+\.md)\)',txt[f]):
        if not os.path.exists(m): print('broken',f,m)
