**Gaps found and what changed (10 files, +132 lines):**
- **Check engine:** the specs didn't say how scanner rules are authored or run. Following your decision, `backend-spec.md` now wraps open-source scanners behind our own adapters. It covers a normalised result format, rule packs, check-to-control mapping, and licence vetting (rule SEC-17).
- **Tenant lifecycle and platform operators:**
  - Operator-provisioned tenants, with offboarding as export then deletion, and audited break-glass access for support (rule SEC-15).
  - The new endpoints are API-130 to API-134, and the role is the new persona PER-7.
- **External auditors:** time-boxed, scoped, read-only invitations, audit-logged (rule SEC-16). They get a new persona PER-8, API-140 and API-141, and a scoped `/auditor` view.
- **Control catalogue:** you author the v1 unified control set, and the mapping agent proposes the remaining mappings for expert approval (spec section 10a).
- **Missing database tables:** added for the check engine, scan schedules, notifications, copilot history, regulatory changes, evidence uploads, tenant settings, and auditor and break-glass grants.
  - I also split `connectors` from `integrations` so the API and database names match.
  - I fixed the row-level security for shared embeddings, which would have blocked the shared rows.
- **Missing routes and permissions:** `frontend-spec.md` now has routes for questionnaires, compare, history, regulatory changes, notifications and auditors. The role matrix in `backend-spec.md` covers the new roles.
- **Per-tenant secrets:** Kubernetes Secrets are now local-only, because they won't scale to many tenants. Production uses a dedicated secret store.
- **Tasks:**
  - T-003 to T-008 are new pre-build tasks, ahead of the scaffold.
  - They cover repo conventions (README, CLAUDE.md, CODEOWNERS, PR template) and verifying PostgreSQL 18.6, `pgvector`, CloudNativePG and the Python 3.13 libraries.

**Still open, none blocking.** The deferred items are brand, locales, KEDA, mTLS, image signing, plan limits and concurrency numbers. A few details are marked TODO in the specs:
- Who approves regulatory-change proposals (the operator or the tenant).
- The default retention for copilot messages.
- Notification templates.

**Before you scaffold, T-004 matters most.** I couldn't confirm that PostgreSQL 18.6, a compatible `pgvector`, or CloudNativePG support for Postgres 18 exist. If any of them doesn't, the version pins and the database image change.

# Plan: finish design.md (architecture + UX/visual design)

## Context
design.md (v0.1.0) has architecture, components, data-model pointer, ADR-1..7 but still has TODO sections (system context, data flows, security architecture, observability, risks) and no UX/visual design. Owner wants it finished and wants closure on colour usage, page layout, and the information/metrics shown in the frontend. Owner stays in plan mode until they say go. After writing: align frontend-spec.md (link to design tokens/screens), spec.md metrics (if new ones), tasks.md, then commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

## GAP REVIEW 2026-10-19 (before build) - findings to fix in specs
Consistency checks run: all US/FR/NFR/API/T/ADR/PER/AG/M/R IDs and constitution rule IDs referenced are defined; all cross-file links resolve. Real gaps:
A. Missing decisions/specs
 1. Deterministic check engine: how scanner rules ("policy-as-code") are authored/stored/run (build own vs integrate Prowler/ScoutSuite/Steampipe, kube-bench/Trivy/kubescape, Checkov, OPA/Rego), rule-to-unified-control mapping, rule versioning. Not specified anywhere.
 2. Unified control catalogue seed: who authors the initial unified controls + requirement mappings (own, SCF-style open set, expert-reviewed), licensing, versioning.
 3. Platform operator role & tenant lifecycle: tenant provisioning/onboarding, offboarding/data export/deletion, support/break-glass access, platform super-admin (PER-6 is only tenant admin).
 4. External auditor access: invited, time-boxed read-only access to a tenant.
 5. Connector permissions: exact least-privilege read-only policies per source (AWS SecurityAudit-style roles, GCP/Azure roles, GitHub app scopes, Entra Graph scopes, Metabase), per-tenant secret storage at scale (K8s Secrets not suitable for many tenants).
 6. Scan scheduling/drift: cron model, schedule storage (US-12), drift detection rules.
 7. Notification catalogue (events x channels), templates.
 8. Report templates/formats per framework (open), evidence upload malware scanning (TODO).
B. Inconsistencies / missing detail
 1. DB lacks tables for APIs: scope schedules (column), notification_preferences, copilot conversations/messages, regulatory_changes (proposals), evidence_uploads, sso_settings/connectors naming (API `connectors` vs DB `integrations`), tenant_settings (retention, budgets, detail level, region).

 3. frontend-spec route table lacks questionnaires, answer library, regulatory changes, compare/history, copilot, notifications routes; backend RBAC matrix lacks questionnaire/copilot/regulatory-change/history permissions.
 4. tasks.md header (owner/date/version 0.1.0) and "Blockers and Notes" TODO; no tasks for rule engine, control catalogue seeding, tenant provisioning, connector permission policies, repo conventions.

C. Verify-before-build: PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector PG18 support; CloudNativePG PG18 support; owner-supplied framework instruments; Python 3.13 compatibility of LangGraph/asyncpg etc.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.
3. Orchestration (LangGraph graphs per workflow: assessment, mapping, questionnaire, regulatory change, report, copilot); state schema; interrupts; checkpointing; retries; budgets.
4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).
8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.

12. Audit logging and traceability: run records, steps, redacted inputs, model/prompt versions, tokens/cost, approvals (maps to agent_runs/agent_steps/approvals).
13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

# Plan: finish design.md (architecture + UX/visual design)

## Context
design.md (v0.1.0) has architecture, components, data-model pointer, ADR-1..7 but still has TODO sections (system context, data flows, security architecture, observability, risks) and no UX/visual design. Owner wants it finished and wants closure on colour usage, page layout, and the information/metrics shown in the frontend. Owner stays in plan mode until they say go. After writing: align frontend-spec.md (link to design tokens/screens), spec.md metrics (if new ones), tasks.md, then commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

## GAP REVIEW 2026-10-19 (before build) - findings to fix in specs
Consistency checks run: all US/FR/NFR/API/T/ADR/PER/AG/M/R IDs and constitution rule IDs referenced are defined; all cross-file links resolve. Real gaps:
A. Missing decisions/specs
 1. Deterministic check engine: how scanner rules ("policy-as-code") are authored/stored/run (build own vs integrate Prowler/ScoutSuite/Steampipe, kube-bench/Trivy/kubescape, Checkov, OPA/Rego), rule-to-unified-control mapping, rule versioning. Not specified anywhere.
 2. Unified control catalogue seed: who authors the initial unified controls + requirement mappings (own, SCF-style open set, expert-reviewed), licensing, versioning.
 3. Platform operator role & tenant lifecycle: tenant provisioning/onboarding, offboarding/data export/deletion, support/break-glass access, platform super-admin (PER-6 is only tenant admin).
 4. External auditor access: invited, time-boxed read-only access to a tenant.
 5. Connector permissions: exact least-privilege read-only policies per source (AWS SecurityAudit-style roles, GCP/Azure roles, GitHub app scopes, Entra Graph scopes, Metabase), per-tenant secret storage at scale (K8s Secrets not suitable for many tenants).
 6. Scan scheduling/drift: cron model, schedule storage (US-12), drift detection rules.
 7. Notification catalogue (events x channels), templates.
 8. Report templates/formats per framework (open), evidence upload malware scanning (TODO).
B. Inconsistencies / missing detail
 1. DB lacks tables for APIs: scope schedules (column), notification_preferences, copilot conversations/messages, regulatory_changes (proposals), evidence_uploads, sso_settings/connectors naming (API `connectors` vs DB `integrations`), tenant_settings (retention, budgets, detail level, region).

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).

# ---- constitution
rep('constitution.md',[
("## 8. Spec-Driven Development Rules",
"""## 7c. Licensing, Provenance and Content Rules

AUCoFF MUST NOT contain, depend on, or distribute anything that creates a free/open-source (FOSS) licence issue or a plagiarism/copyright issue. Anything freely available on the internet (libraries, tools, container images, fonts, icons, illustrations, datasets, prompts, text, standards) is **not** automatically free to use. If an item has a licence or provenance issue, it MUST NOT be used; an alternative MUST be found instead.

| ID | Rule |
|----|------|
| LIC-1 | **Permissive allow-list only.** Third-party code, tools, images and fonts MUST use one of: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, PostgreSQL licence, MPL-2.0 (unmodified), SIL OFL (fonts), or equivalent permissive terms reviewed by the owner. |
| LIC-2 | **Disallowed:** AGPL, GPL, LGPL, SSPL, BUSL/BSL, "source-available", non-commercial or field-of-use restricted licences, unlicensed code, and anything with unclear or unverifiable provenance - including transitive dependencies and container base images. |
| LIC-3 | **Check before adoption.** The licence of every direct and transitive dependency, tool, image, font, icon, dataset and content item MUST be verified from the official source and recorded in the licence register before use. Training-data knowledge or assumptions are not sufficient. |
| LIC-4 | **Replacement first.** If a licence or provenance issue is found at any time, the item MUST be removed and replaced with an alternative that meets LIC-1; the decision is recorded in the licence register (and an ADR if architectural). |
| LIC-5 | **Automated enforcement.** CI MUST generate an SBOM and run a licence scan that fails the build on any disallowed or unknown licence; exceptions are not allowed without an owner-approved, time-limited ADR. |
| LIC-6 | **No copied content.** Code, text, standards and regulatory wording, images, icons, fonts, prompts, test data and documentation MUST NOT be copied from the internet or other sources unless their licence permits it (LIC-1) and attribution requirements are met. Standards text (PCI DSS, ISO, SOC 2, etc.) MUST NOT be reproduced verbatim unless licensed; AUCoFF stores its own summaries and clause references only. |
| LIC-7 | **Attribution and notices.** Required attributions and licence texts are kept in a NOTICE/licence register that ships with the product. |
| LIC-8 | **Generated content.** AI-generated code, text, reports, prompts and questionnaire answers MUST NOT reproduce copyrighted or third-party material; generated deliverables are reviewed for originality (similarity checks where practical) before release, and source citations point to references instead of copying wording. |

I added the licensing and provenance rules to the constitution and `spec.md`. I committed and pushed them to `origin/main` as `10ac976`, and I'm back in plan mode. The push went through without a rebase.

**`constitution.md` (v0.8.0): new section with rules LIC-1 to LIC-8**
- **Permitted licences:** only permissive ones: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, the PostgreSQL licence, MPL-2.0 unmodified, and OFL for fonts.
- **Disallowed:** AGPL, GPL, LGPL, SSPL, BUSL, source-available or non-commercial licences, and anything with unclear provenance, including transitive dependencies and base images.
- **Replacement first:** if an item has a licence or provenance issue, it isn't used and an alternative is chosen.
- **Verification and enforcement:** licences are verified before adoption and recorded in a licence register. CI generates an SBOM and fails the build on a disallowed or unknown licence.
- **Copied content:**
  - No copying of code, text, images, fonts, prompts or datasets without a compatible licence and attribution.
  - Standards such as PCI DSS and ISO are never reproduced verbatim. We store our own summaries and clause references.
- **Generated content:** AI-generated output is reviewed for originality.
- **Related rules:** QA-11 (definition of done) and SEC-17 now reference these rules.

**`spec.md` (v0.5.0)**
- NFR-15 states the compliance requirement.
- R-2 now says own summaries and references only.
- R-7 is a new risk with its mitigations.
- The open questions track the licence audit.

**Tools flagged for replacement.** From my memory, which I have not verified, these are likely AGPL, GPL or restrictive:
- **Object store:** MinIO.
- **Observability:** Grafana, Loki and Tempo.
- **Scanners:** Steampipe, ScoutSuite and the Semgrep rules.

I marked each as "not approved; licence review required; permissive alternative to be selected" in `backend-spec.md`, `infrastructure-spec.md`, `design.md` and `tasks.md`. Candidates such as SeaweedFS, Jaeger, VictoriaLogs and Perses are listed but unvetted.

- **New tasks:** T-009 audits the licences and provenance of every named dependency, tool, image, font and dataset, and creates the licence register. T-010 adds the CI gate. T-009 blocks the scanner choices (T-007) and the object-store and observability work (T-405, T-407).
- **ADR-12:** it records the permissive-only policy.

I also fixed an ID clash that the consistency check caught: the constitution's API rules clashed with the endpoint IDs `API-1` and `API-2`. They are now `APIR-1` to `APIR-6`.

**Before building, check these two.** The licence claims above are my recollection, so T-009 must confirm each from the official source. I also haven't audited tools I didn't flag, such as Redis, RabbitMQ and Keycloak. T-009 covers those too.

# Plan: finish design.md (architecture + UX/visual design)

## Context
design.md (v0.1.0) has architecture, components, data-model pointer, ADR-1..7 but still has TODO sections (system context, data flows, security architecture, observability, risks) and no UX/visual design. Owner wants it finished and wants closure on colour usage, page layout, and the information/metrics shown in the frontend. Owner stays in plan mode until they say go. After writing: align frontend-spec.md (link to design tokens/screens), spec.md metrics (if new ones), tasks.md, then commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

## GAP REVIEW 2026-10-19 (before build) - findings to fix in specs
Consistency checks run: all US/FR/NFR/API/T/ADR/PER/AG/M/R IDs and constitution rule IDs referenced are defined; all cross-file links resolve. Real gaps:
A. Missing decisions/specs
 1. Deterministic check engine: how scanner rules ("policy-as-code") are authored/stored/run (build own vs integrate Prowler/ScoutSuite/Steampipe, kube-bench/Trivy/kubescape, Checkov, OPA/Rego), rule-to-unified-control mapping, rule versioning. Not specified anywhere.
 2. Unified control catalogue seed: who authors the initial unified controls + requirement mappings (own, SCF-style open set, expert-reviewed), licensing, versioning.
 3. Platform operator role & tenant lifecycle: tenant provisioning/onboarding, offboarding/data export/deletion, support/break-glass access, platform super-admin (PER-6 is only tenant admin).
 4. External auditor access: invited, time-boxed read-only access to a tenant.
 5. Connector permissions: exact least-privilege read-only policies per source (AWS SecurityAudit-style roles, GCP/Azure roles, GitHub app scopes, Entra Graph scopes, Metabase), per-tenant secret storage at scale (K8s Secrets not suitable for many tenants).
 6. Scan scheduling/drift: cron model, schedule storage (US-12), drift detection rules.
 7. Notification catalogue (events x channels), templates.
 8. Report templates/formats per framework (open), evidence upload malware scanning (TODO).
B. Inconsistencies / missing detail
 1. DB lacks tables for APIs: scope schedules (column), notification_preferences, copilot conversations/messages, regulatory_changes (proposals), evidence_uploads, sso_settings/connectors naming (API `connectors` vs DB `integrations`), tenant_settings (retention, budgets, detail level, region).

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### agent.md structure (v0.2.0)
1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.
3. Orchestration (LangGraph graphs per workflow: assessment, mapping, questionnaire, regulatory change, report, copilot); state schema; interrupts; checkpointing; retries; budgets.
4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).
8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.
11. Evaluation: golden datasets per agent, metrics (accuracy, citation correctness >= target, hallucination rate, override rate, answer reuse accuracy, redaction recall), thresholds (proposal), CI regression gate, human feedback loop, red-team/prompt-injection suite.
12. Audit logging and traceability: run records, steps, redacted inputs, model/prompt versions, tokens/cost, approvals (maps to agent_runs/agent_steps/approvals).
13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

Owner instruction: update constitution and spec so there must be NO FOSS licence issue or plagiarism issue when using any library, software or content freely available on the internet; if an item has such an issue, do not use it - find an alternative.
Decisions: strict permissive allow-list (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3, ISC, PostgreSQL licence, MPL-2.0 unmodified, OFL fonts, CC0 / CC-BY content with attribution); disallowed: AGPL, GPL, LGPL, SSPL, BUSL/BSL, non-commercial or "source-available" restrictive licences, content with unclear provenance. ## NEW TASK (previous, done): complete agent.md (owner chose to do this first, then design.md below)
Pending state: repo clean at c3dd93f, pushed. agent.md is still the v0.1.0 template (22 TODOs). Execute agent.md + its alignment edits first, commit/push, then design.md work.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### agent.md structure (v0.2.0)
1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.
3. Orchestration (LangGraph graphs per workflow: assessment, mapping, questionnaire, regulatory change, report, copilot); state schema; interrupts; checkpointing; retries; budgets.
4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).
8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.
11. Evaluation: golden datasets per agent, metrics (accuracy, citation correctness >= target, hallucination rate, override rate, answer reuse accuracy, redaction recall), thresholds (proposal), CI regression gate, human feedback loop, red-team/prompt-injection suite.
12. Audit logging and traceability: run records, steps, redacted inputs, model/prompt versions, tokens/cost, approvals (maps to agent_runs/agent_steps/approvals).
13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).
- database-spec.md: new `assessment_snapshots`, `severity_counts`/`metric_points` (tenant_id, metric_id, assessment_id, scope_id, framework_id, value, captured_at), monthly partitions, retention row (>= 13 months, tenant-configurable up, never below 12), RLS, backup coverage; ensure results of deleted evidence keep metadata so history stays comparable.
- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

## NEW TASK (previous, done): complete agent.md (owner chose to do this first, then design.md below)
Pending state: repo clean at c3dd93f, pushed. agent.md is still the v0.1.0 template (22 TODOs). Execute agent.md + its alignment edits first, commit/push, then design.md work.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.

5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.

8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>AUCoFF Session Summary</title>
<style>
:root{--bg:#fff;--surface:#f8fafc;--border:#e2e8f0;--text:#0f172a;--muted:#475569;--brand:#1d4ed8;--deep:#0b2a6f;--teal:#0f766e;--pass:#15803d;--warn:#b45309;--fail:#b91c1c}
@media (prefers-color-scheme:dark){:root{--bg:#0b1220;--surface:#111a2e;--border:#1e293b;--text:#e5e7eb;--muted:#9ca3af;--brand:#60a5fa;--deep:#93c5fd;--teal:#2dd4bf;--pass:#4ade80;--warn:#fbbf24;--fail:#f87171}}
*{box-sizing:border-box}
body{margin:0;background:var(--bg);color:var(--text);font:15px/1.6 Inter,system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,sans-serif}
header{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#0b2a6f,#1d4ed8);color:#fff;padding:40px 16px}
header .wrap{max-width:1100px;margin:0 auto}
h1{margin:0 0 6px;font-size:30px}
header p{margin:0;opacity:.9}
main{max-width:1100px;margin:0 auto;padding:24px 16px 64px}
h2{margin:40px 0 12px;font-size:22px;color:var(--deep);border-bottom:2px solid var(--border);padding-bottom:6px}
h3{margin:20px 0 8px;font-size:16px}
.grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(200px,1fr));gap:12px}
.card{background:var(--surface);border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:12px;padding:14px 16px}
.kpi{font-size:32px;font-weight:700;color:var(--brand);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
.muted{color:var(--muted)}
table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin:8px 0 16px;font-size:14px;display:block;overflow-x:auto}
th,td{text-align:left;padding:8px 10px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);vertical-align:top}
th{background:var(--surface);font-weight:600;white-space:nowrap}
code{background:var(--surface);border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:6px;padding:1px 5px;font-size:13px}
.tag{display:inline-block;border-radius:999px;padding:1px 10px;font-size:12px;font-weight:600;border:1px solid currentColor}
.ok{color:var(--pass)}.warn{color:var(--warn)}.bad{color:var(--fail)}

<h2>3. Key decisions</h2>
<h3>Product and scope</h3>
<ul>
<li>Multi-tenant SaaS; operator-provisioned, invite-based tenants in v1; audited break-glass operator access; time-boxed scoped external auditor access.</li>
<li>Personas: compliance officer, auditor, engineer, executive, CISO, tenant admin, platform operator, external auditor.</li>
<li>All listed frameworks in v1 (PCI DSS v4.0.1, PCI 3DS, SOC 2, ISO 27001:2022, ISO 27701:2025, ISO 20022-1:2026 Ed.3, GDPR, DPDP, RBI DPSC and PPI, FFIEC BSA/AML 2026 and IT Handbook, FTC Safeguards, GLBA, NYDFS 500, PSD2, DORA). Framework versions are owner-supplied and must be verified.</li>
<li>Scanning is read-only; remediation is advisory. Due-diligence questionnaire agent drafts answers from real environment evidence; no auto-submission.</li>
<li>1 year of history (stored 13 months) with any-to-any scan comparison; severity counts for the latest scan against the previous two.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Technology</h3>
<table>
<tr><th>Area</th><th>Choice</th></tr>
<tr><td>Frontend</td><td>Next.js (App Router), TypeScript strict, shadcn/ui + Tailwind, TanStack Query, generated OpenAPI client, Auth.js BFF session</td></tr>
<tr><td>Backend</td><td>Python 3.13, FastAPI gateway + agent microservices over RabbitMQ, SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic, LangGraph with Postgres checkpoints</td></tr>
<tr><td>Data</td><td>PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector 0.8.6 (owner-confirmed), Row-Level Security tenancy, 1024-dim embeddings</td></tr>
<tr><td>LLM</td><td>Anthropic Claude via provider interface; redacted data only; tiered strong/small models</td></tr>
<tr><td>Check engine</td><td>Wrap vetted open-source scanners behind adapters; checks map to unified controls</td></tr>
<tr><td>Platform</td><td>kind + umbrella Helm chart, CloudNativePG, NGINX ingress (<code>aucoff.localtest.me</code>), cert-manager; Terraform + EKS later</td></tr>
<tr><td>API</td><td>REST /api/v1, OpenAPI at <code>backend/openapi.yaml</code> linted with Spectral, Swagger/ReDoc for every endpoint, SSE, cursor pagination, Idempotency-Key</td></tr>
</table>
<h3>UX and design</h3>
<ul>
<li>Light default with dark mode; professional, Gen-Z feel (rounded 8-12 px, soft shadows, large KPI numerals, gradients only on hero KPI cards).</li>
<li>Deep blue brand, teal accent; status colours with icon and text; contrast computed (text at least 4.5:1, UI at least 3:1).</li>
<li>Left sidebar, top bar with global time-range and scan selector, right detail drawer; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Agents and AI controls</h3>
<ul>
<li>13 agents: orchestrator, mapping, four scanners, document analyzer, remediation advisor, report generator, reviewer, regulatory-change, copilot, questionnaire.</li>
<li>Eval gates: citation correctness 98% or more, hallucination 1% or less, agreement 90% or more, redaction recall 99% or more.</li>
<li>Budgets: USD 25 per assessment, USD 10 per questionnaire; approvals expire after 7 days and never auto-approve.</li>
<li>Outputs leaving the tenant must be human-approved, redacted and audit-logged (AI-16).</li>
</ul>

<h2>4. Licensing and provenance rule</h2>
<p>Owner directive: no FOSS-licence or plagiarism issue is acceptable. Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, PostgreSQL, MPL-2.0 unmodified, OFL fonts) are allowed; if an item has an issue it is replaced. Standards text is never copied; only own summaries and clause references are stored. See constitution LIC-1 to LIC-8, NFR-15, risk R-7.</p>

# Plan: finish design.md (architecture + UX/visual design)

## Context
design.md (v0.1.0) has architecture, components, data-model pointer, ADR-1..7 but still has TODO sections (system context, data flows, security architecture, observability, risks) and no UX/visual design. Owner wants it finished and wants closure on colour usage, page layout, and the information/metrics shown in the frontend. Owner stays in plan mode until they say go. After writing: align frontend-spec.md (link to design tokens/screens), spec.md metrics (if new ones), tasks.md, then commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

## GAP REVIEW 2026-10-19 (before build) - findings to fix in specs
Consistency checks run: all US/FR/NFR/API/T/ADR/PER/AG/M/R IDs and constitution rule IDs referenced are defined; all cross-file links resolve. Real gaps:
A. Missing decisions/specs
 1. Deterministic check engine: how scanner rules ("policy-as-code") are authored/stored/run (build own vs integrate Prowler/ScoutSuite/Steampipe, kube-bench/Trivy/kubescape, Checkov, OPA/Rego), rule-to-unified-control mapping, rule versioning. Not specified anywhere.
 2. Unified control catalogue seed: who authors the initial unified controls + requirement mappings (own, SCF-style open set, expert-reviewed), licensing, versioning.
 3. Platform operator role & tenant lifecycle: tenant provisioning/onboarding, offboarding/data export/deletion, support/break-glass access, platform super-admin (PER-6 is only tenant admin).
 4. External auditor access: invited, time-boxed read-only access to a tenant.
 5. Connector permissions: exact least-privilege read-only policies per source (AWS SecurityAudit-style roles, GCP/Azure roles, GitHub app scopes, Entra Graph scopes, Metabase), per-tenant secret storage at scale (K8s Secrets not suitable for many tenants).
 6. Scan scheduling/drift: cron model, schedule storage (US-12), drift detection rules.
 7. Notification catalogue (events x channels), templates.
 8. Report templates/formats per framework (open), evidence upload malware scanning (TODO).
B. Inconsistencies / missing detail
 1. DB lacks tables for APIs: scope schedules (column), notification_preferences, copilot conversations/messages, regulatory_changes (proposals), evidence_uploads, sso_settings/connectors naming (API `connectors` vs DB `integrations`), tenant_settings (retention, budgets, detail level, region).
 2. embeddings RLS: shared rows have tenant_id NULL but policy is equality -> need explicit policy for shared rows.
 3. frontend-spec route table lacks questionnaires, answer library, regulatory changes, compare/history, copilot, notifications routes; backend RBAC matrix lacks questionnaire/copilot/regulatory-change/history permissions.
 4. tasks.md header (owner/date/version 0.1.0) and "Blockers and Notes" TODO; no tasks for rule engine, control catalogue seeding, tenant provisioning, connector permission policies, repo conventions.
 5. Repo conventions not specified: monorepo layout, CODEOWNERS, PR template, branch strategy, README/CLAUDE.md.
C. Verify-before-build: PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector PG18 support; CloudNativePG PG18 support; owner-supplied framework instruments; Python 3.13 compatibility of LangGraph/asyncpg etc.
D. Deferred is fine: brand, locales, KEDA, mTLS, image signing, plan limits, concurrency numbers.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.

5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).

8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.
11. Evaluation: golden datasets per agent, metrics (accuracy, citation correctness >= target, hallucination rate, override rate, answer reuse accuracy, redaction recall), thresholds (proposal), CI regression gate, human feedback loop, red-team/prompt-injection suite.

13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).
- database-spec.md: new `assessment_snapshots`, `severity_counts`/`metric_points` (tenant_id, metric_id, assessment_id, scope_id, framework_id, value, captured_at), monthly partitions, retention row (>= 13 months, tenant-configurable up, never below 12), RLS, backup coverage; ensure results of deleted evidence keep metadata so history stays comparable.
- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

how should we go ahead with the implementation?
Claude's response (1 message, 0 tool actions) 
I'd build in thin vertical slices rather than layer by layer. Each slice should work end to end, from the database to the UI to a real scanner, before the next one starts. Doing all frameworks in v1 is the biggest risk (R-1), so I'd cut internal milestones from the order below.

**Phase A: pre-build gates (short, mostly checks)**
1. **T-001:** you review and sign off the constitution and spec.
2. **T-009:** the licence audit. It decides the object store, the observability stack and the scanners, so it blocks several later choices.
3. **T-004 and T-005:** verify CloudNativePG with PostgreSQL 18.6 and `pgvector` 0.8.6, the Python 3.13 libraries, and the framework versions you supplied.
4. **T-006:** you author the v1 unified control set. Scanners and mapping can't be tested meaningfully without it. Start with a small set, for example PCI DSS plus SOC 2.
5. **T-002 and T-003:** the repo scaffold, README, CLAUDE.md, CODEOWNERS and PR template. The licence and secret scans go in at this step. Ideally T-010 lands here too.

**Phase B: walking skeleton (Milestone 1)**
Build the thinnest path through the whole stack:
- **Local stack:**
  - A kind cluster with the Helm chart, PostgreSQL via CloudNativePG, RabbitMQ and Keycloak (T-401 to T-403, T-405, T-408).
  - The remaining items of T-405 and T-406 (the object store chosen under T-009, ingress TLS, NetworkPolicies and Pod Security) land as the chart grows.
- **Backend:**
  - A FastAPI health endpoint and the OpenAPI pipeline with Spectral and the drift check (T-101, T-108).
  - The first migrations with roles and row-level security (T-102 to T-104, T-107), including tenant isolation tests.
- **Frontend:** a Next.js shell with the Keycloak login (T-301).
- **CI:** the CI pipeline (T-409).

The exit criterion is that you can log in, call an authenticated tenant-scoped API, and see CI enforce the OpenAPI, licence and secret gates.

**Phase C: first real assessment (Milestone 2)**
- Seed the control catalogue (T-106).
- Build the check-engine adapter and a single scanner (T-116, T-203), with the LangGraph orchestrator and approval interrupt (T-202).
- Add the LLM provider interface and redaction (T-201).
- Add snapshots (T-111, T-112) and the review and approval screens (T-304, T-305).

The exit criterion is one scope assessed end to end, with cited results approved by a human and the snapshot written. I'd choose Kubernetes configuration or a GitHub repository as the first scanner, because they're easiest to test locally without cloud credentials.

**Phase D: breadth (Milestones 3 to 5)**
In this order:
1. Remaining scanners and the document analyzer (T-204, T-205).
2. Findings, the dashboard metrics, history and compare (T-114, T-115, T-309, T-310) and the evaluation gates (T-207, T-208).
3. The questionnaire agent (T-209, T-210), tenant provisioning and auditor access (T-117, T-118), and the copilot and regulatory-change agents.
4. Frameworks added in batches of two or three, adding mappings and checks only.

**Phase E: hardening and AWS**
Observability, backup drills, the OWASP and API security gates, and then Terraform and EKS (T-501, T-502).

**Working practices I'd keep**
- One task, one PR, with the spec section and rule IDs cited. Spec changes ship in the same PR as any behaviour change.
- Tests first for tenant isolation, row-level security, audit immutability and redaction. A mistake there is the costliest.
- A recorded-LLM test mode from the start, so CI is deterministic and cheap.
- Leave the visual polish for after Milestone 2. Build the design tokens and app shell early, but keep the dashboard to core KPIs until real data exists.

Next steps. Are you ready to start Phase A? The items I'd do first are T-003 and T-004. You'll need to do T-001, T-005 and T-006, and I can draft starting material for the control set if you want. I'd also run T-009 early, since it unblocks tool choices. I'm in plan mode, so tell me when to go.
