# Plan: finish design.md (architecture + UX/visual design)

## Context
design.md (v0.1.0) has architecture, components, data-model pointer, ADR-1..7 but still has TODO sections (system context, data flows, security architecture, observability, risks) and no UX/visual design. Owner wants it finished and wants closure on colour usage, page layout, and the information/metrics shown in the frontend. Owner stays in plan mode until they say go. After writing: align frontend-spec.md (link to design tokens/screens), spec.md metrics (if new ones), tasks.md, then commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

## GAP REVIEW 2026-10-19 (before build) - findings to fix in specs
Consistency checks run: all US/FR/NFR/API/T/ADR/PER/AG/M/R IDs and constitution rule IDs referenced are defined; all cross-file links resolve. Real gaps:
A. Missing decisions/specs
 1. Deterministic check engine: how scanner rules ("policy-as-code") are authored/stored/run (build own vs integrate Prowler/ScoutSuite/Steampipe, kube-bench/Trivy/kubescape, Checkov, OPA/Rego), rule-to-unified-control mapping, rule versioning. Not specified anywhere.
 2. Unified control catalogue seed: who authors the initial unified controls + requirement mappings (own, SCF-style open set, expert-reviewed), licensing, versioning.
 3. Platform operator role & tenant lifecycle: tenant provisioning/onboarding, offboarding/data export/deletion, support/break-glass access, platform super-admin (PER-6 is only tenant admin).
 4. External auditor access: invited, time-boxed read-only access to a tenant.
 5. Connector permissions: exact least-privilege read-only policies per source (AWS SecurityAudit-style roles, GCP/Azure roles, GitHub app scopes, Entra Graph scopes, Metabase), per-tenant secret storage at scale (K8s Secrets not suitable for many tenants).
 6. Scan scheduling/drift: cron model, schedule storage (US-12), drift detection rules.
 7. Notification catalogue (events x channels), templates.
 8. Report templates/formats per framework (open), evidence upload malware scanning (TODO).
B. Inconsistencies / missing detail
 1. DB lacks tables for APIs: scope schedules (column), notification_preferences, copilot conversations/messages, regulatory_changes (proposals), evidence_uploads, sso_settings/connectors naming (API `connectors` vs DB `integrations`), tenant_settings (retention, budgets, detail level, region).
 2. embeddings RLS: shared rows have tenant_id NULL but policy is equality -> need explicit policy for shared rows.
 3. frontend-spec route table lacks questionnaires, answer library, regulatory changes, compare/history, copilot, notifications routes; backend RBAC matrix lacks questionnaire/copilot/regulatory-change/history permissions.
 4. tasks.md header (owner/date/version 0.1.0) and "Blockers and Notes" TODO; no tasks for rule engine, control catalogue seeding, tenant provisioning, connector permission policies, repo conventions.
 5. Repo conventions not specified: monorepo layout, CODEOWNERS, PR template, branch strategy, README/CLAUDE.md.
C. Verify-before-build: PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector PG18 support; CloudNativePG PG18 support; owner-supplied framework instruments; Python 3.13 compatibility of LangGraph/asyncpg etc.
D. Deferred is fine: brand, locales, KEDA, mTLS, image signing, plan limits, concurrency numbers.

## (done) owner 2026-10-19: licence and provenance rule (no FOSS-licence or plagiarism issues)
Owner instruction: update constitution and spec so there must be NO FOSS licence issue or plagiarism issue when using any library, software or content freely available on the internet; if an item has such an issue, do not use it - find an alternative.
Decisions: strict permissive allow-list (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3, ISC, PostgreSQL licence, MPL-2.0 unmodified, OFL fonts, CC0 / CC-BY content with attribution); disallowed: AGPL, GPL, LGPL, SSPL, BUSL/BSL, non-commercial or "source-available" restrictive licences, content with unclear provenance. Existing named tools to mark "licence review required - find permissive alternative" (from assistant recollection, MUST be verified): MinIO (AGPL-3.0), Grafana/Loki/Tempo (AGPL-3.0), Steampipe (AGPL-3.0), ScoutSuite (GPL-2.0), Semgrep rules (restrictive rules licence), possibly Redis (licence changes), Keycloak/RabbitMQ/others to confirm. Candidate alternatives (unvetted): SeaweedFS or filesystem-backed S3 shim (Apache-2.0) for MinIO; Jaeger/OpenTelemetry + VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs/Prometheus/Perses for Grafana stack; Prowler/kubescape/kube-bench/Trivy/Checkov (Apache-2.0, to confirm) instead of Steampipe/ScoutSuite; Opengrep/own rules instead of Semgrep rules.

1. constitution.md: new section "Licensing, Provenance and Content Rules" with rules LIC-1..LIC-8 (allow-list/deny-list; licence check before adoption incl. transitive deps; automated licence scanning + SBOM in CI blocking disallowed licences; no copying of copyrighted/standards text, code, images, fonts, prompts or datasets without a permissive licence or written permission; attribution/NOTICE file; AI-generated content must not reproduce copyrighted material - plagiarism/similarity checks for generated docs, reports, prompts; third-party framework texts (PCI DSS, ISO, etc.) stored only as own summaries/references with clause IDs unless licensed; replacement-first policy: if an issue is found, remove and choose an alternative, record in licence register/ADR); extend SEC-17 cross-reference; QA/definition-of-done gets licence check; bump version 0.8.0 + changelog; resolve/link spec R-2.
2. spec.md: NFR-15 (licence and IP compliance), NFR for content provenance; update R-2 (licensing of standard texts -> own summaries/references only, legal review) and add R-7 (OSS licence/plagiarism risk, mitigation: allow-list + scanning + alternatives); US/FR: FR-31 licence register/SBOM report available to admins? (keep minimal: licence register maintained in repo, CI gate); update section 4 licensing note; open questions: licence audit results; version 0.5.0.
3. backend-spec.md §4a, infrastructure-spec.md §2/§8 (MinIO, Grafana/Loki/Tempo), design.md components table, database-spec (Steampipe/others none): annotate affected tools "licence review required; permissive alternative to be selected" and remove hard commitments (keep as candidates pending T-009); agent.md tools unaffected except `web.fetch` sources (content terms) and prompts/datasets provenance.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### agent.md structure (v0.2.0)
1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.
3. Orchestration (LangGraph graphs per workflow: assessment, mapping, questionnaire, regulatory change, report, copilot); state schema; interrupts; checkpointing; retries; budgets.
4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).
8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.
11. Evaluation: golden datasets per agent, metrics (accuracy, citation correctness >= target, hallucination rate, override rate, answer reuse accuracy, redaction recall), thresholds (proposal), CI regression gate, human feedback loop, red-team/prompt-injection suite.
12. Audit logging and traceability: run records, steps, redacted inputs, model/prompt versions, tokens/cost, approvals (maps to agent_runs/agent_steps/approvals).
13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).
- database-spec.md: new `assessment_snapshots`, `severity_counts`/`metric_points` (tenant_id, metric_id, assessment_id, scope_id, framework_id, value, captured_at), monthly partitions, retention row (>= 13 months, tenant-configurable up, never below 12), RLS, backup coverage; ensure results of deleted evidence keep metadata so history stays comparable.
- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

Owner instruction: update constitution and spec so there must be NO FOSS licence issue or plagiarism issue when using any library, software or content freely available on the internet; if an item has such an issue, do not use it - find an alternative.
Decisions: strict permissive allow-list (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3, ISC, PostgreSQL licence, MPL-2.0 unmodified, OFL fonts, CC0 / CC-BY content with attribution); disallowed: AGPL, GPL, LGPL, SSPL, BUSL/BSL, non-commercial or "source-available" restrictive licences, content with unclear provenance. ## NEW TASK (previous, done): complete agent.md (owner chose to do this first, then design.md below)
Pending state: repo clean at c3dd93f, pushed. agent.md is still the v0.1.0 template (22 TODOs). Execute agent.md + its alignment edits first, commit/push, then design.md work.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### agent.md structure (v0.2.0)
1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.
3. Orchestration (LangGraph graphs per workflow: assessment, mapping, questionnaire, regulatory change, report, copilot); state schema; interrupts; checkpointing; retries; budgets.
4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).
8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.
11. Evaluation: golden datasets per agent, metrics (accuracy, citation correctness >= target, hallucination rate, override rate, answer reuse accuracy, redaction recall), thresholds (proposal), CI regression gate, human feedback loop, red-team/prompt-injection suite.
12. Audit logging and traceability: run records, steps, redacted inputs, model/prompt versions, tokens/cost, approvals (maps to agent_runs/agent_steps/approvals).
13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).
- database-spec.md: new `assessment_snapshots`, `severity_counts`/`metric_points` (tenant_id, metric_id, assessment_id, scope_id, framework_id, value, captured_at), monthly partitions, retention row (>= 13 months, tenant-configurable up, never below 12), RLS, backup coverage; ensure results of deleted evidence keep metadata so history stays comparable.
- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

The specs now say v1 is local-only, and I pushed that as `7203be8`. One part didn't complete: `docs/session-summary.html` was not updated. I'm back in plan mode, so that fix is waiting for your go.

**What the pushed commit changed**
- **Kind versus minikube:** I chose kind. It is Docker-based and lighter, it matches CI, and it needs no VM. Minikube is not used.
- **`constitution.md` (v0.9.0):** a new rule, ENV-4, says v1 must be buildable, runnable and fully testable on a laptop with kind, with no cloud hosting. The only external dependencies are the LLM API (with an offline mock mode) and optional read-only scan targets. I reworded ARC-11, SEC-3, ENV-1 and ENV-3. The AWS migration notes are now informational and don't gate v1.
- **`spec.md` (v0.6.0):**
  - NFR-12 now states the local-only scope.
  - NFR-3 and NFR-7 are tied to local v1. The 99.9% availability target and regional hosting apply after v1.
  - AWS hosting, Terraform/EKS and multi-region are out of scope for v1.
- **`infrastructure-spec.md`:**
  - AWS is "post-v1, out of scope", and there is no `values-aws.yaml` in v1.
  - A new laptop profile covers the cluster layout, prerequisites, and a first resource guess of about 8 CPUs and 16 GB for the full stack, with a minimal profile for 8 GB machines.
  - It also covers offline mode with recorded LLM and scanner fixtures.
- **Other specs:**
  - `design.md` has the new ADR-13 and the updated ADR-7.
  - `database-spec.md`, `backend-spec.md` and `tasks.md` carry the same local-only wording.
  - In `tasks.md`, the AWS tasks T-501 and T-502 are deferred, and T-410 is a new laptop smoke test and resource profile task.

Cloud scanners still scan customer AWS/GCP/Azure accounts read-only. That is scanning, not hosting. In v1 they run against recorded fixtures, or optionally real read-only test accounts. Kubernetes Secrets are fine for a single-laptop v1, and a managed secret store is the post-v1 path.

**What went wrong with the summary page**
My script died on a bad check before it could edit `docs/session-summary.html`. My shell chain didn't stop, so the specs were committed and pushed anyway.
- **Summary page:** it still says "Terraform + EKS later" and shows the old commit count. The page predates the local-only decision.
- **Consistency check:** it didn't run in that step. I ran it afterwards, read-only, and it passed. Every referenced ID is defined, every constitution rule exists, and every link resolves.

Tell me when to go and I'll update the summary page, then commit and push it.

# Plan: finish design.md (architecture + UX/visual design)

## Context
design.md (v0.1.0) has architecture, components, data-model pointer, ADR-1..7 but still has TODO sections (system context, data flows, security architecture, observability, risks) and no UX/visual design. Owner wants it finished and wants closure on colour usage, page layout, and the information/metrics shown in the frontend. Owner stays in plan mode until they say go. After writing: align frontend-spec.md (link to design tokens/screens), spec.md metrics (if new ones), tasks.md, then commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

## GAP REVIEW 2026-10-19 (before build) - findings to fix in specs
Consistency checks run: all US/FR/NFR/API/T/ADR/PER/AG/M/R IDs and constitution rule IDs referenced are defined; all cross-file links resolve. Real gaps:
A. Missing decisions/specs
 1. Deterministic check engine: how scanner rules ("policy-as-code") are authored/stored/run (build own vs integrate Prowler/ScoutSuite/Steampipe, kube-bench/Trivy/kubescape, Checkov, OPA/Rego), rule-to-unified-control mapping, rule versioning. Not specified anywhere.
 2. Unified control catalogue seed: who authors the initial unified controls + requirement mappings (own, SCF-style open set, expert-reviewed), licensing, versioning.
 3. Platform operator role & tenant lifecycle: tenant provisioning/onboarding, offboarding/data export/deletion, support/break-glass access, platform super-admin (PER-6 is only tenant admin).
 4. External auditor access: invited, time-boxed read-only access to a tenant.
 5. Connector permissions: exact least-privilege read-only policies per source (AWS SecurityAudit-style roles, GCP/Azure roles, GitHub app scopes, Entra Graph scopes, Metabase), per-tenant secret storage at scale (K8s Secrets not suitable for many tenants).
 6. Scan scheduling/drift: cron model, schedule storage (US-12), drift detection rules.
 7. Notification catalogue (events x channels), templates.
 8. Report templates/formats per framework (open), evidence upload malware scanning (TODO).
B. Inconsistencies / missing detail
 1. DB lacks tables for APIs: scope schedules (column), notification_preferences, copilot conversations/messages, regulatory_changes (proposals), evidence_uploads, sso_settings/connectors naming (API `connectors` vs DB `integrations`), tenant_settings (retention, budgets, detail level, region).
 2. embeddings RLS: shared rows have tenant_id NULL but policy is equality -> need explicit policy for shared rows.
 3. frontend-spec route table lacks questionnaires, answer library, regulatory changes, compare/history, copilot, notifications routes; backend RBAC matrix lacks questionnaire/copilot/regulatory-change/history permissions.
 4. tasks.md header (owner/date/version 0.1.0) and "Blockers and Notes" TODO; no tasks for rule engine, control catalogue seeding, tenant provisioning, connector permission policies, repo conventions.
 5. Repo conventions not specified: monorepo layout, CODEOWNERS, PR template, branch strategy, README/CLAUDE.md.
C. Verify-before-build: PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector PG18 support; CloudNativePG PG18 support; owner-supplied framework instruments; Python 3.13 compatibility of LangGraph/asyncpg etc.
D. Deferred is fine: brand, locales, KEDA, mTLS, image signing, plan limits, concurrency numbers.

## TASK NOW (owner 2026-10-19): v1/MVP is local-only (kind or minikube; choose kind) - NO AWS deployment in v1

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.

Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.

- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.

- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).

## (done) owner 2026-10-19: licence and provenance rule (no FOSS-licence or plagiarism issues)
Owner instruction: update constitution and spec so there must be NO FOSS licence issue or plagiarism issue when using any library, software or content freely available on the internet; if an item has such an issue, do not use it - find an alternative.
Decisions: strict permissive allow-list (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3, ISC, PostgreSQL licence, MPL-2.0 unmodified, OFL fonts, CC0 / CC-BY content with attribution); disallowed: AGPL, GPL, LGPL, SSPL, BUSL/BSL, non-commercial or "source-available" restrictive licences, content with unclear provenance. Existing named tools to mark "licence review required - find permissive alternative" (from assistant recollection, MUST be verified): MinIO (AGPL-3.0), Grafana/Loki/Tempo (AGPL-3.0), Steampipe (AGPL-3.0), ScoutSuite (GPL-2.0), Semgrep rules (restrictive rules licence), possibly Redis (licence changes), Keycloak/RabbitMQ/others to confirm. Candidate alternatives (unvetted): SeaweedFS or filesystem-backed S3 shim (Apache-2.0) for MinIO; Jaeger/OpenTelemetry + VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs/Prometheus/Perses for Grafana stack; Prowler/kubescape/kube-bench/Trivy/Checkov (Apache-2.0, to confirm) instead of Steampipe/ScoutSuite; Opengrep/own rules instead of Semgrep rules.

Pending state: repo clean at c3dd93f, pushed. agent.md is still the v0.1.0 template (22 TODOs). Execute agent.md + its alignment edits first, commit/push, then design.md work.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### agent.md structure (v0.2.0)
1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.
3. Orchestration (LangGraph graphs per workflow: assessment, mapping, questionnaire, regulatory change, report, copilot); state schema; interrupts; checkpointing; retries; budgets.
4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).
8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.
11. Evaluation: golden datasets per agent, metrics (accuracy, citation correctness >= target, hallucination rate, override rate, answer reuse accuracy, redaction recall), thresholds (proposal), CI regression gate, human feedback loop, red-team/prompt-injection suite.
12. Audit logging and traceability: run records, steps, redacted inputs, model/prompt versions, tokens/cost, approvals (maps to agent_runs/agent_steps/approvals).
13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).
- database-spec.md: new `assessment_snapshots`, `severity_counts`/`metric_points` (tenant_id, metric_id, assessment_id, scope_id, framework_id, value, captured_at), monthly partitions, retention row (>= 13 months, tenant-configurable up, never below 12), RLS, backup coverage; ensure results of deleted evidence keep metadata so history stays comparable.
- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

<h3>Prompt</h3><pre>{E(p)}</pre>
<h3>Output</h3><p>{o}</p></article>'''

from html.parser import HTMLParser
class P(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(s): super().__init__(); s.st=[]; s.bad=[]
    void={'meta','br','img','link','hr','input'}
    def handle_starttag(s,t,a):
        if t not in s.void: s.st.append(t)
    def handle_endtag(s,t):
        if t in s.void: return
        if not s.st or s.st[-1]!=t: s.bad.append((t,s.st[-3:]))
        else: s.st.pop()

def text_of(m):

    out=[]

        if not t.strip(): continue

        print(k,i,repr(t[:110]))

# Plan: finish design.md (architecture + UX/visual design)

## Context
design.md (v0.1.0) has architecture, components, data-model pointer, ADR-1..7 but still has TODO sections (system context, data flows, security architecture, observability, risks) and no UX/visual design. Owner wants it finished and wants closure on colour usage, page layout, and the information/metrics shown in the frontend. Owner stays in plan mode until they say go. After writing: align frontend-spec.md (link to design tokens/screens), spec.md metrics (if new ones), tasks.md, then commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

Consistency checks run: all US/FR/NFR/API/T/ADR/PER/AG/M/R IDs and constitution rule IDs referenced are defined; all cross-file links resolve. Real gaps:
A. Missing decisions/specs
 1. Deterministic check engine: how scanner rules ("policy-as-code") are authored/stored/run (build own vs integrate Prowler/ScoutSuite/Steampipe, kube-bench/Trivy/kubescape, Checkov, OPA/Rego), rule-to-unified-control mapping, rule versioning. Not specified anywhere.
 2. Unified control catalogue seed: who authors the initial unified controls + requirement mappings (own, SCF-style open set, expert-reviewed), licensing, versioning.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).

def fmt_input(inp):
    parts=[]
    for k,v in inp.items():
        if isinstance(v,str):
            if '\n' in v or len(v)>120: parts.append(f'<div class="k">{E(k)}</div><pre class="v">{E(v)}</pre>')
            else: parts.append(f'<div class="k">{E(k)}</div><div class="v1">{E(v)}</div>')
        else:
            parts.append(f'<div class="k">{E(k)}</div><pre class="v">{E(json.dumps(v,indent=2,ensure_ascii=False))}</pre>')
    return ''.join(parts)
def res_text(res):
    if res is None: return None,False
    c=res.get('content')
    if isinstance(c,str): s=c
    else: s='\n'.join(b.get('text','') if b.get('type')=='text' else json.dumps(b) for b in (c or []))
    return clean(s),bool(res.get('is_error'))
def render_event(ev):
    k=ev[0]
    if k=='text': return f'<div class="say"><pre class="msg">{E(ev[1])}</pre></div>'
    if k=='term': return f'<div class="tool term"><div class="th">Terminal event</div><pre class="out">{E(ev[1])}</pre></div>'
    b,res=ev[1],ev[2]
    s,err=res_text(res)
    head=f'<div class="th"><span>Tool: {E(b["name"])}</span>'+('<span class="err">error / declined</span>' if err else '')+'</div>'
    body=f'<div class="inp">{fmt_input(b["input"])}</div>'
    out=('<div class="k">result</div><pre class="out%s">%s</pre>'%(' errc' if err else '',E(s))) if s is not None else '<div class="k">result</div><pre class="out">(no result recorded)</pre>'
    return f'<div class="tool">{head}{body}{out}</div>'

    p=re.sub(r'</pasted_content id="[^"]*">','[pasted content ends]',p)

class P(HTMLParser):

# Plan: finish design.md (architecture + UX/visual design)

## Context
design.md (v0.1.0) has architecture, components, data-model pointer, ADR-1..7 but still has TODO sections (system context, data flows, security architecture, observability, risks) and no UX/visual design. Owner wants it finished and wants closure on colour usage, page layout, and the information/metrics shown in the frontend. Owner stays in plan mode until they say go. After writing: align frontend-spec.md (link to design tokens/screens), spec.md metrics (if new ones), tasks.md, then commit, `git pull --rebase origin main`, push.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).

Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.

## (done) owner 2026-10-19: licence and provenance rule (no FOSS-licence or plagiarism issues)
Owner instruction: update constitution and spec so there must be NO FOSS licence issue or plagiarism issue when using any library, software or content freely available on the internet; if an item has such an issue, do not use it - find an alternative.
Decisions: strict permissive allow-list (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3, ISC, PostgreSQL licence, MPL-2.0 unmodified, OFL fonts, CC0 / CC-BY content with attribution); disallowed: AGPL, GPL, LGPL, SSPL, BUSL/BSL, non-commercial or "source-available" restrictive licences, content with unclear provenance. Existing named tools to mark "licence review required - find permissive alternative" (from assistant recollection, MUST be verified): MinIO (AGPL-3.0), Grafana/Loki/Tempo (AGPL-3.0), Steampipe (AGPL-3.0), ScoutSuite (GPL-2.0), Semgrep rules (restrictive rules licence), possibly Redis (licence changes), Keycloak/RabbitMQ/others to confirm. Candidate alternatives (unvetted): SeaweedFS or filesystem-backed S3 shim (Apache-2.0) for MinIO; Jaeger/OpenTelemetry + VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs/Prometheus/Perses for Grafana stack; Prowler/kubescape/kube-bench/Trivy/Checkov (Apache-2.0, to confirm) instead of Steampipe/ScoutSuite; Opengrep/own rules instead of Semgrep rules.

## NEW TASK (previous, done): complete agent.md (owner chose to do this first, then design.md below)
Pending state: repo clean at c3dd93f, pushed. agent.md is still the v0.1.0 template (22 TODOs). Execute agent.md + its alignment edits first, commit/push, then design.md work.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### agent.md structure (v0.2.0)
1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.
3. Orchestration (LangGraph graphs per workflow: assessment, mapping, questionnaire, regulatory change, report, copilot); state schema; interrupts; checkpointing; retries; budgets.
4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).
8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.
11. Evaluation: golden datasets per agent, metrics (accuracy, citation correctness >= target, hallucination rate, override rate, answer reuse accuracy, redaction recall), thresholds (proposal), CI regression gate, human feedback loop, red-team/prompt-injection suite.
12. Audit logging and traceability: run records, steps, redacted inputs, model/prompt versions, tokens/cost, approvals (maps to agent_runs/agent_steps/approvals).
13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).
- database-spec.md: new `assessment_snapshots`, `severity_counts`/`metric_points` (tenant_id, metric_id, assessment_id, scope_id, framework_id, value, captured_at), monthly partitions, retention row (>= 13 months, tenant-configurable up, never below 12), RLS, backup coverage; ensure results of deleted evidence keep metadata so history stays comparable.
- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about pgvector 0.8.6 and PostgreSQL 18 support:

pgvector v0.8.6 was released for PostgreSQL 18 on July 30th and was tested in PostgreSQL 18.4 with Microsoft Windows 11 x64.

However, it's important to note that PostgreSQL 18 support was added in pgvector 0.8.1, which means pgvector 0.8.6 continues that support. The earlier version 0.8.1 was the first to introduce PostgreSQL 18 compatibility.

pgvector v0.8.6 was also released for multiple other PostgreSQL versions including 13, 14, 15, 16, and 17, indicating it's a multi-version compatible release.

I found comprehensive information about CloudNativePG's support for PostgreSQL 18 with pgvector extension and image volumes. Here are the key findings:

## CloudNativePG PostgreSQL 18 Support with pgvector and Image Volumes

**Core Capability:**
CloudNativePG supports the dynamic loading of PostgreSQL extensions into a Cluster at Pod startup using the Kubernetes ImageVolume feature alongside the extension_control_path GUC introduced in PostgreSQL 18, a feature to which the CloudNativePG project contributed.

**pgvector Extension:**
The CloudNativePG Community maintains a suite of extension container images, including pgvector and PostGIS, as part of the postgres-extensions-containers project.

**How It Works:**
This feature allows you to mount a PostgreSQL extension, packaged as an OCI-compliant container image, as a read-only and immutable volume at a designated filesystem path within a running pod.

**Requirements:**
PostgreSQL 18 or later is required for extension_control_path support. Additionally, Kubernetes 1.35 or later is needed, as the ImageVolume feature is enabled by default. Container runtime support includes containerd v2.1.0 or later, or CRI-O v1.31 or later.

**Extension Management:**
For extensions requiring database-level installation via the CREATE EXTENSION command, you can use the Database resource's declarative extension management to ensure consistent, automated setup across all your PostgreSQL databases.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding Grafana, Loki, and Tempo's relicensing:

Grafana Labs relicensed their core open source projects (Grafana, Grafana Loki, and Grafana Tempo) from the Apache License 2.0 to the Affero General Public License (AGPL) v3. Plugins, agents, and certain libraries remained Apache-licensed.

AGPLv3 is an OSI-approved license that meets all criteria for Free and Open Source Software. The AGPLv3 offers protection against cloud providers that make changes to the code without submitting them back to the project.

According to Grafana Labs CEO Raj Dutt, the company considered the SSPL license after there was a trend by companies like MongoDB and Elastic to switch to the license, but ultimately decided against SSPL since it was not an OSI-approved license. There wasn't a specific event that triggered the license change to AGPLv3; the company just thought after many years of debate it was time to make a decision and move forward.

Based on the search results, here's information about Semgrep rules licensing and commercial use restrictions:

## Semgrep Engine License

The Semgrep Engine is open source, licensed under LGPL 2.1, and both the Semgrep Community Edition engine and Opengrep engine are licensed under LGPL 2.1.

## Semgrep Rules License

Semgrep maintains a collection of rules written by the community and Semgrep, Inc., and they are licensed under the Semgrep Rules License. This license limits their use to internal, non-competing, and non-SaaS contexts, and explicitly limits certain commercial usage.

In December 2024, licensing for Semgrep-maintained rules changed from Commons Clause with LGPL 2.1 to the Semgrep Rules License. This change limits certain commercial usage of the rules authored by Semgrep and contributed to our public repositories.

## Commercial Use Restrictions

The Semgrep Registry license's commercial restrictions only come into effect if you are selling a product using rules provided in the Semgrep Registry. If that's the case, contact for a license. However, Semgrep is safe to run on your private code, meaning internal use does not require special permission.

Based on the search results, here's information about the licenses mentioned in your query:

## Redis Licensing

In March 2024, Redis Ltd. changed the licensing of Redis from the permissive BSD-3-Clause license to a dual-license model: the Server Side Public License (SSPL) and the Redis Source Available License v2 (RSALv2). In May 2025, Redis 8 added AGPLv3 as a third license option alongside the two source-available ones.

Redis 8 in Redis Open Source and later versions are available under a tri-license, including RSALv2, SSPLv1, and AGPLv3.

## Valkey Fork

Major cloud providers (AWS, Google, Oracle) and other companies responded to the license change by forking Redis 7.2 (the last BSD-licensed version) as Valkey, under the Linux Foundation. Valkey is licensed under BSD-3-Clause and is maintained as a true open-source project.

## AGPLv3 Details

AGPLv3 requires that if you run a modified version as a network service, you must make the source code available to users of that service.

## License Comparison

AGPLv3 is a copyleft license with a network clause, while Valkey's BSD-3-Clause is permissive with no strings and a foundation rather than a single company steering it.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about SeaweedFS:

**License and Overview:**
SeaweedFS is licensed under Apache 2.0, making it a permissive open-source project.

**S3 Compatibility:**
SeaweedFS has grown into a full-featured storage platform supporting S3 API, and features S3 API with SigV4 auth, multipart uploads, ranged reads and per-bucket isolation. Full Amazon S3 API compatibility lets you use existing S3 tools, SDKs, and applications as a drop-in replacement for cloud object storage.

**Object Store Capabilities:**
SeaweedFS is a fast, simple, and highly scalable distributed file system for storing and serving billions of files. Features include erasure coding, cloud tiering, cross-datacenter replication, AES-256-GCM encryption, automatic compaction, file TTL, and a built-in admin UI.

**Key Technical Design:**
The architecture separates concerns into a master server for volume management, a volume server for blob storage, a filer for directory/file abstraction, an S3 gateway for S3 compatibility, and a WebDAV server for mounted drive access.
