cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# AUCoFF

AgenticAI Unified Compliance Framework for Fintechs (AUCoFF): a multi-tenant web application in which agentic AI services read-only scan a fintech's cloud, Kubernetes, code, SaaS tools and documents, assess them against one unified control set mapped to many regulations and standards, and produce cited findings, advisory remediation and audit-ready reports. Humans approve every consequential outcome.

**v1 (MVP) scope: everything is built, deployed and tested on a developer laptop using [kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/). Nothing is deployed to AWS or any other cloud in v1.**

## Specification-driven development

The specifications in [`specs/`](specs/) are the source of truth; code follows specs, not the other way round. Start with [`specs/constitution.md`](specs/constitution.md) (non-negotiable rules), then [`specs/spec.md`](specs/spec.md). Task breakdown: [`specs/tasks.md`](specs/tasks.md). A readable session history is in [`docs/session-summary.html`](docs/session-summary.html).

| Spec | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| [constitution.md](specs/constitution.md) | Architecture, coding, quality, security, AI, database, API, licensing and environment rules |
| [spec.md](specs/spec.md) | Product spec: personas, frameworks, user stories, requirements |
| [design.md](specs/design.md) | Architecture, UX design, metrics catalogue |
| [agent.md](specs/agent.md) | The 13 agents, orchestration, guardrails, evaluation |
| [backend-spec.md](specs/backend-spec.md) / [frontend-spec.md](specs/frontend-spec.md) | Services and UI |
| [api-contract.md](specs/api-contract.md) | REST + SSE contract (OpenAPI is the source of truth) |
| [database-spec.md](specs/database-spec.md) | PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector schema and security |
| [infrastructure-spec.md](specs/infrastructure-spec.md) | kind + Helm, CI/CD, observability |

## Repository layout

```
specs/      specifications (source of truth)
backend/    FastAPI gateway and (later) agent services   (Python 3.13, uv)
frontend/   Next.js app                                    (TypeScript strict)
deploy/     kind cluster config and the umbrella Helm chart
docs/       session summary and licence/provenance records
```

## Prerequisites (laptop)

Docker-compatible runtime running (for example Colima: `colima start`), `kind`, `kubectl`, `helm`, `make`, Python 3.13 with `uv`, Node 22+ with `npm`, and `gitleaks` (a pre-commit hook runs it). Run `make doctor` to check.

## Quick start

```
make doctor          # check tools
make setup           # install backend and frontend dependencies
make check           # lint, type-check, tests, OpenAPI drift, licence scan
make cluster-up      # create the local kind cluster (needs a running Docker runtime)
make cluster-down
```

## Rules that apply to every change

- Follow [`specs/constitution.md`](specs/constitution.md); cite the spec section and rule IDs in your PR.
- **Licences:** permissive only (LIC-1 to LIC-8). Check a dependency's licence before adding it and record it in [`LICENCES.md`](LICENCES.md). Never copy code, text, images or standards wording from the internet unless its licence allows it.
- No secrets in git, images or logs. Test data is synthetic only.
- Never deploy outside the local kind cluster in v1.

## Project licence

The repository's [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) is the GNU AGPL v3. Confirm this is the intended licence for AUCoFF before distributing it; the dependency rules above govern what AUCoFF may use, not how AUCoFF itself is licensed.
EOF
cat > CLAUDE.md <<'EOF'
# AUCoFF: guidance for AI coding agents

Read `specs/constitution.md` first; it wins over every other document. Specs in `specs/` are the source of truth: change the spec in the same PR as any behaviour change, and cite spec sections and rule IDs (ARC-, DES-, COD-, QA-, SEC-, AI-, DB-, APIR-, LIC-, ENV-) in commits and PRs.

## Hard rules
- **v1 is local-only (ENV-4):** build, run and test on a laptop with kind. Do not add AWS/cloud deployment code, Terraform, or `values-aws.yaml`.
- **Licences (LIC-1 to LIC-8):** permissive only (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, PostgreSQL, MPL-2.0 unmodified, OFL fonts, plus PSF-2.0 if the owner approves it). Never add AGPL/GPL/LGPL/SSPL/BUSL or unclear-provenance code. Verify a dependency's licence from its official source before adding it and update `LICENCES.md`. If a package has an issue, replace it; do not work around it. Do not copy text, code, images or standards wording from the internet.
- **Secrets:** never commit secrets; the global pre-commit hook runs Gitleaks. Synthetic data only.
- **Architecture (ARC-1..11):** frontend talks only to the FastAPI gateway; layers `api -> domain -> db/messaging/llm`; business rules in `domain`; every external dependency behind an interface; every tenant table has `tenant_id` and row-level security.
- **API (APIR-1..6):** every endpoint documented in OpenAPI; `backend/openapi.yaml` must match the generated spec; Spectral must pass.
- **AI (AI-1..16):** agents are advisory, read-only against customer systems; consequential actions need human approval; outputs leaving the tenant are approved and redacted.
- **Honesty:** record versions or licences you could not verify as unverified, and add a task to verify them.

## Workflow
1. Pick a task from `specs/tasks.md` and read its spec sections.
2. Write tests first for tenant isolation, RLS, audit, redaction and anything security relevant.
3. Run `make check` before committing. Small commits with a clear message; end commit messages with the Co-Authored-By trailer when Claude Code authored them.
4. `git pull --rebase origin main` before pushing; do not force-push.

## Useful commands
`make doctor`, `make setup`, `make check`, `make backend-run`, `make openapi`, `make cluster-up`, `make cluster-down`, `make helm-lint`.

from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="AUCOFF_", extra="ignore")

    environment: str = "local"
    service_name: str = "aucoff-gateway"

def get_settings() -> Settings:

"""Liveness and readiness probes (api-contract.md, API-2). No authentication."""

from fastapi import APIRouter
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

router = APIRouter(prefix="/health", tags=["health"])


class HealthStatus(BaseModel):
    status: str = Field(description="`ok` when the check passes.", examples=["ok"])
    service: str = Field(description="Service name.", examples=["aucoff-gateway"])
    version: str = Field(description="Service version.", examples=["0.1.0"])


@router.get(
    "/live",
    operation_id="healthLive",
    summary="Liveness probe",
    description="Returns 200 while the process is running. Used by Kubernetes liveness probes.",
    response_model=HealthStatus,
)
def live() -> HealthStatus:
    from app.core.config import get_settings

    s = get_settings()
    return HealthStatus(status="ok", service=s.service_name, version=s.version)


@router.get(
    "/ready",
    operation_id="healthReady",
    summary="Readiness probe",
    description=(
        "Returns 200 when the service can accept traffic. Dependency checks (database, "
        "queue) are added as those layers are implemented."
    ),
    response_model=HealthStatus,
)
def ready() -> HealthStatus:
    from app.core.config import get_settings

    s = get_settings()
    return HealthStatus(status="ok", service=s.service_name, version=s.version)
EOF

"""AUCoFF FastAPI gateway entry point."""

from fastapi import FastAPI

from app.api import health
from app.core.config import get_settings


def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    settings = get_settings()
    app = FastAPI(
        title="AUCoFF API",
        version=settings.version,
        description=(
            "AgenticAI Unified Compliance Framework for Fintechs. The OpenAPI document is the "
            "source of truth for the API contract (specs/api-contract.md)."
        ),
        openapi_url="/api/v1/openapi.json",
        docs_url="/docs",
        redoc_url="/redoc",
    )
    app.include_router(health.router, prefix="/api/v1")
    return app


app = create_app()

"""Export the generated OpenAPI document to backend/openapi.yaml.

Usage: uv run python scripts/export_openapi.py [--check]
With --check, exits non-zero if the committed file differs (CI drift check, APIR-2).
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

from app.main import create_app

TARGET = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "openapi.yaml"


def render() -> str:
    spec = create_app().openapi()
    return yaml.safe_dump(spec, sort_keys=True, allow_unicode=True)


def main() -> int:
    rendered = render()
    if "--check" in sys.argv:
        current = TARGET.read_text() if TARGET.exists() else ""
        if current != rendered:
            print("openapi.yaml is out of date; run `make openapi`", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        print("openapi.yaml is up to date")
        return 0
    TARGET.write_text(rendered)
    print(f"wrote {TARGET}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
EOF

cat > scripts/check_licences.py <<'EOF'
"""Licence gate for Python dependencies (constitution LIC-1, LIC-2, LIC-5).

Fails on any disallowed or unknown licence. The allow-list is permissive-only. Exceptions are
explicit, per package, and must be recorded in LICENCES.md with the owner's decision.

Usage: uv run python -m scripts.check_licences
"""

import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ALLOWED = {
    "mit",
    "mit license",
    "apache-2.0",
    "apache software license",
    "apache license 2.0",
    "bsd license",
    "bsd-2-clause",
    "bsd-3-clause",
    "isc",
    "isc license",
    "postgresql",
    "mpl-2.0",
    "mozilla public license 2.0 (mpl 2.0)",  # MPL-2.0 is allowed only unmodified (LIC-1)
}
DENIED_PATTERN = re.compile(r"agpl|\bgpl|lgpl|sspl|busl|business source|commons clause", re.I)

# package -> licence accepted as an explicit exception (pending owner decision, see LICENCES.md)
EXCEPTIONS: dict[str, str] = {
    "typing_extensions": "psf-2.0",  # required by pydantic; permissive, awaiting owner approval
}


def alternatives(expr: str) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Split an SPDX-like expression into OR alternatives of AND terms."""
    return [
        [t.strip().lower() for t in re.split(r"\s+AND\s+|;", alt) if t.strip()]
        for alt in re.split(r"\s+OR\s+", expr)
    ]


def ok(name: str, expr: str) -> bool:
    if DENIED_PATTERN.search(expr):
        return False
    exc = EXCEPTIONS.get(name)
    return any(
        all(term in ALLOWED or term == exc for term in terms) for terms in alternatives(expr)
    )


def main() -> int:
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["pip-licenses", "--format=json", "--with-system"],
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    ).stdout
    bad = [(p["Name"], p["License"]) for p in json.loads(out) if not ok(p["Name"], p["License"])]
    if bad:
        print("Disallowed or unknown licences (constitution LIC-1/LIC-2):", file=sys.stderr)
        for name, lic in bad:
            print(f"  {name}: {lic}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print("licence check passed: all Python dependencies are on the permissive allow-list")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
EOF

from scripts.check_licences import ok


def test_permissive_licences_pass() -> None:
    assert ok("x", "MIT")
    assert ok("x", "BSD-3-Clause")
    assert ok("x", "Apache-2.0 OR BSD-2-Clause")

mkdir -p scripts src/__tests__ && cat > scripts/check-licences.mjs <<'EOF'
// Licence gate for npm dependencies (constitution LIC-1, LIC-2, LIC-5).
// Fails on disallowed or unknown licences. PENDING_OWNER licences are permissive-style but not on the
// constitution's allow-list yet; they pass with a notice until the owner decides (see LICENCES.md).
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";

const ALLOWED = new Set([
  "MIT", "Apache-2.0", "BSD-2-Clause", "BSD-3-Clause", "ISC", "MPL-2.0", "PostgreSQL", "OFL-1.1",
]);
const PENDING_OWNER = new Set(["BlueOak-1.0.0", "0BSD", "CC0-1.0", "CC-BY-3.0", "CC-BY-4.0", "Python-2.0", "PSF-2.0"]);
const DENIED = /agpl|\bgpl|lgpl|sspl|busl|business source|commons clause/i;

const out = execFileSync(
  "npx",
  ["license-checker-rseidelsohn", "--json", "--excludePrivatePackages"],
  { encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024 },
);
const pkgs = JSON.parse(out);

function terms(expr) {
  return expr
    .replace(/[()*]/g, "")
    .split(/\s+OR\s+/)
    .map((alt) => alt.split(/\s+AND\s+/).map((t) => t.trim()).filter(Boolean));
}

const bad = [];
const pending = new Map();
for (const [name, info] of Object.entries(pkgs)) {
  const raw = Array.isArray(info.licenses) ? info.licenses.join(" AND ") : String(info.licenses);
  if (DENIED.test(raw)) {
    bad.push([name, raw]);
    continue;
  }
  const alts = terms(raw);
  const pass = alts.some((ts) => ts.every((t) => ALLOWED.has(t)));
  const passPending = alts.some((ts) => ts.every((t) => ALLOWED.has(t) || PENDING_OWNER.has(t)));
  if (pass) continue;
  if (passPending) pending.set(raw, [...(pending.get(raw) ?? []), name]);
  else bad.push([name, raw]);
}
if (pending.size) {
  console.warn("Pending owner approval (permissive-style, not yet on the allow-list):");
  for (const [lic, names] of pending) console.warn(`  ${lic}: ${names.length} package(s), e.g. ${names.slice(0, 2).join(", ")}`);
}
if (bad.length) {
  console.error("Disallowed or unknown licences (constitution LIC-1/LIC-2):");
  for (const [n, l] of bad) console.error(`  ${n}: ${l}`);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log(`licence check passed (${Object.keys(pkgs).length} packages)`);
EOF

{{- end -}}

spec:

  selector:

  template:

      labels:

---

cd /Users/praveen.da/REPOS-PD/aucoff && cat > Makefile <<'EOF'
# AUCoFF developer commands. v1 is local-only (kind); there are no deploy targets for any cloud.
.DEFAULT_GOAL := help
SHELL := /bin/bash
CLUSTER := aucoff
SPECTRAL := npx --yes @stoplight/spectral-cli@6

.PHONY: help doctor setup lint typecheck test openapi openapi-check spectral licences helm-lint check \
        backend-run frontend-dev cluster-up cluster-down

help: ## Show this help
	@grep -E '^[a-zA-Z_-]+:.*?## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | awk 'BEGIN {FS = ":.*?## "}; {printf "  %-16s %s\n", $$1, $$2}'

doctor: ## Check required tools
	@for t in docker kind kubectl helm uv node npm gitleaks; do \
	  if command -v $$t >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf "  ok       %s\n" $$t; else printf "  MISSING  %s\n" $$t; fi; done
	@docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "  ok       docker daemon running" || echo "  NOT RUNNING  docker daemon (e.g. run: colima start)"

setup: ## Install backend and frontend dependencies
	cd backend && uv sync
	cd frontend && npm install

lint: ## Lint and format-check backend and frontend
	cd backend && uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
	cd frontend && npm run -s lint && npm run -s format:check

typecheck: ## Type-check backend (mypy) and frontend (tsc)
	cd backend && uv run mypy
	cd frontend && npm run -s typecheck

test: ## Run backend (pytest) and frontend (vitest) tests
	cd backend && uv run pytest -q
	cd frontend && npm run -s test

openapi: ## Regenerate backend/openapi.yaml
	cd backend && uv run python -m scripts.export_openapi

openapi-check: ## Fail if backend/openapi.yaml is stale (APIR-2)
	cd backend && uv run python -m scripts.export_openapi --check

spectral: ## Lint the OpenAPI document with Spectral (APIR-1)
	cd backend && $(SPECTRAL) lint openapi.yaml --ruleset .spectral.yaml --fail-severity=warn

licences: ## Licence gate for Python and npm dependencies (LIC-1, LIC-2, LIC-5)
	cd backend && uv run python -m scripts.check_licences
	cd frontend && npm run -s licences && npm run -s audit:prod

helm-lint: ## Lint the Helm chart
	helm lint deploy/helm/aucoff -f deploy/helm/aucoff/values-local.yaml

check: lint typecheck test openapi-check spectral licences helm-lint ## Everything CI runs

backend-run: ## Run the API locally on :8000
	cd backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000

frontend-dev: ## Run the web app locally on :3000
	cd frontend && npm run dev

cluster-up: ## Create the local kind cluster
	kind create cluster --config deploy/kind/kind-config.yaml

cluster-down: ## Delete the local kind cluster
	kind delete cluster --name $(CLUSTER)
EOF

rows=json.load(open('/tmp/direct_deps.json'))

tbl=[]
for n,eco,v,l in rows:

t=f'''# Licence and provenance register

Maintained under constitution rules LIC-1 to LIC-8 (see [`specs/constitution.md`](specs/constitution.md)) and task T-009. Every direct dependency, tool, image, font, icon and dataset is recorded here with its licence and the source of that information. Anything with a licence or provenance issue is **not used**; an alternative is chosen and the decision is recorded here.

Last updated: 2026-10-19. Status: **T-009 in progress** (first pass; not complete).

## 1. How information in this register was obtained

- **Installed package metadata** (`pip-licenses`, `license-checker-rseidelsohn`): the licence declared by the exact installed version. CI re-checks this on every change (`make licences`).
- **Web search results of 2026-10-19:** used for tools not yet installed. These are secondary sources and are marked *unconfirmed* until the project's own `LICENSE` file is read when the tool is adopted. Nothing here was read from a lawyer or from the projects' LICENSE files unless stated.

## 2. Policy decisions that need the owner

The constitution's allow-list (LIC-1) is: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3-Clause, ISC, PostgreSQL, MPL-2.0 (unmodified), OFL fonts. The dependency scan found these permissive-style licences that are **not on the list yet**. CI currently passes them with a notice. Please decide for each: add to the allow-list, or require replacement.

| Licence | Where it appears | Notes |
|---------|------------------|-------|
| PSF-2.0 | Python `typing_extensions` (required by pydantic/FastAPI) | Explicit per-package exception in `backend/scripts/check_licences.py`. Removing it is not realistic. Recommend approving. |
| MIT-0 | npm `@csstools/*` (Tailwind/PostCSS chain) | MIT without the attribution clause; recommend approving. |
| BlueOak-1.0.0 | npm `glob`, `minimatch`, `tar`, `lru-cache`, others (11 packages) | Permissive, OSI-approved; recommend approving. |
| 0BSD | npm `tslib` | Public-domain-equivalent; recommend approving. |
| CC0-1.0 | npm `language-subtag-registry`, `mdn-data`, `spdx-license-ids` | Public-domain dedication (data); recommend approving. |
| CC-BY-4.0 / CC-BY-3.0 | npm `caniuse-lite` (data), `spdx-exceptions` | Data licences requiring attribution; attribution must be carried in NOTICE (LIC-7). |
| Python-2.0 | npm `argparse` | PSF-style, permissive; recommend approving. |

Also for the owner: the repository's own [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) is the **GNU AGPL v3**. The rules above govern what AUCoFF may depend on; they do not say how AUCoFF itself is licensed. Please confirm AGPL-3.0 is intended (it affects how the product can be offered to customers).

## 3. Issue found and fixed during scaffolding

| Item | Problem | Action |
|------|---------|--------|
| `sharp` (optional dependency of Next.js, for image optimisation) | Its prebuilt `libvips` binaries are LGPL-3.0-or-later (disallowed by LIC-2) | Replaced with an in-repo stub via `overrides` in `frontend/package.json` (`frontend/stubs/sharp`) and set `images.unoptimized: true`. The licence scan confirms no LGPL package remains. |

## 4. Tools named in the specs (first-pass verification)

| Tool | Finding (web search 2026-10-19) | Decision |
|------|-------------------------------|----------|
| MinIO | GNU AGPL v3; community repository archived 25 April 2026, source-only, no binaries | **Not approved** |
| Grafana, Loki, Tempo | Relicensed from Apache-2.0 to AGPLv3 (April 2021) | **Not approved** |
| Steampipe | AGPL-3.0 | **Not approved** |
| ScoutSuite | GPL-2.0 (NCC Group) | **Not approved** |
| Semgrep / Opengrep engines | LGPL-2.1 | **Not approved** (LIC-2 denies LGPL) |
| Semgrep rules | Semgrep Rules License (restricts competing/commercial use) | **Not approved** |
| Redis (current) | Tri-licensed RSALv2 / SSPLv1 / AGPLv3 | **Not approved**; Valkey (BSD-3-Clause per search) is the candidate if a cache is ever needed. v1 avoids a cache by keeping the session in an encrypted cookie. |
| Prowler | Apache-2.0 | Candidate (cloud scanning) - confirm from LICENSE on adoption |
| Trivy, Checkov, kube-bench | Apache-2.0 | Candidates - confirm from LICENSE on adoption |
| kubescape | Not found in search | **Unverified** - do not adopt until confirmed |
| SeaweedFS | Apache-2.0 | Candidate replacement for MinIO (S3-compatible) - confirm and test |
| Perses | Apache-2.0 | Candidate dashboard tool replacing Grafana |
| VictoriaLogs | Apache-2.0 (single-node and cluster) | Candidate log store replacing Loki |
| Jaeger | Not found in search | **Unverified** - candidate for traces; confirm |
| Prometheus | Not checked | **Unverified** - confirm before adopting |
| RabbitMQ | Server MPL-2.0 (client libraries Apache-2.0/MPL-2.0 dual) | Allowed (MPL-2.0 unmodified) - confirm on adoption |
| Keycloak | Not found in search | **Unverified** - confirm before adopting |
| PostgreSQL, pgvector, CloudNativePG | PostgreSQL licence (PostgreSQL); pgvector uses the PostgreSQL licence; CloudNativePG Apache-2.0 - **not confirmed in this pass** | **Unverified** - confirm on adoption |

## 5. Direct dependencies in use

| Package | Ecosystem | Version | Licence | Status | Source |
|---------|-----------|---------|---------|--------|--------|
{chr(10).join(tbl)}

Transitive dependencies (about 30 Python and 550 npm packages) are covered by the automated scans; see section 2 for licences outside the allow-list. Full listings: `cd backend && uv run pip-licenses` and `cd frontend && npx license-checker-rseidelsohn --summary`.

## 6. Fonts, icons, images and content

| Item | Licence | Status |
|------|---------|--------|
| Geist / Geist Mono (via `next/font/google`) | SIL OFL 1.1 | Allowed (OFL fonts); build downloads the font from Google Fonts - move to self-hosted files if the build must work offline |
| Next.js/Vercel template logos and sample content | - | Removed from the scaffold (provenance, LIC-6) |
| `favicon.ico` from create-next-app | Template asset | **To replace** with an original icon (T-009) |

## 7. Attribution (NOTICE)

To be generated from the scans before any distribution (LIC-7). Data licences with attribution requirements (CC-BY) must be listed here.
'''
open('LICENCES.md','w').write(t)

cat > .github/workflows/ci.yml <<'EOF'
# CI for AUCoFF v1: build, test, scan. There is NO deployment job (constitution ENV-4: v1 is local-only).
name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: backend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      - run: uv run ruff check .
      - run: uv run ruff format --check .
      - run: uv run mypy
      - run: uv run pytest -q
      - name: OpenAPI drift check (APIR-2)
        run: uv run python -m scripts.export_openapi --check
      - name: OpenAPI lint with Spectral (APIR-1)
        run: npx --yes @stoplight/spectral-cli@6 lint openapi.yaml --ruleset .spectral.yaml --fail-severity=warn
      - name: Python licence gate (LIC-5)
        run: uv run python -m scripts.check_licences

  frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run format:check
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run build
      - name: npm licence gate (LIC-5)
        run: npm run licences
      - name: Production dependency audit
        run: npm run audit:prod

  helm:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
      - run: helm lint deploy/helm/aucoff -f deploy/helm/aucoff/values-local.yaml

  secrets:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Gitleaks (CLI, not the licensed action)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          VERSION=8.30.1
          curl -sSfL "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${VERSION}/gitleaks_${VERSION}_linux_x64.tar.gz" | tar -xz gitleaks
          ./gitleaks detect --source . --redact --no-banner
EOF

# AUCoFF frontend

Next.js (App Router, TypeScript strict) application. See [`specs/frontend-spec.md`](../specs/frontend-spec.md) and [`specs/design.md`](../specs/design.md).

```
npm install        # install (uses the in-repo sharp stub, see ../LICENCES.md)
npm run dev        # http://localhost:3000
npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run format:check
npm run licences   # licence gate (LIC-1, LIC-2, LIC-5)
```

Image optimisation is disabled on purpose: Next.js's optional `sharp` pulls LGPL libvips, which the constitution disallows (LIC-2).

import re
for f,v in {'specs/backend-spec.md':'0.5.1','specs/infrastructure-spec.md':'0.5.1','specs/design.md':'0.5.1','specs/spec.md':'0.6.1','specs/tasks.md':'0.6.0'}.items():
    t=open(f).read(); t=re.sub(r'\| Version \| [\d.]+ \|',f'| Version | {v} |',t,1); open(f,'w').write(t)
import glob,os
txt={f:open(f).read() for f in glob.glob('specs/*.md')}
allt='\n'.join(txt.values()); bad=False
for p in ['US','FR','NFR','API','T','ADR','PER','AG','M','R']:
    d=set()
    for x in txt.values(): d|=set(re.findall(r'^\|\s*('+p+r'-\d+)\s*\|',x,re.M))
    if set(re.findall(r'\b('+p+r'-\d+)\b',allt))-d: print('undefined',p); bad=True
for f in txt:
    for l in re.findall(r'\]\(([a-z\-]+\.md)\)',txt[f]):
        if not os.path.exists('specs/'+l): print('broken',f,l); bad=True
print('spec consistency','FAILED' if bad else 'OK')

`make check` passes locally. I haven't run the CI workflow on GitHub, so it is untested there. Two things it needs from you are in the first list below.

**What now exists**
- **Repo conventions (T-003):**
  - The root `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` (project rules for AI agents).
  - `CODEOWNERS` and a PR template, plus `.editorconfig`.
  - A `Makefile` with `doctor`, `setup`, `check`, `cluster-up` and `cluster-down`.
- **Backend (T-101, T-108):**
  - A FastAPI app with layered packages and `/health/live` and `/health/ready`.
  - `backend/openapi.yaml`, generated and committed, with a drift check. The Spectral linter shows no warnings.
  - A Python licence gate and 7 tests that pass, plus ruff and mypy.
- **Frontend (T-301):**
  - A Next.js skeleton with strict TypeScript and Tailwind.
  - Vitest, Prettier, ESLint and an npm licence gate.
  - The production build works.
  - I removed the template's Vercel logos.
- **Deploy:** a kind cluster config and a Helm chart skeleton with a restricted pod security context, ingress and default-deny network policies. `helm lint` passes.
- **CI:** one workflow for backend, frontend, Helm and secret scanning, with no deploy job. It installs the gitleaks command line directly because the packaged gitleaks action needs a licence for organisations.

**Verified from web search (secondary sources, confirm on adoption)**
- `pgvector` 0.8.6 supports PostgreSQL 18.
- CloudNativePG loads `pgvector` as an image-volume extension, which needs PostgreSQL 18, Kubernetes 1.35 or later, and containerd 2.1 or later.
- These tools are AGPL, GPL, LGPL or restricted, so they are not approved:
  - MinIO is AGPL-3.0, and its community repository was archived in April 2026.
  - Grafana, Loki and Tempo have been AGPLv3 since 2021.
  - Steampipe is AGPL-3.0, and ScoutSuite is GPL-2.0.
  - The Semgrep and Opengrep engines are LGPL-2.1, and the Semgrep rules licence is restrictive.
  - Current Redis is RSALv2, SSPLv1 or AGPLv3.
- Apache-2.0 candidates, per the same search: Prowler, Trivy, Checkov, kube-bench, SeaweedFS, Perses and VictoriaLogs.
- The first-pass register is in `LICENCES.md`. I did not confirm kubescape, Jaeger, Prometheus, Keycloak or the PostgreSQL stack, and they are marked unverified.

**Problems I found and fixed**
- Next.js's optional `sharp` pulls LGPL libvips, which our rules disallow. I replaced it with a stub and turned off image optimisation. The npm scan shows no LGPL package left.
- A peer-dependency conflict and a missing native binding broke Vitest. A clean reinstall fixed both.

**Needs you**
1. **Install on your laptop:** run `brew install kind`, then `colima start` (the Docker daemon is stopped). I did not install anything. `make cluster-up` needs both.
2. **GitHub:** enable branch protection and review the CI workflow once it first runs.
3. **Licence decisions in `LICENCES.md`.**
   - The scan found several permissive-style licences that aren't on your allow-list. CI passes them with a notice for now:
     - PSF-2.0, which Python's `typing_extensions` needs.
     - MIT-0, BlueOak-1.0.0, 0BSD and CC0.
     - CC-BY data licences, which need attribution.
   - Please approve or reject each.
4. **Project licence:** the repository's own `LICENSE` is AGPL-3.0. Confirm that's what you intend for AUCoFF.
5. **T-001 and T-006:** your sign-off on the constitution and spec, and the v1 unified control set.

**Still open:** the npm audit reports 5 high-severity issues in dev tooling (`eslint-config-next`). Production dependencies show 0. The kind node image tag is not pinned until `kind` is installed. Dockerfiles, the Keycloak login, the database, RabbitMQ and the first scanner are not started.

I'm in plan mode, so the next session is yours to start. The natural next step is to build the backend and frontend images, bring up the cluster, then add PostgreSQL, the migrations and row-level security.

## Owner decisions (this round)
- Theme: light default + dark mode, clean enterprise; professional with a Gen-Z feel.
- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.
- Layout: left collapsible sidebar + top bar (tenant switcher, global search, notifications, user) + content area with breadcrumbs, page header/actions, right detail drawer.
- Density/responsive: comfortable default with compact table toggle; desktop-first, tablet OK, mobile for dashboard and approvals (read/decide).
- Dashboard priority: metrics and quantified data first. Landing shows: overall compliance posture score + per-framework coverage %; open findings by severity + aging; pending approvals + agent activity; jurisdiction heatmap + upcoming audits.
- Metrics/charts: control coverage % and pass/partial/fail distribution; time to audit readiness and remediation cycle time; agent quality (citation correctness, confidence, review override rate); LLM cost/tokens vs budget, scan duration, evidence freshness; control severity (critical/high/medium/low) current counts compared with the last 2 scans.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### agent.md structure (v0.2.0)

2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.
3. Orchestration (LangGraph graphs per workflow: assessment, mapping, questionnaire, regulatory change, report, copilot); state schema; interrupts; checkpointing; retries; budgets.
4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).
8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.
11. Evaluation: golden datasets per agent, metrics (accuracy, citation correctness >= target, hallucination rate, override rate, answer reuse accuracy, redaction recall), thresholds (proposal), CI regression gate, human feedback loop, red-team/prompt-injection suite.
12. Audit logging and traceability: run records, steps, redacted inputs, model/prompt versions, tokens/cost, approvals (maps to agent_runs/agent_steps/approvals).
13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.

- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).
- database-spec.md: new `assessment_snapshots`, `severity_counts`/`metric_points` (tenant_id, metric_id, assessment_id, scope_id, framework_id, value, captured_at), monthly partitions, retention row (>= 13 months, tenant-configurable up, never below 12), RLS, backup coverage; ensure results of deleted evidence keep metadata so history stays comparable.
- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

- Palette (from owner): deep blue, blue, teal, red, yellow, green, amber, gray. Brand primary = deep blue; teal secondary/accent; status semantics: Pass green, Partial amber, Fail red, Unknown grey, N/A slate; yellow for warnings/highlights; always icon + text (never colour alone).
- Style traits: rounded corners 8-12px, soft shadows, generous whitespace; subtle gradients/glass only on hero KPI cards; micro-interactions and friendly empty-state illustrations (respect reduced-motion); bold typography with large KPI numerals.

### Owner decisions for agent.md
- Roster: the 9 services from spec.md 5.6 PLUS `reviewer-agent` (independent verifier of citations/conclusions before human review), `regulatory-change-agent`, `copilot-agent` (user Q&A with citations), and `questionnaire-agent` (due-diligence).
- Scanners: deterministic policy-as-code checks first (produce facts); LLM interprets, maps, explains, handles documents.
- Models: tiered - strong model for assessment/mapping/questionnaire answers/review; small model for extraction/classification/routing; provider-agnostic, Claude default; model IDs in config.
- Knowledge/RAG: shared framework texts + unified controls (read-only, licensing caveat); tenant documents (policies, SOPs, audit reports); collected evidence summaries + prior assessment results (history); remediation playbooks/best-practice library; the tenant's already-answered due-diligence questionnaires (answer library). Tenant embeddings strictly isolated (DB-6).
- Questionnaire agent: accepts uploaded Excel/Word/PDF, standard templates (SIG, CAIQ, HECVAT, VSA), and link/portal questionnaires (drafts answers for manual entry; no auto-submit); answer-library reuse first with freshness checks; grounds answers in real environment: prefer fresh scan evidence, trigger read-only re-scan when stale, cite evidence IDs + timestamps; every answer gets confidence + sources; human approval per answer or batch; export only approved answers; sensitive details (resource IDs, IPs, account numbers, internal hostnames) redacted by default with reviewer override; every export audit-logged; tenant-configurable "shareable detail level".
- Regulatory change agent: monitors allow-listed official sources, proposes catalogue/mapping diffs for human approval; never auto-changes the catalogue.

### Additional numeric decisions (owner, initial/tunable)
- Eval CI gates: citation correctness >= 98%; hallucination rate <= 1%; control-result agreement with reviewers >= 90%; redaction recall >= 99%.
- Budgets: USD 25 per assessment run, USD 10 per questionnaire, tenant monthly cap configurable; alert at 80%, hard stop at 100% (state `budget_exceeded`).
- Approvals expire after 7 days (then item returns to queue and notifies; never auto-approved).
- Retrieval: provider-agnostic embedding interface; hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) with reranking; embedding model/dimension decided at build.

### agent.md structure (v0.2.0)
1. Overview, principles (link constitution AI-1..AI-15), deterministic-first rule.
2. Agent roster table (AG-1..AG-13): purpose, trigger, inputs, outputs, tools, model tier, autonomy level, approval gate, queue name, spec/FR refs.

4. Model strategy: tiers, routing rules, fallbacks, temperature/params, structured output, caching, cost budgets per run/tenant, provider interface.
5. Tools registry: tool name, read/write, side effects, permissions, approval, rate limits (cloud/k8s/repo/saas read-only tools; evidence store; vector search (tenant-filtered); ticketing create (approval); notifications; document parsers).
6. Knowledge and memory: sources, chunking, embedding model/dimension (TODO), refresh, citation format, answer library lifecycle (approved, stale, retired), tenant isolation, history (12-month snapshots) as retrieval source.
7. Prompts: repo layout, versioning, templating, change control, prompt-injection-safe structure (evidence as data).
8. Guardrails: input validation, injection defence, output schemas (Pydantic), citation validator (reject uncited claims), PII/secret redaction before LLM, disallowed actions, refusal/uncertainty behaviour, rate and budget limits.
9. Human-in-the-loop matrix: action -> trigger -> approver role -> timeout/default (finalise control result, accept risk, approve mapping, publish report, export questionnaire answers, catalogue change, ticket creation).
10. Questionnaire workflow (detailed): ingest -> parse/normalise questions -> classify/map to unified controls -> retrieve answer library + evidence -> freshness check/re-scan -> draft answer + confidence + citations -> reviewer agent check -> human approval -> redaction -> export (Excel/Word/PDF) -> save to answer library; Mermaid sequence; data model hints (questionnaires, questions, answers, answer_library) for database-spec.
11. Evaluation: golden datasets per agent, metrics (accuracy, citation correctness >= target, hallucination rate, override rate, answer reuse accuracy, redaction recall), thresholds (proposal), CI regression gate, human feedback loop, red-team/prompt-injection suite.
12. Audit logging and traceability: run records, steps, redacted inputs, model/prompt versions, tokens/cost, approvals (maps to agent_runs/agent_steps/approvals).
13. Failure handling and degradation (provider outage, scan failure -> unknown, budget exceeded, kill switch), cost controls.
14. Security/threat table for agents (prompt injection, data exfiltration via questionnaires, cross-tenant leakage, over-privileged tools).
15. Open questions.

## Historical data requirement (added by owner)
- Retain and expose 1 year (12 months, rolling) of historical scan/assessment results so any scan can be compared with previous scans, not only the last 2.
- Design: immutable per-assessment snapshots (control results, severity counts, coverage, scores) kept for >= 13 months (1 month buffer) regardless of live-data retention; rollup tables/materialised views for daily/weekly/monthly trends; partitioning by month; exempt from agent_steps' shorter retention.
- UI: time-range selector (last 2 scans, 30/90 days, 12 months, custom), trend lines and delta arrows, side-by-side scan comparison view (any two scans: new, resolved, regressed, unchanged controls/findings), per-control history timeline, framework/jurisdiction history.
- API: `/metrics/{id}?from=&to=&granularity=`, `/assessments/compare?base=&target=`, `/control-results/{id}/history`; cursor-paginated; export of history (CSV/JSON).
- database-spec.md: new `assessment_snapshots`, `severity_counts`/`metric_points` (tenant_id, metric_id, assessment_id, scope_id, framework_id, value, captured_at), monthly partitions, retention row (>= 13 months, tenant-configurable up, never below 12), RLS, backup coverage; ensure results of deleted evidence keep metadata so history stays comparable.
- spec.md: new FR (history/compare) and NFR (12-month history retention); metrics catalogue entries gain a "history window" column; constitution: add DB rule for snapshot immutability/retention.

I relicensed AUCoFF from AGPL-3.0 to the MIT License and pushed it as `6555b98`. I'm back in plan mode. The rebase had nothing to do.

**Why MIT rather than Apache-2.0:** MIT has the fewest obligations. A user only has to keep the copyright and permission notice. Apache-2.0 adds a patent grant, but also notice and change-statement duties. You asked for whichever is more permissive, so I chose MIT. If you want Apache-2.0 for its patent protection, say so and I'll switch.

**What changed**
- **`LICENSE`:** the full MIT text, "Copyright (c) 2026 Praveen Darshanam".
- **Package metadata:** `license = "MIT"` in `backend/pyproject.toml` and `"license": "MIT"` in `frontend/package.json`.
- **`README.md` and `LICENCES.md`:** the project-licence section now states MIT, and the earlier "confirm AGPL" question is resolved.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** it tells AI agents to keep the licence files in sync.
- **`specs/constitution.md` (v0.10.0):** new rule LIC-9 says AUCoFF is MIT-licensed. The root `LICENSE` and the package metadata must agree, changing the licence needs an owner decision recorded here and in `LICENCES.md`, and contributions are accepted only under the same licence.
- **`specs/spec.md` (v0.7.0):** new NFR-16 for the project licence.
- **`specs/tasks.md`:** version bumped.

The local checks pass: backend tests, the Python and npm licence gates, and the spec ID and link consistency check.

- **Past versions:** versions of the code that anyone already obtained under AGPL-3.0 stay available to them under that licence. Relicensing only applies to what you distribute from now on.
- **Copyright holder:** I put your name as the holder because you're the sole author. If anyone else has contributed, or you work under an employer who owns your work, check that you're able to relicense it.
